ethan hunt and his im team are tasked with recovering both parts of a key which may be able to control a sentient and now rogue ai, known as 'the entity', which can infiltrate all systems including weapons systems and could potentially take over the world. whilst countries are interested in getting control of the entity for their own ends, hunt is determined to destroy it.

whilst, with the exception of mi 2, i have always enjoyed these films, i found this one a bit hard to take. it's not that it isn't exciting, with the usual death defying action / stunt scenes and indeed the 163 minute running time mostly shot by, it's just that whilst ai is a reasonable target in this day and age, so much of it was a stretch on the imagination - basically i found a lot of it a bit silly. in particular, discussions about the end of the world drag on a bit and a very long and rather boring section at a big party held by vanessa kirby, which suggested the entity was watching them all like some sort of ethereal spirit gone bad was just too much. rebecca ferguson is wasted, simon pegg seems more wired than usual and esai morales is unconvincing as a 60 year old tough guy who seems to be able to beat everyone up. cruise is fine and hayley atwell is the best thing in this and overall there is a lot of fun to be had here leading up to a spectacular and exciting climax. i do look forward to part 2, but the ideas here are a mission to far for me - rogue nation and fallout were much better films.

an artificial intelligence program has just destroyed a russian submarine, making the program the most sought after item for governments...and criminals. ethan hunt and his team are called in to secure the program for the us government but their adversaries appear to always be one step ahead of them.

another action-packed instalment in the mission impossible series. by now you know what to expect: ridiculously scary stunts, often involving heights, and a heap of tension. plot tends to take a back-seat, being more the vehicle to get you to the action scenes, and here it is even more so. the plot is complex to the point of incomprehensibility at times, which is essentially a smokescreen for the fact that the plot isn't very plausible.

the action scenes deliver to expectations though. some absolute heart-stopping scenes.

compared to its immediate predecessor, this one's disappointing. the two movies differ most noticeably in terms of narrative propulsion and emotional resonance.

6 (fallout) constitutes perhaps the most efficient and effective string of action scenes to make it to theatres in the last decade. its first half hour contains enough plot for a feature film in and of itself. the scene with debruuk, for instance, where they fake a hospital room, leaves out an action sequence where benji crashes into debruuk with his car. characters describe the action in dialogue instead, which is smart. the sequence itself is unneeded: we get all the intrigue, all the cool mask reveals, all the halo jumps, and all the bathroom fight scenes we need--all before the first half hour is up.

in dead reckoning, they film the unnecessary scene. it takes place in the desert, and it takes place early. it bloats the runtime. it serves as a red-herring- type manipulation which undercuts the film's emotional payoff (see below). it makes the next scene's reveal that much less intriguing. and so, altogether, it makes 7's set up that much less effective. (no small problem also that the film uses a sandstorm as a set-piece for the second time in the series, which feels too close to recycling for me).

6, like 7, has a series of pursuers: the widow's baddies, the fbi, and even the imf. but where baldwin gets lots of time to play spy, and where cavill gets to reload his biceps, and where kirby at least gets to smile and act intriguingly coy, in dead reckoning the pursuers are all treated with the complexity of angela bassett's character, erica sloane. there are *so many of them* in 7 that the action scenes sometimes have to stop to count the pursuers, presumably so the audience remembers them all. but they're not characters in and of themselves; they have no time to be.

lastly, on the cluttered storyline front, there's the problem of inter-cutting. in fallout, only one big action set-piece (the helicopter chase) is inter-cut with the search for the nukes. we see the halo jump and the bathroom fight from start to finish. we stay with the action. we're in the tension. these early, brutally efficient scenes make room later for a more hectic, inter-cut, and messy climax, wherein the plot, whose threads have all been delineated by separate and effective emotional stakes, resolves. dead reckoning doesn't provide this.

there is **so much happening** that 7 sometimes feels like it undercuts its own tension in service of keeping all its threads in the air. the motorcycle jump occurs in the middle of some thread-untangling, after which the film cuts away: hunt, jumps, he's in the air, he pulls his chute, and then we're somewhere else. the stunt has no time (literally here) to land: it looks great but feels hollow.

to be fair, the movie does create some real tension, which is more than i can say for indiana jones. but it's been done better in previous installments.

the second major difference between 6 and 7 is emotional resonance. not sure if you agree, but--and major spoiler here--i very much disliked the handling of ilsa's death. it's one thing to feel bad after a franchise character dies, but this isn't what the film evokes. ilsa's not in the movie enough--the emotional stakes haven't been developed enough--for her death to have any resonance. there's some sad music, a mournful hunt at sunset for a second. that's it.

the unnecessary desert scene i mention above is a major one for ilsa. we're led to believe she's dead, but then she's not dead, but then she *actually* dies later. why the fake death for a cheap manipulation? she and hunt smooch at the end of 6 (a full-on, lovey-dovey smooch), only for her to be completely abandoned in 7. they could have used ilsa for much, much more tension-building than they did. she's cast aside, forgotten about.

and while hayley atwell is terrific as grace, i couldn't help but feel--as ilsa dies so inconsequentially and as grace lives so giddily and with so much still to explore--that the movie is about how hunt gets tired of an old fling and decides to find a new one.

maybe this is too mean-spirited a description. but the handling of ilsa's death really had me feeling less than completely willing to invest myself in grace's plight. yes, you're brilliant, quirky, competent, strong. yes, i want you to succeed. but there's that other woman--the one who came before you?--who just got left in the ditch. it feels like bad storytelling: not a comment on sacrifice or redemption or friendship, but rather an exercise in substituting the old for the new.

there's a poorly constructed rationale for this substitution--that ilsa dies so grace can live--but there's no *motivation* for it. it's contrived.

which makes the movie itself feel kind of old or empty--like a dvd's plastic wrapping crumpled on a couch. less art, more commodity. less gritty action and more gritty grind culture. whereas in 7, the hollowness ever so slightly starts to creep in, 6 never feels anything less than immersive.

how can this version of another mi movie get scores above 6/10 is proof of bot reviews i believe this is a bear shell of old glory the main thing that left me simmering on after sitting trough 3hour of this is; awkwardness -the deadpan closeups of faces and head nods -the "i'm getting to old for this" "run tom run scenes -the omg what a strange characters -the forces emotional scenes -the villain is laughable and borderline scientology propaganda -the pace of this 1 hour too long borefest and most disappointing of all is the lack of conclusive action scenes. they are just boring and time consuming one of the worst tom cruise and production team eggs in a long time advice : watch any other mi, they're just better.

love tom and love the mi series but this is a big step backwards from fallout etc.

they throw themselves into the action but it would have been nice if they'd put more thought into everything else. and the action is essentially a long version of the trailer - there's no reveal along the way.

there are amusing moments but the narrative path and dialogue is recycled - ethan's drivers, the calculating omnipotence of the adversary (solomon lane mark 2). i hope the stunt team were better rewarded than the writers.

and the opportunities to care for the characters are almost non-existent, with a particular lack of empathy and emotion at a critical moment standing out in its callous pacing.

team, your mission, should you chose to accept it, is to tell a human story. otherwise we can get chatgpt to write it. erie.

i really wanted to enjoy this movie more especially since i'm a long time mi franchise fan.

it gets high marks for the locations, stunts, overall acting, but that's pretty much it. even lorne balfe's score (except for the main title) just didn't do anything for me this time around. in fact, i hardly noticed it & didn't even feel it added anything to the film. take for example the music when ethan did the halo jump in "fallout" or was speeding through paris. that's a score! it added to what we were seeing on the screen.

here, the music felt rushed, snipped, and frankly, when i heard different orchestras were used from different locations, that's when i felt the "fallout" success went to everyone's heads. more fluff, no real substance.

i get it. this was a tough film to make. multiple production delays, a pandemic, stress & pressures to get the movie done. so many interruptions. it's an impossible mission that this movie made it to the theaters at all. however, the whole concept of "writing the movie as you go" didn't quite work this time, fellas. "fallout" was your one-trick-pony. as for mcquarrie's, & erik jendresen's script, i know i've seen better from at least mcq.

it's clear tom cruise gave it his all in this film, like he always does. he needn't worry that the audience is not in tune to his efforts in delivering entertainment. the actors as a whole, did their best, but this was basically a disjointed creation and i would squarely place blame on the script as the foundation.

the film felt rushed, haphazardly pieced together & more of a "what can we do to top 'fallout' and the other films," versus concentrating on making a film the mi franchise is known for. to me, the scene that came closest to that was benji at the airport attempting to disarm the bomb. that scene more than anything else (car chase, bike jump, fights, et al) really had me interested, focused & satisfied the mi thirst i was seeking from mi7.

the newcomer characters & actors did a fine job. however, if there was anyone from the "old gang" that really had nothing to do this time was luther (ving rhames).

in the end, hopefully this movie is similar to other sequel-based entries where the feeling of disappointment is due to only watching "part of the story" and the next installment makes up for it.

not counting the current strike, hopefully no additional pandemics and delays will stand in the way this time so that we can perhaps once again return to a franchise we all know & enjoy.

i feel there needs to be a counter balance to all the over the top hyperbole about this movie - while it stands out from current action movies, that's more about the poor quality of the others more than anything.

the plot is super generic, the villains cartoonish and the stakes seem lower than they should be.

the action, while shot practically, doesn't look all that realistic - it almost like there's a gloss placed over the final result to make it look less real somehow! the big action set piece involving the motorbike jumping off the mountain looks less real than similar stunts from movies from 40 years ago, and you wouldn't know cruise performed the stunt if it wasn't hyped to the nth degree. the fight scenes look bland compared to the likes of the john wick movies as well.

is it a bad movie? not at all, but far from being the greatest action movie the reviews here suggest. top gun maverick is far more worthy of that title.

obviously this is a long running and much loved series and any new instalment now is going to be big budget and a cinema blockbuster. some of the stunts for this one were much publicised before release, and rightly so, some of the stunt shots are really breathtaking.

for me the series is becoming to formulaic and the same cast are looking tired and doing the same thing again and again in each movie. i really hope for some kind of refresh of cast and script for future mi films as i think that time has now come.

as others have said, it is verging on f&f style absurdity and bad dialogue. my main issues are two fold. firstly, a near 3hr film that doesn't have a proper conclusion is a big ask (i actually watched it in three sittings), and finished feeling unsatisfied. secondly (and a huge one in my opinion), is how to make ai appear scary and threatening.

mi is not the first movie to face this problem, and ai may indeed be a real hot topic in the current day and age, but a computer monitor with some pulsing lights and making a computerised purr sound does not work effectively.

on the positive side we get some amazing stunts as mentioned, car chases in beautiful cities, lots of 'cruise run' and an all star cast (you could say too many making it convoluted). but it is fun, you just need to switch of and focus on the visuals more than anything else.

6/10.

i cant believe they killed ilsa and replace it with grace (hailey atwell). she's too bubly and comical, and they somehow made ilsa a bubbling sidekick with no nouse of an mi6 top agent. ethan was lamer this time as if he got caught in a limelight.

they cant seem to decide whether to go with super high tech mi movies or going back to old sleight of hand trick which is very unbelievable. even the best of thieves can't pick pocket the professionals not once but like several times in a minute. come on guys... they're supposed to be a pro and somehow they got pickpocketed by the oldest trick in the world.

and hailey again oh my she's trying to be the star of the show and somehow made it to become an imf member because she can... eer... pickpocket well? at least benji and luther was top hacker and ethan is a superman. the girl can't act. sure he's eye candy and aluring but this is imf universe, not some merry go lucky happy bunch. the stakes are high but the way uncle sam is treating the whole thing looks amateurish.

shea wigum from boardwalk empire just ruins the whole movie. as if they decide a group of fools can somehow jump into the action without any sort of coordination. what's more important, the key or catching ethan? with everything at stake you'd think they'll either help ethan or throw everything to at least get along with the program.

the fight scene are laughable considering where we are technology wise. the super cool french chick who was supposed to be the ace henchman got blindsided too easy. in a world where they have all the gadget in the world they resort to knifes? and steel pipes? and ethan who has no problem shooting bad guys all over the world from berlin to abu dhabi somehow refuse to kill the main evil bar guys.

and gabriel? a laughable antagonist who's only good at knife, i mean come on... at least the previous bad guys are rich and have henchman to do their job.

and dont get me started on a covert russian submarine with a crew who spoke perfect english..

what a waste. you enter the theatre already elated even before the movie has started! wow! i'm gonna watch mission impossible! is going to be ethan hunt against the covid virus? or is going to be.......... no! (a. i.) causing wars , disbalance, chaos etc. how old is this story line? right from the 1960's (2001 space odyssey), 80's (terminator series ) , irobot, eagle eye , ultron etc. we have been bombarded by (a. i. ) as a villain soooo many times and, human hero the saviour. enough is enough! couldn't tom cruise find a better lesser worn out theme to invest his hard work in? 6 stars for the action stunts. zero for the villains and story.

even for this one, quite long movie the thin storyline is not sufficient. however, streching it into two clearly sucks and can only be explained by pure economical logic.

apart from that the flick is solid - not more, not less. tom is good but somehow i find his age shows slowly. especially the fights are coreographed and directed like 20 years ago, not at all comparable with the level of creativity and intensity we know from john wick or even daniel craig's bond movies.

and even the action sequences are only ok but far from being on the edge or innovative.

the usual tc-hype captured us and made me buy ticket for me and my kids. but in the end, we left the cinema a bit disappointed. probably we will watch part 2 next year at home on the small screen.

will start off by saying this movie is still worth seeing in theaters. the action scenes are pretty awesome, as they always are in this series. it's worth seeing on the big screen.

however, dead reckoning pt 1 does not live up to the hype of the two previous installments. there was a lot of forced humor, too many new characters added that convolutes the story big time.

it's hard to create a cohesive story when you are adding in a handful of new antagonists and a new main character/love interest while also giving the core characters enough screen time and development. the previous movies handled that a lot smoother.

they replaced rebecca ferguson (ilsa) with newcomer hayley atwell (grace). the problem with that, was there was not nearly as much emotional connection to grace as there was with ilsa. i found myself wishing that it was ilsa and ethan in the scenes and not grace and ethan. perhaps they are setting up future films for ethan to be more of a mentor/teacher to grace?

for me, the chemistry they built up over the past few movies with ilsa and ethan was wasted for the less convincing grace.

another issue is the main antagonist of the movie. it became a bit convoluted when we are dealing with a fake ai/being that is leading the charge, yet we're seeing esai morales (gabriel) all throughout the film.

i understand that they are trying to have a real world type villain and raise the stakes, but it felt less powerful that the big bad guy was a computer that does not speak. felt like it would have been more effective if it was just gabriel. would have had a lot more time to develop his character and the backstory between him and ethan.

overall, it's not a bad movie by any means, but falls short of the expectations the previous two installments had built up. too convoluted with a bunch of moving parts and characters that don't jell particularly well.

overall: 6.4 / 10.

good news: thankfully tom has a few more years to reach harrison status; also, it was nice to see the filmed introduction of cruise & mcquarrie welcoming their audience as perfect hosts do to their joint project of film wizardry, stunts & non-stop action in a big screen theater. for this, theatre owners & operators should be forever grateful! mi:dead reckoning, part 1 seems to be a throwback to the '50s lone ranger & flash gordon-type, 15min serials that always kept their audiences coming back for more after improbable 'cliffhangers.'

now this segues into the bad news: part 1 is, ahem, a little longer than 15mins...like almost 3hrs! it's length gives the impression of spliced together film snippets of fast-paced, death-defying stunts, former franchise previews & trailers with script dialogue seemingly, pun intended, a. i. generated. one needs to be infected with a virus from the entity to understand the plot which is wending its way through the brain of villain, es(ai) morales. in fact, most of the plot seems to be still in the entity's black hole (eerily similar to nolan's interstellar) which, hopefully, will be retrieved in time for part 2! my rating of 6 reflects the incompleteness of a total movie (i need 1&2) and the fact that top gun:maverick was so much better, as tom cruise movies go!

personally out of all the mi movies i would rank this towards the bottom. like maybe the 3rd from the bottom.

what did work for me? i loved the addition of hayley atwell in the film. she's badass yet also feels like she represents the "every woman". i feel like i could relate to her if i were thrown into a spy mission and being completely out of my element. and she's charismatic and funny too. there are great action set pieces too. the train derailment is instantly an iconic moment from the franchise.

what didn't work? mainly for me, the villain. he's touted as being this important figure from ethan's past. the man who essentially made ethan who he is. but it's a completely new character to us. so the tension was just never there for me. it felt unearned. and as much as i liked hayley atwell, i didn't love it at the expense of ilsa. plus, i feel like the plot is a little convoluted.

it wasn't a bad film per se. it's not like i wouldn't recommend it. just a tad disappointing.

i love ethan hunt so although a good movie, it still left me hanging. its a good movie for action and fightinh scenes. there are great views from multiple angles. the movement is fast and intense, with several plot twists, stunts are performed well, and the sound and picture quality is great. however, it delivers an impossible question still understand: purpose for this movie? watch it and you will still be left hanging. the new technology that is made by a villainous group is very difficult to comprehend, because the plotline is too fast. even the characters themselves havent the faintest clue, and not even the object that they are deemed to find can fix this either. it leaves the viewer confused throughout. there is also a new character but they dont add any value to the plot, because without them hunt still can do his mission. overall, good to see for an action packed thriller, however it leaves confusion throughout and is missing purpose for the franchise series.

i still end up comparing these all to the bourne series and now most recently craigs bond series. mi just always falls far short for me and despite my very high hopes this last one does as well...

it's very big on eye candy (stunts, cinematography, gadgets) but its always light on story/arch and meaningful character development outside of ethan.

the complimentary side kicks in mi always remain just that and nothing more. the roles/scope they are limited to don't allow them to develop any sense of depth or meaning even though they've been in all 7 of these now.

i hate to say it but i truly believe cruise monopolizes too much of the show, and this sabotages any other character development.

i'll be honest i forgot i watched it 10 minutes after i left the theater, unlike no time to die... i couldn't wait to see it again in imax and then couldn't wait to own the blueray.

i'm a big cruise fan but i can but this is just eye candy without substance and i just never got into it even though i really tried.

first things first: this is a competently made, well-filmed, well-paced, and nice looking and sounding movie. seeing it on the biggest screen near you is certainly worth it one time.

that said - overall, it's a pretty standard action movie, and most of the plot "twists" and beats were quite predictable. the whole "entity" malarkey is the mcguffin the entire movie rests upon, and it's not explained in any reasonable or sensible fashion. it just makes vaguely threatening digital noises... and the film's other villain is a james bond-esque escalation/callback which made me roll my eyes. tom cruise is good, as usual, but the rest of the cast isn't given too much to do - except for atwell, who does fine until the end, when the climax on the train really pulls the rug out from her characterization.

i wish it was better. but, worth it to see it one time in plf. otherwise, i don't care too much about part 2 anymore.

putting aside how viscerally unlikeable atwell's character is, mission impossible: dead reckoning part 1 is disappointingly lacking in the blood-pumping action and quick wit the franchise is known for. this fetch-quest of a first instalment leaves much to be desired of part 2. audiences will have to wait for next year when the conclusion of this grey-nomad-gone-rogue two-parter reveals the fate of one of the world's most beloved spies and his dwindling crew.

whilst cruise's efforts to rebuild the blockbuster error of cinema are noble, it seems this isn't the film to do the job. dead reckoning (pt 1) comes in as a series low. what crazy stunts will tom cruise pull next? unfortunately, it doesn't seem to matter as the weakness in this film is not in the action (or action star), but in the subpar writing.

this felt like a a recycled old hits album - familiarly satisfying without piquing new interest. car chases, hand to hand combats, fighting on trains, motorcycle stunts - old-fashioned movie making for modern times! tom cruise is on a legacy run, like harrison ford. this one is not as good as top gun maverick, but still worth a theater watch for the spectacle.

that said, it is best to leave most of your brains at home. sadly, i tried to suss out the plot and ended up with a long list of confusing plot points below.

spoiler alert!

why is the entity's source code hidden on a soviet submarine, when it was developed by us intelligence?

how did the master key go from the dead soviet officers in the ocean to alana getting one half and ilsa the other half?

who was the buyer in abu dhabi? how and why did he have a (fake) key? why was he killed by paris?

did alana hire grace to steal the key from this buyer or from ethan? since the buyer's key was fake, it was a miracle that grace stole the authentic key from ethan - a real mcguffin!!

why was gabriel even at abu dhabi airport? why did he place the fake bomb in baggage? what was the point of benji bomb defusing sequence? how did gabriel disappear from ethan's sight (since ai can only manipulate digital images, not real eyes!)?

if gabriel is working for the entity, who is all knowing and predicts the future, why didn't he know the buyer had a fake key and focus on ethan to get the real key? worse, he could've foreseen the two keys being in venice and later on the train, and avoid abu dhabi altogether!

why was paris trying to kill grace and ethan when they had the key and would've brought it to venice anyway?

why was gabriel at the venice party (especially when he later predicted the key would be on the train and he'd take it from there)? alana intended to get the matching key from grace and sell it to a bidder on the orient express, so why did she invite gabriel there?

why does (gabriel predict) one of grace and ilsa has to die? why does he try to get one key from grace when he intends to get both keys on the train the next day?

why does alana get on the train to meet the bidder when she doesn't have both keys and knows the deal won't be done?

why does grace not go through with the transaction with kitteridge so they could follow where it leads to? the money was part of the original deal and shouldn't have weighed on her conscience.

i could go on but you get the point. if you use your brain, you will end up with too many questions...

how can anyone rate this? do we judge it simply by the other mission: impossible movies? then it's bottom-of-the-barrel, in a close contest with m:i-2 for last place. do we judge it by the high-budget movies studios are typically releasing? then it's one of the best in years.

one of the problems the film has to deal with is that it's following three movies in the series that have absolutely crushed. the fourth, fifth, and sixth m:i movies are probably the best action films ever made (unless we're including more adventure-style films like indiana jones, though that line is finicky). how do you follow these and still reach greatness?

apparently, you don't. the action itself isn't nearly as good or interesting as the previous films; there's nothing even close to the burj khalifa set piece in #4 or the skydiving sequence in #6. the very last set piece got grating and annoying (something not even m:i-2 did) as the same action beats repeated over and over again. i barely remember any of the action, to be honest. there's a car chase that's fine, there's a fight in an alley, there's some stuff at the end... what else happened? it was forgettable to say the least.

the story itself is pretty dumb. only the first m:i had any real story or character depth to speak of, but this one really drives home the complete pointlessness of everything outside the action scenes. there are multiple "twists"/reveals that are extremely obvious a mile away and keep getting treated as if they're something major (think the henry cavill stuff from 6, but happening 4-5 times throughout the movie). the dialogue is terrible and pointless. characters have zero integrity or... well, character (ethan hunt tells a woman who has left him to die multiple times that he'd risk his life for her... what?). the ai story has been done before, been done better, and doesn't fit the world of the m:i movies. henry czerny and cary elwes are used in the most uncreative ways possible and have almost nothing to do. and don't get me started on how they did rebecca ferguson dirty.

and yet... it's still somewhat good. not great; a low point in the series; but good. certainly better than most superhero movies or maverick or avatar or pretty much anything getting a wide release recently. it's at least enjoyable, and until the very last action sequence, it never once felt like it dragged.

it's good; it's just also... disappointing.

the story seems to be copied from multiple hollywood and bollywood movies. it lacks coherence. some special effects are amazing while many like submarine scene is subpar. car chase is dejavu feeling being similar to many thousand movies. tom cruise is old and lost his shine. this mi could have been definitely better made. if you are tom cruise fan then you will be sad to see him old. there is too much monologue not helping the screen play. european alps and the bike scene is must watch. but that's it nothing unique. please don't have high expectations. previous mi movies were 100 times better.

just got back from seeing this film & to be honest i have mixed feelings about this one.

the film sees ethan hunt track down a deadly weapon that threatens humanity if in the wrong hands. with not knowing who to trust & the world at stake, ethan finds himself forced to consider that nothing can matter more than the mission, even the people he cares about.

i found the film to be not bad, but overly long & bloated. i mean, why films like this have to be so drawn out & long is beyond me. the story is good & the villain was interesting, but the dialogue scenes were way too overly long & drawn out, even the action scene by the 3rd act was taking the absolute biscuit. i mean it was good but like fallout, you'd just had enough at that point & wanted it to end.

the runtime is a whopping 2 hours & 36 minutes!!! way! too! long! whoever edited this film clearly needs to brush up on their editing skills & be more mindful of not torturing their audience!! sorry, not sorry, but it really annoys the sugar honey ice tea out of me when films like this have to follow this overly bloated runtime kak. whatever happened to consistency?

anyway, the films story was good as i said, but confusing when too many characters & sub plots began to overlap one another & muddy things more & of course everything was drawn out so you forgot certain characters plots because of how long & drawn out the time between seeing the characters was. it was part & parcel of the problem fcs.

however, there was some great eye candy with the white widow, vanessa kirby (hottie!!) & that other woman & hayley atwell! the action was good & humour wasn't too bad either despite being a bit ott in areas, but it wasn't all bad, the action was good & kept your focus in. the ending of course, drags on too long as with the middle part of the film. hey, even the opening alone was 29 minutes long!! the death of elsa was just a dirty little insult to the fans of the franchise, like killing bond in no time to die! bad, move!!

overall, it's heavily overrated, i can't tell if it's better or worse than fallout, in some ways it's better in terms of villain & story, but in others it isn't. fallout is drawn out but shorter by 22 minutes & has a bit more action & less of the blah blah blah dialogue which i couldn't make ends meat with, thereby making it pointless entirely for not just fans, but for non fans & it over bloated the runtime for no reason whatsoever. the eye candy is ace with the birds seen in this flick & the action is pretty good & in your face. the story & villain are alright, but the whole film from the over bloated opening to the drawn out middle & annoyingly drawn out ending just made this film a chore to watch, especially given it was 156 minutes too bloody long!! you may or may not enjoy this, but it is worse than fallout in more ways than one.

6/10 & that's generous considering!!

it's a decent cinema movie, preferable to watch from imax screen. kind of movie that i wouldn't bother to watch at home. as an cinema experience, the movie works. it's big, loud and looks and sounds good, but that's pretty much it. to be honest, anything above rating 6 is overrated for this movie.

the movie has way too many let downs for any better rate. action scenes aren't executed that well. to be honest, they are clumsy. way too many coincidences which saves the character. there isn't actually any thrilling bits in action scenes which would stand out from the movie. the biggest missed opportunity was the car chase. the idea was hilarious. old fiat 500 upgraded with electric motors. super cool shout out to old-meets-new technology. but the execution of the car chase? nah, wasn't nearly as good as it should had. this movies would had really benefit kind of director from john wick 4. that movie executed the action scenes almost perfectly. most of the action scenes in this movie was just lame. the whole train act felt really almost like a random thing that as just added there for reason why not. tom cruise motorcycle stunt, wasn't totally worth of the hype. the issue with the stunt was the execution.y. with probability of 1 to million he hits the target with the jump and without any shred of a thrill if the stunt goes wrong or he misses the target. also what happened after the jump, was probably worst part of the movie. super agent just happens to lose the thing he's most after which then leads to final action scene on the top of the train. there were just too many good coincidences in the movie.

why it feels like tom cruise has some issues with female actors and the characters they portray. some of the scenes with tom cruise and rebecca ferguson, which should tell that ilsa and ethan starts to get fond of each other and really cares of each other, looks so artificial. almost like they would run a relationship in real life where they have agreed, that hey let's just act this thing out. the execution of that relationship in the movie made me almost facepalm. virtually two scenes with some really odd cuddling things from kindergarten which should tell us that these two really care about each other? oh my god. the hugging scene looked like it's the last thing rebecca ferguson would really want to do. and it's not only that. also connection to other characters is super artificial. which is ironic, since the whole point of the movie is about caring and trusting to people which are closest to you. the exact same thing happened with top gun: maveric and that made me think if it's ego of tom cruise and that if he wants it's him who really should be noted at the movie and rest it's just there.

also the plot from top gun: maveric has another similarity with this movie. which is the faceless enemy. i really wonder why to repeat the same thing in this movie? tom cruise believes faceless enemy and that there's something evil out there who just wants to destroy us. oh my god. this movie would had totally benefit from bunch of characters that clearly are behind of this thing and then with some reason why they are actually doing that. or then, if the thing is with self developing computer program that wants to control just because it's programmed that way, then the movie should be clear about that. now there is just some thing called the entity which is doing things just because the thing is the entity. oh my god. this movies really had issues to convey believable villain..

the final act where gabriel, the villain, shouts "ethaaaan!" was yet again another facepalm. total random thing from a character you least would think to act that way. it was embarrassing. like, what were they thinking? lets take the last credibility out of the character which had issues with credibility in the first place. another oh my god.

so in overall: mediocre action scenes, poor relationships between star act and side act with really poor writing, silly plot, unconvincing story with unconvincing coincidences at the scenes. so how somebody can give this better than 6?

well tom cruise seems to be on fire after riding a high with "top gun maverick!" as he is in the filming the latest "mission impossible" movie film series.

his ethan hunt makes secret agents really look like they are in a sense, nerds but ethan once again does awesome stunts and one reviewer says that he can't keep doing these stunts at now 61-years old(2023). but he looks amazing.

simon pegg and ving rhames come back as his buddies and comic relief in the film. haley atwell is the new female co star. and wished she would had made it more after "captain america." still her character is where ethan and his buddies at. join the mi team or jail/morgue as she is a pickpocket person that is anything but that and you will have to see.

with a pretty lousy script, action saves it and charisma from the actors and actresses.

rebecca ferguson, the underrated henry czerny playing hunt's boss from the original movie, and vanessa kirby round out the cast. one of many actors and actresses.

i'd give this is a 6.5/10, maybe even a 7. it's not terrible, but it's incredibly boring and drawn out. i had trouble staying focused throughout pretty much the whole movie, and my husband fell asleep multiple times.

cons -


>> it has a very slow start with bad acting and dialogue, all of the politicians/gov. officials were giving noticeably bad performances. they were the focus for a lot of the beginning of the movie, not a great way to start.

>> the sandstorm scene was almost laughably bad. bad cgi gets a pass if the story is interesting, but that's not the case.

>> the biggest annoyance was the overuse of dutch angles, you can't make a boring movie more interesting by having every 3rd shot be a dutch angle. you're left with a boring movie with bad editing.

>> this could have easily been 1 movie instead of 2, they padded the run time with loads of exposition and justifications for location changing.

i had high hopes for the action scenes, part of each one was fun but overall they felt drawn out and repetitive. i went in hoping for some fun (not high expectations) and left excited for the movie to be over. i doubt i will be watching part 2.



>> tom cruise is great, he has amazing chemistry with his core crew.

>> the stunt off a cliff in norway (which has a sweet bts video) was awesome, even more so knowing it was a practical stunt.

if you're looking for some dumb fun you may enjoy this, but i do think it's just too boring. but, better this than the new indy trash tho...

dead reckoning was a bland follow up to what had been a great run from mi3 through fallout. the cast is incredibly bloated. hayley atwell's character feels completely forced and out of left field here. don't get me wrong, atwell is great on screen in anything she does but her character is just shoehorned in. does tc feel there always needs to be a damsel for him to rescue? along with atwell's grace we also get esai morales' gabriel, pom klementieff's paris and shea whigham's briggs. with all these new characters, our legacy characters get sidelined. rebecca ferguson is completely wasted. ilsa has been built up to be on par with ethan hunt and has become such an interesting character, but is sidelined for so much of this. we always have ethan's core team yet we get them for mere minutes of screen time. benji is off screen entirely too much and same for luther. with the return of kittridge and also, the white widow, there is entirely too many characters in this film. we're shown a brief flashback that is supposed to show us that gabriel and ethan have a past. but it means nothing. gabriel is meant to be this existential threat but we aren't given a reason as to why we should be threatened by him. he does not feel menacing in any way. he comes across as every other bland villain from any other action/thriller. briggs is also someone we're supposed to immediately be interested in. but we have nothing on him. all we know is that he's after ethan for reasons. when his own man asks, briggs just ignores him. is this one exchange of dialogue meant to make us suddenly care why briggs is after ethan and his team?

as always, the action is great and chaotic (in a good way). seeing cruise motorcycle jump and subsequent parachuting off the cliff was a great visual. knowing cruise performs this himself makes it that much more impressive. the sequence where the train is hanging over a cliff with hunt and grace going from car to car went on entirely too long and was not the least bit thrilling. never once did it feel either character was in danger of being killed off onscreen. i actually fast forwarded about 1/2 through. i didn't really care how they got through car 3 after getting through the first two.

cruise and mcquarrie had been on such a great run of mi films together. this one utterly disappoints. completely bloated, too many new characters that were meant to have an immediate interest in, legacy characters sidelined, and a run time that is entirely too long. maybe the point of this film was a mere setup for part 2, but this was just a big miss from tc.

'mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one' is the first part of a two-part finale for the popular spy action movie franchise, starring tom cruise as ethan hunt.

the movie tries to be an epic and dramatic conclusion to the mission: impossible saga, but ends up being a boring, even disappointing one. the movie is over too long, running for almost four hours, and too slow, with a lot of unnecessary scenes that drag the story and the pace. the movie also lacks the excitement and the fun of the previous mission: impossible movies, which were known for their fast-paced action, and witty humor. this time, for me, the movie does not have almost any memorable scenes, and instead relies on cgi to create artificial tension and spectacle.

the movie also suffers from a poor casting choice, as the new female lead character, played by ana de armas, is unlikeable, irritating, and unconvincing. she does not have charisma or chemistry with tom cruise, who btw looks too old and puffy to play the role of ethan hunt. tom cruise also seems to have lost his enthusiasm, so instead he tries to act serious, which does not suit his movie character. the film also wastes the talents of rebecca ferguson, and especially simon pegg, who this time is more than ever presented as unfunny sidekick.

this is a movie that had the potential to be a thrilling and satisfying sequel "ending", but instead turned out to be a tedious, even uninspiring one. it is a film that does not do justice to the legacy and the quality of the franchise, and does not offer anything new for fans (me).

i give it a rating of 6.5/10 just because of the production.

mission impossible has always been about masks, impossible stunts and twists. well, this has all of that and some more. the "some more" part probably brought down the film for me by a couple of notches.

the plot is interesting but the focus of the film stays 1-dimensional. the imf team and almost all the big intelligence agencies are in a "hunt" (unintended pun) for the key that could shut down a villainous ai.

the movie did not hold me, particularly scenes like an overlong chase sequence where they use an official imf car that turns out to be a fiat 500. fiat 500 is a super small car and this scene is intended to humour up the audience with the sound design for the car that keeps making a small box sound as it moves while big trucks and alfa romeos are chasing them. the joke fell flat except some teenagers giggling here or there.

you wait for it to end, while it keeps going on and on without pushing the plot further.

there are unbelievable coincidences that would even make fast and furious look better. cruise breaks through the exact window of a long train where his partner is held as a hostage, kicking down the villain.

you always have the popular train-roof fight sequences in many films. we had one in spider-man 2, skyfall, matrix reloaded, ra-1, uncharted 2, etc etc. mission impossible just recycles all of those scenes and does not do much different. you have people punching and kicking each other on the roof of a high-speed train where both forgot their pistols. and then you obviously have them ducking down for tunnels and electrical poles. obviously, the bridge ahead is bombed for the train to crash. obviously, tom cruise saves the whole train.

enough with the masks, enough with the trains and enough with last-minute extreme unlikely coincidences. fast and furious at least doesn't claim to be as smart as the mi series.

this is unfortunately the weakest film in the franchise.

the only way they can fix part 2 is by having it revealed at the beginning of the film that artificial intelligence is not omniscient and in fact there is a man and a secret organization behind everything, and this organization is controlling a very advanced program, but the ai is far from omniscient.

if they don't do this, they risk having a gigantic failure on their hands. i myself have no interest in seeing the next film if the premise remains the same. ethan hunt against a computer? no thanks!

that said, the film isn't bad. hayley atwell was a good addition to the cast. vanessa kirby is amazing, as always! and the rest of the cast is ok. the villains pom klementieff and esai morales were not convincing. better actors are needed in the central role as villains. someone capable of stepping into the shoes of sean harris and henry cavill. very sad how little importance rebeca ferguson had in the film. such a capable actress should have had something better to work with.

i must add that the chase scenes that took place in rome have terrible cgi. it's obvious that filming the car chase scenes in the historic city wouldn't be allowed, and the moment you start to think that it's all fake, it becomes very easy to notice the signs of bad cgi. the rest of the film is convincing.

but the film's biggest problem was the theme, which was very science fiction. did not like. need to move on to the next one. it would be very sad to end the franchise in a downward spiral.

there was also something else that started to make me quite uncomfortable. why doesn't tom cruise kiss these women? i mean, the film suggests that he has a kind of relationship with the character ilsa, they even say that he loves her. but he's not able to kiss her the entire movie, not even once? this just makes me think that tom cruise might be gay. the kind of thing you shouldn't be thinking about during the movie. next time, tom, take one for the team. it is not so difficult. and no, this is not objectifying women. it's life, people who are together kiss and give public displays of affection.

great franchise that has gone to the well too often. ethan hunt morphs from invincible fighter to stymied combatant ad nauseum during this repetitive cowboy chase of a film. in keeping with this well worn formula our hero manages to see another love interest killed arriving seconds late to the rescue. his girlfriends have the life expectancy of a little joe cartright fiance. dont worry, ethan gets another gal pal by film's end. surprise! is it hollywood law now that every action film have a ubiquitous waif-like female ninja who defeats dozens of manly men? the scenic train, plane (actually parachute) and automobile antics entertain like the well worn gadgets of a james bond movie. oh and there's a submarine too! escapes by both good guys and bad guys make marvel movies look more plausible. of course some good guys are really bad guys and some bad girls are not so bad after all. the new gal pal morphs from simple thief to ethical, kick ass heroine. suprise, again! despite the tired recipe, its comfort food. baked in are the seeds of the next sequel: mission impossible: "assisted living!"

someone please buy vin rhames another costume besides that of a new jersey longshoreman.

when i saw 3-star rating imdb, i decided to give this movie a look-see. started out with an interesting premise & does manage to hold your attention which is a sign of a good script, acting & directing. all was well until the chase scene which defied reality, went on too long & did something i thought was out of character for ethan hunt aka tom cruise. the head of the imf force was acting corny, silly & being outsmarted by his fellow actors (more than one & once) & where they should have prevailed, we see ethan character managing the "impossible" in eluding & invading essentially turning invisible to escape the onscreen pursuits. i kept thinking about if they did this with 007-bond character & movies & how it would flop. respect for the 00 or double o has to be maintained as he lives life & death at times. in m. i., they prolong the joking segments in addition to letting it take place to begin with. this movie should be given a sub-heading tag of comedy becasue it delves into it. the gray man & extraction movie stars don't have time to fool around or joke but they do have time to kick your butt when called upon. if the mission is impossible, lets keep it on the edge of impossibility & not deviate. one last thing, this putting on a mask & becoming another person stretches the concpet a little too far. there is no such mask that can perfectly duplicate another persons face but in this movie as with others, you cannot tell the imposter from the real guy. sounds like a magic show so add that tag to the movie description rating: silly at times & fantasy for magic sequences. c'mon tom, you got money, power, fame & expereince. use that to go deeper into the entertainment world not so much for money but to create comeback, memorable, must see this movie again experiences.

first and foremost, hats off to tom cruise and the entire cast & crew for all the hardwork they put in to make this movie. no doubt the stunts and action sequences were fantastic, more so because they were actually done instead of resorting to some lame cgi. all of the scenes were amazingly choreographed.

one interesting thing is that they increased the situational humour in this movie so it contains more funny moments compared to the previous movies. so that's a good thing.

now that we got that out of the way, lets come to the flaws. why were the russian officers speaking english with one another inside a russian submarine? jack ryan season 3 had the same problem. showing all the russians to be speaking english is ridiculous. they could have easily shown them to be speaking russian and put subtitles on.

another problem is the pacing. during the middle of the movie, it became extremely slow. especially the scene where they were in venice attending the gala night. the pace became extremely slow and i nearly fell asleep quite a few time during the movie.

also during the deal when grace was posing as alana, the talking was too long and the pace became extremely slow again making me wish i could fast forward.

another surprise was the death of ilsa. i did not see that coming. i don't really see the point of killing her off. having her in the team would have been fun and there was absolutely no reason to kill her off.

in my opinion this movie was good but not great. the pacing in this movie was a little uneven so it was hard to enjoy every bit of it. nonetheless it had a lot of enjoyable moments, mainly the action scenes but overall it was a little weak compared to the previous movies. hopefully part 2 will be better than this.

i went to the theatre really excited for this movie, although the trailer didn't really hype me.

but i really loved the last 3 instalments and i was looking forward to it.

to my disappointment, it was not even close to being as good as fallout was.

many scenes felt like scenes randomly put together.

acting was subpar, only simon pegg nailed it again. mediocre performances by vanessa kirby, hailey atwell and cruise himself.

the two guys that hunt ethan don't feel a threat, gabriel himself is cool but also doesn't feel like a big threat, paris is underused, could have been a menace.

they kill off ilsa to replace her with grace just before the final instalment? ilsa was one of the best characters in the last movies and she barely gets to speak in this one.

also, as many have said, where was the mission impossible, where were the plot twists, where was the excitement?

the movie has great production values, great filming locations, but it feels more like an excuse for tom cruise to show off his stunts...

this is the first mission impossible movie that felt superficial and soft. i understand cruise is older and just cannot be as physical as before (realizing he did do some of the outstanding stunts- fantastic). the new woman character introduced did not work. in acting or in chemistry. she always seemed to be on the verge of laughing or smiling. it was weird. dialogue was goofy and at times did not make sense. goofy scenes too. long, drawn out movie. sigh. i'm surprised cruise did not push for more quality and perfection. this is his baby. but it was a weekend action flick to watch at home with some popcorn.

the movie has all the action in the world, but something is missing.

in the past, they had an excellent team, but now they are at a minimum level and i do not see it working well. had it not been for the film's plot and the surprises that its events and story witnessed, it was not the strongest among the parts of the series.

tom cruise faces aging no matter what he does to stop the time machine, but his face is no longer the same, his eyes have lost their sparkle .

simon pegg was not what he used to be. i missed his anxious and decisive personality and the jokes he used to make, as if he were not him.

rebecca ferguson didn't add anything to the movie and her death wasn't as dramatic as it should have been , hayley atwell, she was very good and added a lot of action and excitement, but i hope that the next part will be better in all respects.

oh how much do i hate those "invincible a. i. taking over humanity and mysteriously has an archilles' heel". when secret-agent action movies want a global crisis that could be solved by one person single-handedly, that used to be nuclear missiles, but it seems that the current trend is a. i., and the new nuclear football is... its source code. as an analogy, that's like archilles being killed by his dna.

that aside, the major plot twists in this movie are introduced by nothing but pocket-picking. had gabriel simply got a zipper in his trousers, the world would already be burning in flames. modern suit designers should take that into consideration. what's more, the movie doesn't even show us how it was done, it's a close-up shot on the pocket and the next moment the key is in someone else's hand. i guess that real magic was involved, no wonder why know-all "entity" couldn't even predict that.

stereotypes. women can't drive and never win in fights. choose between two girls like you were shopping. a french person named paris. blockchains where you enter your bank account instead of a wallet id. american hackers controlling russian satellites. iron bars above train track when people are fighting on top.

lots and lots of free thrills, a fake atomic bomb that just happens to stop at the last second, tom hanks running on top of an airport, destroying train brakes that can be fixed by detaching the engine, bridge bombs counting down meaninglessly, train compartments falling one by one, exploding kitchen, falling piano, exactly one parachute, you could remove them from the film completely and nothing would change significantly.

opening sequence, letdown.

characters that ethan meet for the first time in this movie but somehow he's prepared to die for them.

just the motocycle stunt, that looked better in the behind the scenes footage.

poor score. poor villain.

death of a major character without meaning or impact.

how is this movie better than fallout?

they had venice to shoot amazing scenes but somehow we only got a disco conversation/fight and another fight on a bridge during the night. hello? take a note from your previous movie in paris.

every major stunt was in the trailer, they even had a full sequence with a train, but they gave nothing new that we hadn't scene from other movies.

the good things? ethan, the gang and the fiat 500.

we were promised action sequences unlike anything we have seen before, and the movie delivers. this time, the villain is not a human, but a powerful ai called the entity, who tricks a russian super-submarine into self-destructing in the film's clever pre-credit scene. if it weren't for the action packed content, the story would have lacked the necessary tension to keep viewers engaged until the end due to its unusually long runtime of two hours and forty-five minutes. as usual, the plot serves as an excuse for increasingly elaborate set pieces, executed so skillfully that cruise has earned a reputation for doing all the crazy things hunt is asked to do throughout the film.

this movie might only be one half of a two part ending, but it's enough to make us want to watch the other half, and there's every reason to think the last one will be even better.

~ p. x.

it's very strange writing this, being so excited after top gun maverick and mission impossible fallout, but mission impossible dead reckoning is not a good movie.

terrible story development - limited unlimited ai who can hack anything yet not using its abilities, tom cruise can only jump on a mountain train with parachute sure - like whole part of story was build around someone's desire to parachute from mountain bike jump. bad montage - multiple unneeded scenes: long car chase in rome, jumping through all train cars.

there are some good sides also - like acting - very good cast performance. humor really tries but sometimes fails.

took me a while to get round to watching this - and i'm wondering why i bothered. this is nearly as bad as mi:2. the story could have been written on a postcard - and maybe was. the set-piece stunts were not worth the effort. the italian car chase was sub- roger moore era bond, complete with an 'hilarious' moment where ethan picks up a secret car and instead of the ferrari sticking out, it turns out to be an electric fiat 500. oh, my aching sides. oh, and of course, the hard-man killer is a deranged woman - surely the very definition of a modern cliché. the motorbike stunt has been shown so many times there was no surprise and - really? - a fight on top of a train? yawn. no good story, no good lines, no good characters, no point.

as expected stunts and effects are solid as the cinematography.

the cast is brilliant selected and delivers a fantastic chemistry. we experience well written believable characters.

the story works but has two flaws: the back story between cruise and the secondary villain and an incident with too random a chance.

the movie sometimes feels stretched. it would have worked better if it was 20-30 minutes shorter.

the really bad thing is the jokes which don't land and look like they are a try for marvel humour. as if we aren't fed up enough with that.

all in all a good movie, go see it but don't expect a revelation for this franchise.

mission impossible: dead reckoning i is packed with stunts and tom cruise has done a good job doing stunts. the plot is okayish, kids and teen adults might connect to the plot better but the plot is definitely lame for understanding adult audience.

the hype was real but the delivery was subpar. the story is too long so sometimes you will feel bored. simon pegg has done a good job with well timed delivery of jokes and the jokes do make one laugh so kudos to simon. vanessa kirby does a damn good job as ilana, totally convincing acting.

some dialogues are very very lame. the car scene, the train scene, the fights bring the movie together. tc could do better on the story.

overall, a once in a while watch movie, watch on discounted movie tickets maybe. hoping a good part ii.

originally i wanted to rate this film 10/10. but the plot, problematic and somewhat unexpectedly bad. i agree that the actions are all flawless. but killing ilsa is a big mistake. it would be better off to kill her character off and not introduce a new female lead, but kill her and introduce a new character and ethan to say "your life to me is worth more than mine", step back and think, really? are you not mourning for ilsa? just a little even? i have always love the tom and mcq combo, but if this is the plot that you're carrying to part two, you will lose a fan, someone that has been behind you since day one.

although is has all the standard ingredients of a mission impossible movie (or a james bond movie etc) with the big bad russia, the impossible mission, ethan hunt who has to be immortal (with lots of botox) and a super human because he can do it all (and we think that superhero movies are sciencefiction) and the always young woman that are in the midst of it all and need some kind of saving it's very entertaining and action packed. it's as good as the others, but with one big flaw. why did they have to kill off ilsa faust? she was the most interesting character of the movie franchise and a great counterpart for ethan hunt. killing her off feels rushed and unnecessary only to make place for a new woman that will likely be killed off in the coming movies.

really bad and confusing.

ilsa died saving them. her role and character didn't do justice to her previous stunning impressions so much so that many were expecting her solo movies in mi franchise in future. her presence in future movies is also skeptical now. the way her death was portrayed looks like she will be in future movies as dream sequences. too much importance to hayley atwell character. at times i felt like it was her movie.. i would have wanted some young characters. the villain this time didn't felt dangerous and was too normal.

no cast made an impression. not even tom cruise this time. not like he did in maverick.

dear oh dearie me. where do i begin in explaining how this particular movie is on par for, or indeed takes the title of being the worst mission impossible movie in the history of the franchise? well, i guess i'll start at the beginning.

how it's possible that such accomplished actors, and a top notch production crew, and an experienced director can create two poorly written and executed exposition scenes in a major motion picture that is not a fast movie, is simply beyond my comprehension. scenes where lines of exposition that are handed off from one actor to next, like olympic relay racers hand off a baton, and then in the immediate scene fallowing, ethan and his cohorts literally hand off a mcguffin from one character to another, while handing off equally as poorly written lines of dialog. these two scenes in conjunction were not just horrible to watch, but i literally found them to be nauseating.

unfortunately this movie has no idea what it's trying to be, from the poorly written and executed comedic elements, to the paul greengrass, bourne supremacy style cinematography and editing, to the jj abrams style lens flares, to the john wick style locations and set dressing, to tom cruise playing a jackie chan-esque hapless hero, constantly apologizing and saying things like "it's okay, it's okay", before continually asking extras for assistance in driving the plot; but whatever this film is trying to be, it certainly is not trying to be a mission impossible movie.

and now we come to the actor playing the villain of the piece, mr. esai morales. and while i am a fan of his filmography, i must say that i was not a fan of his performance in this movie. while it's true that his character isn't given much to work with, what he is give to work with falls flat, making his depiction of the character, possibly the worst villain in the entirety of the franchise.

and now to the film's director, mr. christopher mcquarrie. the great albert einstein defined insanity as doing the same thing over and over again and constantly expecting different results. so, if this is the case, then surely in the world of filmmaking, constantly covering up great stunt work with poor cgi is the height of insanity! why this particular director continually insists on ruining what would otherwise be visually stunning shots, and great stunt work, by overlaying poor cgi smoke, clouds, lightning strikes, etc, again, is beyond by comprehension. maybe i missed the class in film school where you ask the star of your movie to risk life and limb in performing dangerous, yet spectacular stunt work, and then completely counteract everything that was accomplished by mixing in some ubiquitous computer generated imagery. and while some of the stun work in this film is top notch. unfortunately, the stunt fighting is some of the worst that i have seen in a film of such size and scope in quite a while. and after some of the best fight sequences in the entirety of the franchise taking place in the previous mission film, fallout, the difference in quality is noticeable.

this is not a bad movie per se, but it is a bad mission impossible movie, and one that i desperately hope will be improved upon with the release of mission impossible - dead reckoning part ii.

like the title says - this is not anywhere near an awful movie. it was shot great, and directed with real skill. and the stunts - like usual - are top notch. it's the writing and acting that really betray it.

it didn't need to be anywhere near 3 hours. the plot is too simple to sustain it and as a result the whole thing feels repetitive. the pick pocket aspect was way overused and felt like watching the same scene over and over. he finds her to help her, she crosses him and escapes while leaving him in trouble, he takes care of it and tracks her down to help her, and the process starts over again. and again. and again. related to that - the new main character is clearly an attempt at earning a spin-off soon as cruise gets too old for these. she was boring and cliché unfortunately with not much to add to the team.

speaking of which - the team had nothing to do for most of the movie. ving and simon kept waiting for something to do but ended up as 'one guy in front of the camera talking out what they're doing on the computer.' and this very much comes off like a covid movie with tons of scenes of 1 person at a time on screen and talking to each through through ear pieces or phones or whatever. none of it was smooth or hidden well and the tension was diminished because of it.

and the worst part is that all the best stunts are given away by the trailer. if you've seen them - you've seen the best parts of the movie. most of which is people talking and about 3 big action set pieces total. and the talking, good lord, the opening 10 mins is seriously just expository dialogue spoken directly to the audience and camera. i don't know what happened to the writing in this one, but it was super amateur and came off like someone good was writing with someone who has never written a screenplay before.

the ai plot bad guy is pretty weak and not super well explained too. what does it want? power? humans to die? to 'help us'? for machines to take over? i dunno, nobody else i saw the movie with was super clear on that either. we all have a general guess but if a group of adults all have different answers - maybe it wasn't that well written.

they also tried to kinda do the requel thing and turn this into a semi remake of the first one by bringing characters back from it and ending with a big train sequence. no idea why they felt the mi series needed to do this - but again it simply didn't work.

so it's probably the weakest of the newer movies by far. rogue nation was the peak in my opinion and fallout was a great successor with a much more solid bad guy for ethan to go up against compared to this one. hoping part 2 is better but after this one i don't have super high hopes...

there is such a thing as doing too much.

after fallout which was tantalising with some tender moments, dead reckoning feels like colour by numbers with tom pretty much in every frame.

the action sequences seem to need the the flimsiest of excuses to get going. sure, there are some cool bits but we are well into john wick-italian job-bourne-fast&furious-bond territory with rehashed mission antics.

what's new? an attempt at pathos (death in venice) with a convoluted, self-important script.

i still hope they bring it home in part 2 but am now prepared for mission to stutter towards the finishing line.

i am not going to watch part 2 of this double. during the whole movie it's pretty clear the actors are not in the same room. one in focus and others in a haze, close up after close up never a wide shot. sometimes the proportions don't even match. and what to say about tom cruise. botox rubber face galore, his face looks paralyzed. i sat through the whole movie hence the 6 albeit a weak six.

this weak and annoying way of making movies with no wide shots and once there is a wide shot, it's computer generated. i must say, the cgi is pretty bad in this movie. how come a movie like the fifth element, one of my favorites, has equivalent cgi or better even. it's from 1997 for freaks sake. spend your money on something else.

sat down with my husband to watch this much awaited movie on paramount+ and we were so disappointed.

a meandering script with pacing issues and even as a woman i found there were far too many poorly chosen, uninspiring female characters coupled together with ethen hunt's character being purposely weakened to accommodate all the women makes this the weakest and least cool movie of the franchise.

i have loved every previous mission impossible movie but sadly this one is overly long with poor characters, a weak storyline and comedic misses. paramount took a beating at the box office and i can see why.

let's hope the final outing is much better and a return to form.

the last hour is the better part but still not enough to rate it more than a lackluster 6/10.

disappointed with the classic action movie scenario where the protagonist still has to defeat the threat. the feel of the previous mission impossible was much better, and i just couldn't get into the film. the fight scenes with the film's antagonist were a dud for me, far too slow and lacking in fluidity.

nevertheless, the stunts performed by tom cruise are truly impressive. i literally got shivers when he fell into the void with his motorbike. the one-handed driving is also a very good scene. it's always impressive to see an actor of his age doing all that. i'm still looking forward to the next instalment in the saga, hoping for a film with a better plot.

like the missions before it, mission 7 promises a lot, but things are slower this time. the movie almost hits 3hrs runtime and the plot seems promising, but the action scenes are not as great as the last few movies.

tom cruise manages to once again prove an exemplary stunt man, especially in the final sequence, involving a train, which is probably one of the greatest i've seen.

i feel this overlong plot could have been told in one movie, but part ii comes out next year, so it's not quite the end. the plot mostly revolves around chasing down keys that make up one, which is the start of something possibly leading into part ii, but the pace is very slow in this lengthy movie, which is why i feel the second part could have just been squeezed into this one.

this movie is another example of why making sequels longer does not always work. there is nothing worse than rushing a plot, but the same can be said for slowing a plot down.

"disappointing deviation from the series' essence" ethan hunt's transformation from a covert agent to an infallible savior is emblematic of the issues plaguing this installment.

regrettably, despite my deep affection for this franchise, this film exhibits a plethora of missteps.

excessive mindless action, manipulative attempts to evoke emotion through shallow relationships, subpar writing, and a lackluster plot progression all mar this film. it could have been much better if they had focused more on character building instead of the futile and stretched action scenes. there were particularly scenes which didn't deserve so much time like the car chase scene and the train fall.

overall this movie tarnishes the once-authentic mission impossible series, casting a shadow on its reputation. it's so painful to give a 6 star to tom cruise movie.

im sorry that i went to see this film. it is a couple of hours of my life the i wont get back again.

it is much the same as all of the rest of these films. once again ethan hunt and his crew get shot at a million times and magically none of the bullets seem to hit them. improbable car chases and crashes never seem to hurt them for long. no broken bones or whiplash for our action heroes.

im tired of this sort of rubbish coming out of hollywood.

this film is ok for teenagers who are only looking for action and special effects. anyone else should definitely look elsewhere for a good better film, one with a plausible plot and some actual character development and realistic drama.

i'm really conflicted about only giving midr 6/10 but that is only because, after having never seen any of the imf films previously, i've just watched them all prior to watching this latest on at the cinema. the 4th, 5th and 6th instalments are so incredibly brilliant that dead reckoning had a very high bar to jump over.

on the plus side, the humour was spot on when it needed to be. the car chase through rome, although overly long, was fun and the pom klementiofs character had bags of menace chasing the little fiat in that hummer. the main antagonist, gabriel, was an intriguing baddie and, like others have said, would have been much, much better if he'd been a material manifestation of the ai. having gabriel as a pseudo-human would have been a great piece of sci-fi/tech writing and would have been in line with how the imf films have pushed the envelope with avant-garde technology and gadgets.

on the negative side, it is too long. considering this really is a 5.5hr film split into two, that's preposterous. it's either a blatant cash-grab or it's very poor writing and editing. i found the character of grace really poorly written and acted, but i think the acting was poor because the character was poor and we spent a lot of time with grace when we wanted ethan, ilsa, benjy and luther if we're being honest.

so yes, plenty of good with a few bad bits. i'd say this one was my least favourite if you exclude everyone's least favourite (john woo's impossible mission ii) but i am more excited for the final part of this than say, dune ii.

they dont even try anymore... they just assume that tom would carry the tension with his intense stares and run fast enough to catch our attention.

the scenery, costume, music, direction, action are all top notch, as we would suspect from a mi movie. they are on rails to deliver something entertaining. but they rely way to much on the cruise effect and the story is weak at best. the villain is way less interesting than than the last one. he is generic bad with pure hatred for humanity. no twist, no reveal, he is just after the eradication of everything for the sake of it. the famous stunt was so marketed that we only wonder when it will happen and when it does we say ''oh... there it is.... nice''.

tom assemble his crew and they all run for an hour after a mcguffin. the fact that this is a two part movie is playing against itself. we dont have the usual payoff.

the mi franchise is usually a machine so well oiled , we forget how ridiculous it can be and we let our self being carried by the action. here however, this movie is just the setup for the part 2 and we feel we didnt had the whole pie. this story isnt worth to be tell in this new anticlimactic format. it is basic at best. and there is enough downtime to let us think about the plot. which is bad.

i am still curious about the end, but i hope it will be better than this generic action movie. without the mi brand and the cruise effect, it would have been lost and forgotten, and fairly so.

mission impossible's dead reckoning part one brings back the iconic tom cruise as the fearless ethan hunt, joined by an exceptional ensemble cast including hayley atwell, rebecca ferguson, vanessa kirby, and a host of other talented actors. while tom cruise's performance continues to be exemplary, the film's story falls short of its potential. it delves into a familiar topic that has been explored countless times before, leaving us yearning for something fresh and unpredictable to reignite the franchise's excitement.

amidst the film's shortcomings, one cannot overlook the brilliantly executed action scenes that do make an impact. while there are fewer action sequences compared to the previous instalment, the ones present leave us on the edge of our seats, especially the heart-pounding car chase that adds an adrenaline rush to the viewing experience.

however, not all aspects of the film deliver on their promise. the scenes set in venice, which held great promise, fail to reach their full potential and could have been more thrilling and engaging. nevertheless, the film manages to retain its allure, thanks to the unwavering charisma of tom cruise as ethan hunt.

one of the film's most significant drawbacks is its excessive length, as it could have benefitted from tighter editing to maintain a more captivating pace and keep the audience fully invested in the unfolding events.

in conclusion, mission impossible's dead reckoning part one offers a mix of highs and lows. tom cruise's stellar performance and some standout action scenes add excitement and spectacle to the film, but the repetitive storyline and lack of fresh ideas dampen its overall impact. despite its flaws, fans of the franchise will likely find enough enjoyment to appreciate the latest instalment.
