it's hard to remember the last time i sat down in a theater and had a smile on my face from the movie's opening credits to its ending. it is 2 hours and 45 minutes that fly by, dominated by some of the best action choreography and stunt work in modern cinema. every actor provides solid performances, especially hayley atwell as newcomer grace.

my best praise for this film is that in a way it does bond better than bond has been since skyfall. with outlandish, menacing villains (pom klementieff's assassin was a standout), thrilling action, and a great sense of humor that lands far better than most modern films' attempts at marvel-style quips, dead reckoning takes a step back from fallout's dark, brooding, twisting story to deliver a plot, that while still serious, allows itself to be fun.

finally, i have to praise tom cruise in this film. he delivers all the death-defying stunts you could want, proving that he is, as many have said, "the last true movie star". he and the director, christopher mcquarrie also have a special announcement before the movie starts thanking the audience for supporting the film, which is a sentiment i wish was echoed more in modern cinema, where it often feels the people behind productions hate or are indifferent to the people who watch their productions.

ow boy do i love the mission impossible franchise!

the stunts are still so impressive and a pleasure to look at, knowing most of them were done by tom himself.

the casting choices are as always on point and actors are nailing the characters perfectly.

but let's talk about the best thing about this movie, it's definitely the use of sound.

music is a big part of how you can feel a movie scene and mission impossible always delivers on that part!

the tension they built up and how they deliver it on screen is just amazing.

ethan hunt is still the best spy on the big screen, i stand with that!

on the 7th installment of the popular and lucrative film franchise ethan hunt and co. take on a new task and as always all hell breaks loose. pitted against the "entity", a nemesis of mythological proportions the group must make use of their vast and impressive talents and resources to tackle and defeat such a seemingly insurmountable foe. taking the viewer on a wild ride one is immediately subject to car chases, skilled fistfights, gunfire and things being smashed and thrown about. the varied locations the series is known for is on full display as scenic views alternate with grimy back alleys as backdrop to the nonstop action. what's funny is the breathless rush of the film's pace with it's in your face action is its biggest weakness. suffering from the "john wick" syndrome of compensating a shaky plot with endless head-busting the tired and worn action cliches wear out at once leaving one in paint-drying tedium. the film could have benefitted from good editing and a shorter length. tom cruise looks fine and can still carry the film but age is beginning to show. this film being the penultimate in wrapping up the series would benefit him and the franchise nicely. if anything it's good to see cruise, simon pegg, ving rhames and rebecca ferguson together onscreen again. one of cinema's longest and best series this latest entry is one you wouldn't mind seeing.

exhibiting a visionary approach to contemporary threats, "mission impossible: dead reckoning part 1" introduces artificial intelligence as the main antagonist, reflecting our modern technological landscape. the film is another milestone in the franchise, bolstered by tom cruise's relentless commitment to delivering high-quality action sequences.

a standout moment is cruise's execution of the cliff-jumping scene, shot without a stunt double. this death-defying sequence sets a new standard in action cinema, making even the most seasoned viewer hold their breath.

despite the film's overall strengths, it isn't without a few minor missteps. the stylized fight sequences involving the japanese characters can come off as overdone, while certain moments in the car chase scenes may test the viewers' suspension of disbelief.

however, these small flaws don't detract from the overall enjoyment of the film, which thrills with its intriguing narrative, action-packed scenes, and cruise's masterful performance. i rate it a solid 9 out of 10, marking it as a must-watch for action film enthusiasts. we can only hope the sequel continues this trend of high-quality filmmaking.

if you liked the last few installments in the series then you will like this one too. the stunts are awesome and overall there is an epic scale to the action. tom cruise is tom cruise, the dude is a legend and knows how to make a great movie. there are beautiful women but without the clumsy sex and romance scenes that serve no purpose except interrupting the story and making families uncomfortable. so that's appreciated.

it's not a perfect movie, it does fall back on well-worn action movie tropes and plot devices at times. they're executed well but still, not creative. it's also very long at 2hr43m, though it was enjoyable throughout. there is a nebulous artificial intelligence villain lurking in the background that probably doesn't make much sense if you think about it but i didn't feel any strain in suspending my disbelief.

it's part 1 of 2 but it definitely works as a complete, standalone movie and you feel satisfied at the end. it doesn't leave you hanging with some horrible "to be continued" (1 to 2 years from now) style ending. was a great watch at the theater and lots of effort was put into the audio effects to make use of that environment which was cool. tom cruise knows what's up. looking forward to part 2.

i went to see the movie on my local cinema. at first i had my precautions about the movie because even though the trailer was great we had our share this year with movie who had amazing trailers and they didn't exceed expectations ( ant man 3 , flash , shazam furry of the gods ). but i didn't expect the movie to be so so good ! it started with a mystery on what the submarine was caring and how the hell did the torpedo came back and hit the submarine. then of course it had the classic opening with ethan taking the message for the mission which message then explodes. gabriel's return was really well served and his role in the plot of the movie was big. the story line with the virus was clever and really well written. the fight on the train was amazing directed and every second i was wondering if someone would die. then the movie cuts but not suddenly like spider verse and fast x. all in all it was a really good movie maybe the 3rd best on the series for me or the 4th best and really worth watching it one of the best that came out this year. yom cruise never disappoints.

talking about the movie as the movie is divided into two parts .the action scenes was great no need to doubt because of tom cruise. but coming to story side it was pretty normal story line not as expected .from start of the story it was normal it can be good. the director only focused on the action scenes and to improve the action and thrills of audience than older parts .but really the action scenes are mind blowing compare to older mi movies. no doubt direction was good as other mission impossible series .lets see what happens in part two..overall great movie must watch.

#bestdirection #tomcruise #missionimpossibledeadreckoning.

this is a fun action movie and another worthy entry in a consistently excellent series.

the cast is game, with cruise as protagonist ethan hunt, pegg and rhames as his tech buddies. the gorgeous, soulful rebecca ferguson is present but sadly underused - and yes, i do have a crush for her: blame the opera scene in rogue nation and that yellow dress. newcomers include atwell, klementieff and morales; czerny returns to the series after nearly 30 years (he was the guy who got a fish tank blown up in his face in the first film) as smug-but-not-completely-evil bureaucrat kittridge.

the set-pieces are fun and spectacular as usual, especially an inventive train crash in the climax.

villains are somewhat lacking. the big bad is a personality-less, nearly omnipotent ai who is only occasionally scary and memorable; i liked a creepy scene in venice where it affects the communications between ethan and friends and starts imitating benji's voice misleading ethan: the movie needed more of that. then we have mysterious baddie gabriel, whose previous connection to ethan is implied but never properly explained and made interesting / not cliched. the best is by far pom klementieff as a feral assassin with a unique personal style.

although, to its credit, dead reckoning never really drags, there are too many scenes with characters earnestly trading somber chunks of exposition - this would have been better with the breezier pacing of, say, ghost protocol.

still, another perfectly competent entry. to quote the name of one of hans zimmer's best tracks in mi2: mission accomplished.

7,5/10.

with another addition in the mission impossible series, the rogue ethan hunt is back with his gang to fight the greatest evil yet. even though there are already many movies speculating on the dangers of artificial intelligence, dead reckoning mixes it up with the usual touch of intense action sequences & somewhat unique and newer storyline. all the acts of movie screams mission impossible & tom cruise with hayley atwell's quirky acting tom cruise's once again heart throbbing stunts. although the famous cliff jump sequence is not as impactful as it was hyped up to be, it is mostly because of other much more intense sequences especially in the closing act which is something i assure nobody has seen before in cinemas. it is a mission impossible movie through and through & would expect nothing less. the only setback is the opening act dialogues which feels lazy and cliche, as if they might have been written by ai itself, which would be very on plot if true. but the movie picks up very quickly to more entertaining and fun parts.

i recently watched mission impossible, and i have to say it was an absolute blast! the film lived up to its reputation of delivering jaw-dropping stunts that left me on the edge of my seat throughout. tom cruise, as ethan hunt, once again proved why he is the king of action movies, delivering a top-notch performance that's nothing short of exceptional.

one of the highlights of mission impossible was the introduction of hayley as a new cast member. her presence added a fresh dynamic to the team and her performance was impressive. i was pleasantly surprised by her ability to hold her own alongside the seasoned cast, and i can't wait to see more of her in future installments.

the chemistry among the entire cast was fantastic, and each actor brought their a-game to the table. the camaraderie and banter between the characters added an extra layer of enjoyment to the film, making it not only an action-packed ride but also a fun and engaging experience.

speaking of action, mission impossible delivered in spades! the stunts were mind-blowing, and it's evident that tom cruise's dedication to performing his own stunts pays off in every adrenaline-pumping sequence. the practical effects and well-choreographed action set-pieces truly set this franchise apart from other action films, and mission impossible continues to raise the bar.

the storyline was well-crafted and kept me engrossed from start to finish. the plot twists and turns kept me guessing, and the movie did a great job of balancing high-octane action with moments of suspense and intrigue. it's refreshing to see an action film with a compelling narrative that complements the spectacle.

"mission impossible - dead reckoning part one" was a blast for me. i went to the theatre without ever watching other entries of the franchise and only because of the trust in tom cruise after "top gun: maverick" that i found nice (not spectacular however) and entertaining. and this one to me was even better. i had a great time thanks to the intriguing enough plot and great action. this aspect in particular was very well done thanks to the direction, the editing and also the sets (the venice one was fantastic in my opinion). it is probably too long being around 160' and some repetitions in terms of situations are present, but overall i never found myself bored but always engaged. as mentioned, the plot is nothing special and the characters are not very deep but it's all functional since the goal of the movie is to entertain the viewers and it certainly does. the only thing that here and there bugged me was the cgi that is not always good. and this is particularly evident when you have tom cruise doing his classical stunts that are all practical and a cgi shot shortly after. but in general i won't be too picky with the smaller things that slightly compromises the viewing experience because in the end this one is a great action movie. if you want to watch something thrilling and frenetic this is a perfect choice, that is very well crafted and in which mostly all the parts are contributing in having the viewer on the edge of the seat. if you are instead looking for a deep movie this one is not your choice but it's perfectly ok, it's not the scope of "mission impossible". in the end: have yourself a blast as well!

the iconic "mission impossible" film series has been brought back by christopher mcquarrie with a bang!

in the movie, tom cruise, who plays ethan hunt, is on another mission-this time against ai.

the movie lasts for two hours and forty-five minutes without slowing d. action movie fans will find this to be an amazing experience, and the narrative and colour scheme used throughout, heighten the level of immersion.

this movie features tense action scenes set to stunning frantic music.

on top of that, the film's cinematography is terrific, and the locations that were used for filming have been ingeniously utilised to give audiences a visually compelling experience.

hayley atwell is amazing; she portrays grace and gives a powerful performance, and think she comes out on top in terms of acting.

tom cruise is phenomenal as always, we all know he's famous for a lot of things and is riding a bike is one of them ; the only difference is that he continues doing so as he jumps from the norwegian alps.

yes, he actually jumped off a cliff for real.

the best part about tom's courageous stunt is that, although though we were all aware it was going to happen because this historic moment was heavily featured in the movie's marketing campaign, it still astounds you when it actually happens in the movie.

you didn't even realise it, but you watched the entire scene with your mouth open because of the exceptional level of execution.

this movie is ideal for watching on the widest screen possible with your loved ones.

definitely worth your time and money.

well i just got out of the theater and here are my thoughts!

they introduced a new character, grace. i had no connection whatsoever with her. she was annoying she would always be running away and putting ethan in bad scenarios. the worst part is ethan is head over heals for her and won't let her leave. if your going to kill off ilsa please create a better love interest. that's my only thing i don't like about the movie.

i loved the idea of ai being the villain in the movie. it was something we haven't seen through the mi films.

like the other films it was confusing to put things together but for me it was less complicated and i appreciated that!

the stunts were pretty cool. but they were so infrequent. i think they were saving up for the big jumping off the cliff with the motor cycle. don't get me wrong it was cool but u wished there were some other ones that were big like that to.

overall the movie was an 8/10 and im stoked for the next one!

first and foremost - tom cruise is an action legend. at this point its not even controversial to call him the best action movie star to have ever existed - its factual. no matter which way you cut it, arnie and stallone never dirt biked off a mountain range into a base jump. and that just covers the main stunt in this movie. you only have to look back at the previous entries in the series to see the kind of crazy impressive stunts tom cruise has done. sure, maybe hes a weirdo in his private life, but credit where credit is due... hes basically become ethan hunt for real at this point.

to talk about the actual movie, what can i say? its mission impossible. definitely ridiculous, undeniably watchable. personally, i think this has better action than the last few movies, but previous films in the series make far more sense and have a better plot.

that said, its another impressive installment into a franchise which is remained strong since the late 90s (mission impossible 2 not withstanding obviously). of course everybody has a favorite from the series (1 and 3 being my own choices) but this stands deservedly among the best m:i has to offer.

this is the summer blockbuster of yesteryear audiences have been crying out for. no politics, no wokeism, just good old fashioned action. no wonder its killing at the box office.

this movie emerges as a thrilling cinematic roller-coaster, replete with some of the most awe-inspiring action sequences ever seen on screen. tom cruise consistently proves himself as the linchpin of the franchise, remarkably executing all his stunts - notably the motorcycle cliff leap. his unwavering dedication to both his role and the franchise's integrity is genuinely commendable.

supporting cruise's formidable performance is the robust supporting cast. rebecca ferguson, hayley atwell, and vanessa kirby don't merely keep pace; they provide memorable and compelling performances. beyond the heart-racing action, the film evokes genuine emotion, presenting poignant moments between cruise and his fellow actors, adding an unexpected depth to this film genre.

and i am saying that in every possible way. tom cruise. the man did it again. saved movies & theatres. it felt so good finally watching a real movie after so many generic passable cgi fest for what they call a film nowadays.

everything's good. the action, the cast, the music & all. watching the imf team once again in a frame together did put a smile on my face.

the movie was breathtakingly beautiful. go for the experience. go to watch some terrific action sequences put on the big screen. and finally go for the love of cinema again.

thanks & eagerly waiting for part 2 to experience it all again for one last time in a theatre.

finally, a "part one" that's not afraid to call itself "part one". there's no spider-verse, fast x trickery here. this one actually feels kind of complete by its end, too - even if there is definitely still more of this story to be told. anyway...

dead reckoning part one is the seventh instalment in the long-running mission: impossible franchise and, while it's not quite as good as fallout or even ghost protocol, it's absolutely remarkable that it is as good as it is. we're seven films in and there are no signs of slowing down. christopher mcquarrie returns to direct once again, but (like he did last time) makes this one feel distinct enough from its predecessors to fit the franchise's style of changing direction each and every time. after a slightly oddly-paced start, the remaining 135 minutes completely fly by; set-piece after set-piece of the highest calibre hit the screen and never let up. the action is great, it's got a lot of suspense, the characters are all good and overall it's just a blast. hayley atwell steals the show as grace, the best new character to join the series since rebecca ferguson's ilsa faust (who is sort of put in the background to give grace the chance to shine i guess. come on, tom, you can have more than one strong female character sharing the limelight with you surely), and tom cruise manages to blow your mind with the things he does for your entertainment once again.

this is seriously one of the best film franchises to ever exist. sure, mission: impossible ii is part of it but that's good enough. when the worst in the series is good, the majority are absolutely fantastic, and the best is one of the greatest action films of all time, you know you've got something excellent on your hands.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one, the 2023 action-packed extravaganza directed by the maestro christopher mcquarrie, is an uproariously entertaining installment that takes the mission: impossible franchise to new heights of adrenaline-pumping hilarity. brace yourself for a side-splitting adventure that pays homage to its predecessors while charting its own riotous course.

from the adrenaline-fueled opening scene to the explosive grand finale, dead reckoning part one grabs you by the funny bone and never lets go. the film seamlessly blends action with comedic genius, propelling audiences into a whirlwind world of death-defying stunts and constantly evolving hilarity. this thrilling recipe ensures that both fans of the franchise and newcomers are treated to a side-splitting rollercoaster ride of laughter and awe.

tom cruise, as the indomitable ethan hunt, wields his impeccable comedic timing like a secret weapon. his physicality, timing, and sheer commitment to the role bring a level of comedic brilliance that is rare in action films. cruise fearlessly throws himself into every wild and outlandish action sequence, creating moments that elicit equal measures of gasps and laughter. the way he balances gravity-defying stunts with impeccable comedic delivery is nothing short of jaw-dropping.

the film hits its comedic stride by expertly blending its action-packed sequences with a cavalcade of quirky supporting characters. simon pegg, reprising his role as the hilarious benji, delivers non-stop one-liners and punchy banter that consistently land. ving rhames, as the ever-wise luther stickell, provides a blend of deadpan humor and steady guidance amidst the chaos. the chemistry and camaraderie among the cast translates seamlessly, injecting the film with a contagious energy that will leave you in stitches.

one cannot overlook the relentless creativity infused into the film's action set pieces, which serve as fertile ground for uproarious moments. from high-speed chases involving absurdly unconventional vehicles to a sequence that involves a daredevil mission through a hall of mirrors, the film's action scenes never fail to surprise and, more importantly, entertain. director christopher mcquarrie has masterfully woven comedy into the fabric of every thrilling sequence, enhancing the already dynamic mission: impossible formula.

most exhilaratingly, the film enjoys self-awareness that amplifies the laughter. it winkingly acknowledges the over-the-top nature of the franchise while reveling in its own outrageousness. the script embraces the absurdity and runs with it, refusing to take itself too seriously. this deliciously tongue-in-cheek approach ensures there's never a dull moment, with a constant stream of witty lines and unexpected comedic beats that will keep you guessing and guffawing until the credits roll.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a supercharged bundle of action and hilarity that showcases the franchise's evolution in its ability to make you clutch your sides in laughter. it perfectly marries spectacle, wit, and tomfoolery, appealing to both action enthusiasts and followers of comedic cinema. so fasten your seatbelts, prepare for jaw-dropping stunts, and get ready to embark on a mission that will make you laugh your way to cinematic bliss.

in conclusion, this uproarious installment of the mission: impossible franchise sets new heights for action-comedy fusion. tom cruise's comedic brilliance, coupled with a consistently funny ensemble cast and chaotic set pieces, instantly propels dead reckoning part one into the pantheon of unforgettable action comedies. with a combination of thrilling missions and laugh-out-loud moments, this film proves that even when facing impossible odds, laughter is the best weapon in ethan hunt's arsenal. mission achieved, hilarity obtained!

let me just say, this is the reason i go to the movies. those 2 hours and 45 minutes felt like 1. tom cruise is one of the last true movie stars left in the industry.

the acting, music, set pieces, adrenaline, stakes, story, writing were all top notch. my favorite aspect of this movie though, would have to be the villain(s?) the "entity" can be everywhere and nowhere at once, and has access to almost everything under the sun. this makes for a feeling of desperation to be draped over the entirety of the movie. his semi-physical counterpart gabriel is convincing as well.

the most well done scene was the one in the club, where ethan and company realize that the entity is completely surrounding them. well done camera angles, music and acting.

i also loved how they had the balls to kill off a prominent character. it gives the story real stakes and adds to the feeling of dread. that being said, ilsa/rebecca ferguson will be missed.

one of my only real problems with this movie was certain action scenes where a character *narrowly and miraculously* escapes certain death. this happens quite a lot at the end and it gets exhausting. that being said, the falling train and the motorcycle sequence were astounding to watch, regardless of the occasional cliches.

a truly spectacular movie, and the best in the franchise so far. tom cruise continues to kill it and has no signs of stopping.

what more can i say than first "thank you tom cruise for making going to the movies worth it. it's been a pleasure to experience your sheer genius in cinema. "this is till now the best movie of the year. cannot wait for the second part to arrive quickly. i was literally on the edge of my seat with thrill. not a single dull moment. and the masterful stunts are perhaps the most thrilling in movie history. after they way they ended fallout i really thought it was the best way you could end an action flick. but tom cruise and co outdid themselves. with benedict del toro playing one of the greatest villains of all time. if you haven't watched it yet,it's your turn to rush to the movies.

seriously, i really hope we're in the endgame of the franchise since it's been going for a little bit too long, cruise getting old, and we don't now how long he can maintain his performance in the ever-growing need of action flick situation thanks to hollywood takin the political message spreading route no one asks for. as the first part of the franchise's endgame i pretty enjoy it very much, it's very much the mission impossible we know and love action-wise, story-wise, character-wise, twist-wise with the added distinguished feature of longer, if not time-wasting, humor and non-human main threat, or in other words, it's getting closer to the sci-fi genre than the previous installment without diminishing the importance of human element. sure some scenes get a little bit dragged on but it's paid off with a satisfying climax and cliffhanger ending that makes us wanting for more immediately. i have no expectation for the second part, since i already know it's gonna be cool as hell as usual, other than expecting the challenge gets monstrously harder for our heroes and heroines here that it able to give us a satisfying ending, one with global impact on humanity as a whole at all aspects of their live, because i want the story to be much more significant than the good guys kicking the bad guys' asses then accepting the next mission without the environment even aware of what's going on around as usual, or in other words, let it be armaggeddon!!

8.5/10.

i am such a huge fan of this franchise, my voicemail greeting has been based off the m:i intro with the theme music for well over a decade. "m:i dead reckoning: part one" had its moments but i've never been a fan of huge leaps. the biggest, by far, is ethan hunt's life, pre-imf - the only way the villain, gabriel, comes into existence. who was marie to ethan anyway? the only mention of hunt's life pre-imf has been margaret hunt and donald hunt, who kittridge used as pawns in the original movie. i can't say i am a fan of a new villain who ethan apparently knew before joining the imf. a new villain known to no one would have been better because we have no background on marie, who gabriel killed though ethan was charged with the murder. ethan had to choose between going to prison for marie's murder or joining the imf. i really didn't care that we had no background on ethan and his team members in the original movie. it's especially sad that ilsa faust is lost only because of gabriel. the ilsa from "rogue nation" and "fallout" could have easily taken gabriel. ethan hunt, on top of killing the ai entity, will seek to avenge the deaths of marie and ilsa by killing gabriel in the next film.

i wasn't sure what to make of grace's character but disguised as white widow, she declined $100m usd from kittridge, and it was epic. grace and ethan should make for an exciting "part two" next year. finally, for a film over 2.5 hours in length, i expected more explanation of how the two keys were retrieved from the dead sailors yet nobody retrieved their sunken submarine, which houses the ai entity. part two will likely be a race to retrieve the submarine and the ai entity. i have a feeling ethan will welcome another new member in part two otherwise he is the only frontline fighter on his team. i don't see hayley atwell/grace, training to become a fighter after a many years of being a thief. it could be paris, who still had a pulse at the end of part one. if she survives, she should be loyal to the americans for saving her life, especially after ethan had spared her.

mission: impossible is undoubtedly another adventure and action movie by tom cruise. this movie will cross billions no doubt. the cast is great, the new additions add so much to the usual mi crew. the stunts are performed in the usual high quality and hope to give you that wow feeling. cruise, pegg and rhames were awesome as always, whigham and davis were great additions, but the power quartet of ferguson, atwell, klementieff and kirby, really went above and beyond in making this movie perfect. not to mention the chilling confidence of morales as gabriel, who practically oozes tangible danger.

mission impossible series is my favourite, i was eagerly waiting for the next sequel when the trailer was released, i was starstruck after watching high-octane scenes and car chases. tom cruise is the most hardworking actor i have ever seen. pom klementiff played the character paris the acting was mindboggling, i must say she captured the screen whenever she appears there is an action sequence she pulled off. i've become a fan of her. hailey atwell, i have watched her movies a few, in mi she outperformed her role awesomely. the man, the legend, and my childhood hero tom cruise one word for him "amazing" i was feeling goosebumps in the scenes when he jumped off his bike from the cliff or the train fight sequence. vanessa kirby aka white widow looks elegant when she appears on screen and her act was awesome wingh rhames and simon pegg they played their roles beautifully. all the other actors were amazing.

prepare to be blown away as mission impossible 7: dead reckoning delivers an action-packed thrill ride that leaves you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. as a die-hard fan of the mission impossible franchise, i can confidently say that this latest installment is a jaw-dropping spectacle that has set the bar even higher for action films. from heart-stopping stunts to mind-bending espionage, this movie has it all!

one of the standout scenes that had me completely captivated was the breathtaking end train sequence. in true mission impossible fashion, the tension escalates with each passing second, keeping you glued to the screen as ethan hunt (tom cruise) executes seemingly impossible maneuvers to save the day. the stunning cinematography combined with the high-octane action had my heart pounding, and i found myself holding my breath throughout the entire sequence. it's a rollercoaster of emotions, and it's moments like these that remind you why the mission impossible franchise continues to be an unstoppable force in the action genre.

but it's not just the action that makes mission impossible 7: dead reckoning shine. the film's plot is intricate and keeps you guessing until the very end. twists and turns abound as ethan hunt and his team navigate a treacherous world of international espionage, double-crosses, and unexpected alliances. the screenplay is cleverly written, keeping the audience engaged while seamlessly blending moments of intense action with character-driven scenes that provide depth to the narrative.

one of the film's strongest points is undoubtedly the exceptional performances by the cast. tom cruise's portrayal of ethan hunt is as impeccable as ever, proving once again why he is the perfect fit for this iconic role. his dedication to performing his own stunts is awe-inspiring, and it adds an authenticity to the action that is hard to come by in modern cinema. the supporting cast, including rebecca ferguson, simon pegg, and ving rhames, bring their a-game and infuse the movie with humor and emotional depth that elevate the overall experience.

as a fan, i couldn't help but appreciate the nods to previous mission impossible films scattered throughout the storyline. these callbacks serve as a homage to the franchise's rich history while also adding an extra layer of nostalgia for long-time followers like myself.

the film's visual effects are top-notch, seamlessly blending practical stunts with cutting-edge cgi. the cinematography captures the grandeur of the action sequences, making it feel as though you are right in the middle of the adrenaline-pumping chaos. the intense sound design further enhances the experience, immersing the audience in every explosion, chase, and fight.

mission impossible 7: dead reckoning also successfully manages to strike an emotional chord, exploring the human side of its characters. ethan hunt's internal struggles and the sacrifices he makes for the greater good make him a relatable and complex protagonist. this emotional depth adds substance to the film, making it more than just a high-octane action flick.

as the credits rolled, i couldn't help but feel a sense of anticipation and excitement for the future of the mission impossible franchise. the seeds planted throughout the film for potential sequels have left me eagerly awaiting what comes next.

in conclusion, mission impossible 7: dead reckoning is a true cinematic gem that deserves all the praise it receives. the end train scene alone is worth the price of admission, but the film as a whole is an enthralling experience that leaves you begging for more. with its heart-pounding action, engaging plot, exceptional performances, and stunning visuals, this film exemplifies the epitome of the action genre. i'm already counting down the days until the next mission impossible installment. bravo, mr. cruise and the entire creative team!

mission impossible has carried the torch for the sans superhero action blockbuster and you can tell dead reckoning spared little to no expense for the budget. the sound design, soundtrack and visuals continue to perform at a high level. the filming locations are beautiful, the choreography for the action is tight and the effort to go with some practical choices as opposed to cgi are reflected in how good the movie looks. whether cruise is whipping around in a fiat, soaring through the air in a parachute or sprinting through an airport, dead reckoning part one is always engaging and keeps you on the edge of your seat.

tom cruise may not be an ageless wonder but he works his tail off for the box office winnings. the commitment he shows to attempt what he attempts in every mi movie is some kind of dedication. he doesn't look like he's 30 years old anymore but he's still a bona fide action star and i still enjoy his performances as ethan hunt every time. ving rhames and simon pegg are your regulars and i've always enjoyed that the later movies are more team centric. i look forward to watching pegg's frantic yet funny delivery and rhames' cool presence just as much and they help keep things bouncier when the movie needs to release some of the tension. rebecca ferguson can be a little hit and miss with project choices (even though she's usually good in the role no matter what) but ilsa faust is my preferred character for her to play. she's appropriately steely when the action gets hairy but she's always got this mischievous glint in her eye (accompanied with a knowing smirk) that fit perfectly when she's interacting with the team and she's always been a seamless fit in the franchise. i was so happy to see hayley atwell in the trailers for this, she's long overdue for another turn in a tentpole franchise. she does it all in part one, she's great in every scene, she's gorgeous and i hope she continues to be a featured player going ahead. i wasn't sure what to think of esai morales in the marketing but i really liked his take on gabriel. he's as smooth as silk as the overconfident envoy for the entity, he stole almost every scene he was in without falling into any maniacal cliches. shea whigham got a bunch of laughs as briggs. if there was any disappointment for me, i wish pom klementieff had gotten a more developed character. she's great in the guardians movies and although she's throwing her all into paris, she's reduced to just fighting, driving and being a generically evil flunky for the entity.

i enjoyed dead reckoning part one throughout but i wasn't as blown away by it as i thought i would be. it's well directed, well cast and it has some decent set pieces but it lacked the wow factor that some of the previous mi movies have delivered. i do have to applaud them for saving the best for last however. the scene on the train is long but it's by far the most satisfying in the movie. you get some crazy stunts, some interesting twists in the narrative and a rewarding payoff. it certainly had me squirming in my seat and while you know the probable outcome, it certainly gave me what i wanted from a mission impossible movie.

this franchise continues to have a ridiculous amount of staying power. dead reckoning: part one isn't the high point in the franchise that fallout was but dr part 1 is still way better than most stuff being shown in this genre. a decent entry in this franchise is worth the price of admission at your local theatre every time. tom cruise and the rest of the cast are still a ton of fun in their respective roles, they push the envelope with the action with each new film and i'm definitely looking forward to seeing where dead reckoning part two will go next. i'd fully recommend catching it at the theatre if you feel like a little heart-stopping action while on your night out.

the latest installment in the mission impossible movie franchise is entertaining and exciting. it's well worth the money and time to see it in a movie theater. the action sequences are amazing . . . however, the movie is mostly about the action sequences. there is little to the plot ("get the key!" alternating with "what does the key do?"). this is combined with lots of slight of hand (literally)

tom cruise is solid (again) as ethan hunt. and i always wish there was more of simon pegg (benji) and ving rhames (luther). there are lots of bad guys . . . which means lots of fights. and i don't ever want to see pom klementieff (paris) behind me in traffic. the rome car chase seen is one of the best car chase scenes i've ever watched. too bad paris died.

i predict that ilsa faust is truly not dead. rebecca ferguson contributes too much to the franchise. plus, it goes back to what ethan tells ilsa early in the movie "you're dead! stay dead!" i suspect she's already a step ahead in locating the submarine. after all, she was able to locate one half of the key early on. she knows more than we've seen so far.

esai morales (gabriel) is not fully developed and does little more than give sinister looks. vanessa kirby (the white widow) gives her helter-skelter look while uttering the line "but, i'm merely a broker.", but also felt underdeveloped. since these characters will continue into part ii, perhaps they will become more developed.

briggs and degas seem superfluous to the story and movie. their looks of "what are we doing here?" are probably in sync with how the actors feel about their characters in the movie. perhaps their presence will make more sense in part ii.

whether kittridge (henry czerny) is good or bad is left to be seen. cary elwes as denlinger seems miscast. playing a conniving and powerful character just seems too much of a stretch for him. i felt relief when gabriel slit his throat and leaves him for dead (and unlike, ilsa, i do believe denlinger is dead).

one thing that tom cruise doesn't get enough credit for is the creation of characters for women that hold their own in the storyline, in fights, and more. yes, these women can throw a punch and kick a$$. but, once again, they are not treated with kid gloves and take beatings too. the premise that 'you don't hit girls' is unknown to these people.

cruise might be showing his age, but his films sure aren't. dead reckoning combines some of the greatest action sequences in recent memory, with a futurist plot that far surpasses any of the other mission impossible films.

as with nearly every installment of this franchise, there is some rather unashamed narrative exposition towards the beginning, but in this case it was probably for the best. the "show, don't tell" theory of screenwriting is usually best, but with a runtime already nearing three hours, i think this was probably a wise choice.

i am particularly impressed that this film managed to take the tired setting of a speeding train, and turn it into something genuinely gripping. those last few minutes are easily the stand outs for the entire franchise.

finally, most characters (new and old) really show some sort of character development, which i believe is a key to making a film of this length feel worth the watch. i am very excited for part two.

since the moment rogue nation hit the theaters, the revamp of this franchise was dubbed for me as a success, to this day i still feel rogue nation is peak mission impossible, and they have successfully managed to do one of the most difficult things in a hollywood franchise: quality consistency.

i was introduced to mission impossible back when it launched it's third title, i can't say i became an instant fan, i saw the first and second after and while i do acknowledge for their time they were fresh and action packed, they were also a bit generic and predictable action type films. ghost protocol already showed some signs of improvement but then rogue nation came to theaters and i was blown away.

the production value was outstanding, amazing action packed sequences, including some of the most crazy practical effects led by tom cruise ever put on a film for the sake of entertainment, great new charismatic characters, amazing landscapes and a solid storyline with some good twists, an overall success for the action genre that has been pretty generic for many years.

i was pulled back into it, this is how you revitalize a franchise while maintaining its original elements in an almost "homage" type of approach. fallout was also a solid sequence to rogue nation but it didn't have the same impact as the previous for me and i slightly feel the same way about dead reckoning part one - it still manages to give you some adrenaline pumping moments, i can't stress enough how great the majority of the action and fight sequences look and the classic practical crazy stunts from tom cruise and most important for me in this particular title the charismatic people that lead the film.

i feel they play a huge part on it both the familiar faces and the new characters they are the soul of this action flick, while i praise the same elements as the previous that manage to still feel fresh and original, plot wise i am not as engaged as i was for rogue nation, i feel to a certain extent it will be hard to continue to create original and plausible threats in the world for our heroes to save it, but then again it's still a very good movie overall, i am definitely eager to see it wrapped up on part 2.

since these became high-budget blockbusters, the story has more or less revolved around a bad guy and a nuke. more than any of those other recent ones, you need to suspend your disbelief with regard to the main story in this. it's exposed very cheesily in the writing through awkward dialogue and cringy "briefings".

as such, the line between these and the fast & furious movies grows ever thinner; as the fast series has become more of a "save the world" franchise, mi has strayed into "i got family" territory. the imf is treated like a frat now, pledge and get in.

if you're able to look past these things, this is one of the most entertaining movies i've seen. tom cruise is himself, hayley atwell turns in an awesome performance as the fish out of water, and the action is still incredible.

the stunts were incredible in a vacuum - if the other mi movies hadn't existed, we'd all be blown away - but in the face of climbing the burj, racing choppers in a canyon, or hanging onto a plane as it takes off, these stunts were relatively muted.

it was cool to see ethan hunt function a little more as a member of a team than the solo acts he seems to have been forced into the last couple of movies.

the villain didn't top henry cavill's all-time performance in the last film, but he was very good, as were his henchmen and women.

overall, had a blast. highly recommend. just really, really turn your brain off.

dead reckoning isn't without flaws. with the stakes being ever higher, it also becomes harder to incorporate some levity into the movie. that is not to say there isn't some humor here and there, but it's less present than it used to be. and with the runtime being about half an hour longer than previous mi movies, the franchise just got a whole lot more serious, which won't be to everyone's taste. and the fact that this movie is doesn't get a proper ending (neither does it end with cliffhanger) won't help in making it more digestible for the less hardcore fans of the franchise.

but that's not to say that dead reckoning isn't one hell of a good movie. it's gripping, visually impressive, smart and innovative. tom cruise is still able to kick ass, and it seems he's still having as much of a good time that he had with the first movie nearly 20 years ago. he runs, ride motorcycle and jumps from high places, everything we're looking for in a mi movie. he knows what his audience wants and he's more than willing to give it to them, something that's getting rarer these days with hollywood movies...

just stepped out of the theater after watching mission: impossible 7, and i'm buzzing with excitement to share my thoughts on this action-packed spectacle! as a die-hard fan of the mi franchise, i was eagerly waiting to see what new thrills and jaw-dropping stunts tom cruise had in store for us this time.

right off the bat, i must say that mi 7 didn't disappoint in terms of story and engagement. the plot kept me on the edge of my seat throughout, and the addition of comedy scenes was a delightful surprise. the infusion of humor added a refreshing twist to the movie, making it a well-rounded package of action and entertainment.

however, i couldn't help but notice that the opening sequence and some of the fight scenes in the desert fell slightly short of my high expectations. don't get me wrong, tom cruise's dedication to performing his stunts is truly commendable. he's a true pioneer for ray-ban glasses, effortlessly making them an iconic fashion statement in every scene. his suave and charming persona combined with those stylish sunglasses has undoubtedly made him a darling for ladies worldwide.

speaking of action, i have to admit that mi 7 lacked some of the heart-pounding moments that have become synonymous with the mission: impossible series. while there were certainly intense sequences sprinkled throughout, i was hoping for even more adrenaline-pumping moments to get my heart racing.

but fear not, fellow fans! all is redeemed by the spectacular last train sequence. that scene was an absolute showstopper, the pinnacle of the film, and a true testament to the signature mi-style action we've all come to adore. the heart-stopping intensity and jaw-dropping stunts during that sequence were unparalleled, and it left me breathless.

now, let's talk about the cars! throughout the movie, we mainly saw alfa romeo and bmw in action. the choice of alfa romeo, being an italian brand, was a stroke of brilliance, adding a sense of authenticity and elegance, especially considering the movie's setting in italy. the alfa romeo's luxurious allure perfectly complemented the storyline, making it a fantastic addition to the movie's visuals.

one thing that has always impressed me about the mission: impossible series is its ability to evolve with the times. mi 7 didn't disappoint in this regard, incorporating cutting-edge technology-oriented scenes that left me fascinated. the face recognition for mapping faces and the use of augmented reality glasses were mind-blowing innovations that added an extra layer of intrigue and excitement to the movie. it's clear that the franchise knows how to stay ahead in the tech-driven world of espionage.

as we navigate through a sea of thrillers released each year, the mi franchise has to continually raise the bar to remain distinctive. while some action scenes may not have fully hit the mark, the innovative use of technology and the gripping storyline kept me invested and entertained.

now, let's take a moment to appreciate tom cruise's unwavering dedication. as i watched him perform those jaw-dropping stunts, i couldn't help but reflect on the passing years. by the time the next mi installment rolls around, tom cruise will be nearing 65 years of age. yet, i sincerely hope he continues to muster the same energy and passion to deliver stunts and scenes that elevate the mi franchise to greater heights with each release.

in conclusion, mission: impossible 7 served up a captivating mix of innovation, thrilling moments, and, of course, tom cruise's iconic presence. while some aspects could have been improved, the movie delivered on its promise to entertain and keep audiences on the edge of their seats. here's to hoping that the mi franchise continues to surprise and astound us with more action-packed adventures in the future!

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one, directed by christopher mcquarrie, who also helmed the previous two films, is a blockbuster you don't want to miss. it's the seventh instalment in the action-packed spy franchise that stars tom cruise as the fearless ethan hunt. this thrilling ride will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.

the plot is simple but effective: ethan and his imf team must track down a terrifying new weapon that threatens humanity before it falls into the wrong hands. the weapon is called "the entity", a rogue artificial intelligence that can manipulate information and control technology. the entity is everywhere and nowhere, and it has a mind of its own. ethan has to find the key that can unlock its secrets. the key is split into two pieces and hidden in different locations. along the way, he faces a mysterious and powerful enemy named gabriel (esai morales), who wants to use the entity for his own nefarious purposes. ethan also has to deal with his complicated relationship with ilsa faust (rebecca ferguson), who holds part of the puzzle and whose loyalties are unclear.

what makes this movie so exciting is not only the plot but also the execution. the action scenes are spectacular, with cruise doing most of his stunts as usual. there are car chases; motorcycle chases, helicopter chases, train fights, rooftop jumps, underwater escapes, and more. the locations are stunning, from rome to norway to dubai to london. the cinematography by fraser taggart is crisp and colourful, capturing the beauty and the danger of each setting. the score by lorne balfe is tense and dramatic, enhancing the mood and the suspense. the editing by eddie hamilton is fast and smooth, keeping the pace and rhythm of the story.

but what really makes this movie stand out is the acting and the characters. cruise is at his best as ethan hunt, showing his charisma, courage, vulnerability, and humanity. he makes us care about his mission and choices, even when they seem impossible. hayley atwell is a great addition to the cast as grace, with witty and fiery chemistry with cruise. she is a strong, smart character who challenges ethan and helps him. esai morales is a formidable villain as gabriel, who has a personal connection to ethan and a ruthless ambition. he is cold and menacing but also charismatic and intriguing. rebecca ferguson returns as ilsa faust, who has a complex and emotional bond with ethan. she is a fierce and loyal ally but also a potential threat. the rest of the cast is also excellent, with ving rhames, simon pegg, vanessa kirby, pom klementieff, and henry czerny reprising their roles from previous films.

the movie also explores some interesting themes and tones, such as the role of technology in our lives, the nature of truth and deception, the cost of loyalty and sacrifice, and the meaning of family and friendship. the movie sometimes has a dark and serious tone but balances it with humour and warmth. the dialogue is witty and clever, with memorable lines and jokes. the movie also pays homage to classic spy movies and references iconic moments from the franchise.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is one of the best movies of the year and one of the most exhilarating movies of a long time. it delivers everything you want from an action movie: thrilling stunts, stunning visuals, engaging characters, smart plot twists, and emotional stakes. it's a movie that will make you feel alive and entertained for 163 minutes (yes, it's long, but it doesn't feel like it). it's also a movie that will leave you wanting more (luckily, there's a sequel coming next year). so what are you waiting for? go see it now!

something is different here, it's not that high tech as the previous movies, it reminds me more of 007 flicks at moments. ethan is more vulnerable and tired, luther and benji are merely there, ilsa gone too soon. it also feels like an hommage to the first mi. the enemy is invisible but very dangerous, doomsday dangerous, skynet dangerous, gabriel is just an instrument and passes as a solid villain.

the action is as always fantastic, not too pretentious and exaggerated; i loved the falling train escape, made me bite my nails, car chases were also decent. all in all the movie misses that typical showing off which isn't bad at all, it was time for such a turn.

loved the movie but had some questions.

the head of national security said they stole the ai and then transmitted the source code via satellite to the russian sub. the reason they want to get to the sub is to get to an earlier version before it rebelled.

if they transmitted source code, how can the ai program run? unless they also sent a compiler that compiled the source code with the transmission?

other than, tom cruise delivers as usual.

the action sequences are insane.

how tom cruise can do even half of these stunts when he was in his 30s (much less in his mid 50s) is beyond comprehension.

so i dont really what happened with the previous movie; you can still see my review on it and i gave it a 4/10 because i really didnt get into it. but this movie was really different! from the beginning i thought it was a different movie in a good way. the plot is way more interesting and the number of the characters really make things really interesting even if we cant avoid the cliché of the big vilain with a tortured vision of the reality and power. the new character grace was a really deep character with an interesting development and the finished: she integrates the program with ethan and the others. to see again the white widow and how she get into the business once again. we have also some dilemma from ethan who needed to choose between ilsa and grace. i found the actions scenes way more interesting: the car chase ( i really laughed hard when ethan was in fiat and not with a luxury car as usual in that kind of movie), the jump to land on the train (some really funny moments). we couldnt avoid some "deus ex machina" when ethan land on the train at the right moment and at the right location to save grace: that kind of scene really ruined a little bit the mise en scene but it was not really that annoying. what else to say? i like also the fight scenes: way more dynamic and more interesting also in the plot( the fight when grace tried to avoid ethan). and didnt feel boring because there were tensions, challenges and some motivations from each characters. it really reminded me john wick 4 at some parts: i dont know if there were inspired of that movie. i love also the train sequence when everything fell apart and the comedy worked surprisely well (the trust that ethan asked from grace). it was a really great surprise for me! and i really enjoyed each part of the movie. a really worth watching movie and erase the mistakes of the previous movie at least for me. go watch it!

i'll start by saying that this is probably the best franchise in the history of cinema, as they achieved something that usually no other does: every new entry is better than the previous. unfortunately, i don't think this feat happened once again with dead reckoning pt. 1. that doesn't mean it's a bad movie by any means (far from it), but it does have it's flaws, and fallout was already a very hard film to top. it's the best action movie of the last ten or fifteen years. i'd put dr between ghost protocol and rogue nation.

starting with the plot, which i think was the weakest part. it's really not that creative, and to be honest i am not a fan of scary ai that is going to dominate the entire world. meh. they could have also gone for a bold ending for pt. 1, instead they went for the most obvious route: hunt securing both keys and going for the submarine.

now, regarding the cast, introducing hayley atwell was a major win. she's incredibly charismatic, and her chemistry with cruise was maybe the best of the franchise yet. losing ferguson but having her instead feels more than ok to me.

the villain was kind of disappointing, as he wasn't really scary nor was a imposing threat like the previous one.

on to the action sequences, i thought something was off about it. the only one that really impressed me, was the entire train act, which i'd say it was one of the best minutes out of any movie or show i have seen all year (john wick 4 still the king). besides that, none sticked out to me. i think this lacked a really good and exciting fight scene, like the bathroom one from fallout, for instance. that scene alone was like a statement of what's to come.

none from dr comes close to that one. there's a lot of action in this, but nothing really stellar or something they haven't done before. maybe the yellow fiat chase scene was creative, as they were handcuffed to themselves and the way they got away was fun, but the rest wasn't groundbreaking or anything.

it reads like i am disappointed, and i kind of am because i expected a little more, but i guess that says a lot about this franchise and the bar they have raised was too high for them to overcome themselves.

i really wish pt.2 will be the last entry and they can make a shorter, better movie with a tighter script.

so, the main thing is, i don't usually watch trailers lately, mostly just the teaser and the main trailer, but the problem is that the big moment of the movie is spoiled if you have a bit of deductive logic.

also, i feel like the producers, as in tom cruise, got greedy by pushing for a 2 part movie. this movie could have had some filler scenes cut and made into a 3 and a half hour motion picture. like this it feels too long. also, this strategy kinda blew up in their faces with a disastrous box office by launching at the same time as barbie and oppenheimer, which have destroyed everything.

also, another minor gripe i have is that watching agent carter with hailey atwell has engrained a certain archetype that she can play very well and as grace she felt a bit out of her comfort zone. i find it hard to believe she is this master thief when she kinda flusters in so many scenes. the moment she felt natural was in the final part of the movie. speaking of which, major props to vanessa kirby for making me feel like there are two characters with her same face. in my book, she is the standout for me.

otherwise, the movie is spectacular, very good action scenes, tom cruise is tom cruise, the actors are good, the story is captivating. it's a mi movie, for god's sake, you know what you're getting.

major spoiler time

the problem is that we know that ilsa will die the moment gabriel says that one of the 2 girls will die and grace appears in the trailers in the train chapter of the movie.

it kinda spoils everything and i just hate this thing people do with trailers lately. it absolutely cheapened the scene and felt like the screewriters just took me for an absolute idiot.

would have loved to be surprised.

as "mission impossible - dead reckoning part one" (2023 release; 163 min) opens, we are in "the bering sea" and a russian submarine moves about undetected--or is it? mayhem quickly ensues... we then go to "amsterdam", where ethan hunt receives his latest mission orders, "should you choose to accept it". at this point we are 10 min into the movie.

couple of comments: even though this is writer-director christopher mcquarrie's third film n the mi franchise, let's be clear: this is a tom cruise production from start to finish. it is absolutely amazing to me that the guy is now 61, with the energy and determination of someone 20-25 years younger than that. the movie goes big, and delivers big. the action scenes are out of this world, one better than the other. cruise's costars are also at the top of their game, including hayley atwell (as grace), rebecca ferguson (as ilsa), and vanessa kirby (as alanna), just to name those. it all leads to the hair-raising train ride at the end of the film. just watch. most amazing is that when the end credits start rolling, i couldn't hardly believe that 2 hrs. and 42 min had flown by just like that. this proves that the latest mission impossible is the gold standard of big hollywood action movies.

"mission impossible - dead reckoning part one" opened in us theaters this past weekend, and promptly underwhelmed at the box office, not even reaching $100 over its 5 day (wed to sun) opening release. wow, just wow. how to explain this lackluster box office performance? it's certainly not for a lack of critical acclaim. the movie is currently rated 96% certified fresh on rotten tomatoes, and for good reason. if you are a long-time fan of the mission essential franchise, of simply of great action movies in general, i'd readily suggest you check this out, and draw your own conclusion.

why oh why are we supposed to care about grace? and why do why are we to believe ethan hunt cares about her? why is she suddenly one of the most important people to him and right up there with ilsa, benji, and luther? terrible writing in this regard. to bring on a new character in this manner and expect any of us to find her their equal is insane. to top it off we lose a beloved character to save her. boo. she seemed to be the focus of the movie and we were just not fans of this. take her out and you have a great movie. edge of your seat as always. they are always great and something the whole family can enjoy together.

after seeing this film in cinemas twice here's my spoiler-free review of mission impossible: dead reckoning part one! as usual, i'll be talking about my thoughts, my favourite bits of watching it 2 times in a row and my conclusion/rating! tom cruise is fun to watch whether he's running, hanging or both! he's 61 years old now! more than that even injured his ankle doing the rooftop stunt in fallout & the most dangerous one he's done yet is the motorcycle mountain jump (which they filmed first). the cast members from the previous instalment are back; simon pegg's benji dunn, rebecca ferguson's ilsa faust, ving rhames' luther stickell (who's been present in all these films), vanessa kirby's alanna mitsopolis aka the white widow and a surprise return of henry czerny's eugene kittridge (who also reprised his role in lego dimensions). there are new characters introduced in the film like; hayley atwell's grace, pom klementieff's paris, shea whigham's jasper briggs (who's worked with hayley atwell before in marvel's agent carter) & esai morales' gabriel! the action scenes are cool and entertaining & the music is epic! i would watch mission impossible over bourne and bond cuz back in 2018 (when the last one was released) there was an article that states it has overtaken both those franchises! overall this is so much better than no time to die and i'm looking forward to the next one! that's why i'm giving this an 8/10! hopefully mission impossible: dead reckoning part two will make a billion dollars! ;-)

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a rollercoaster of espionage and adrenaline, and as a die-hard fan, i was ecstatic to join ethan hunt on his seventh mission. clocking in at a whopping 164 minutes, the film's length is palpable, but christopher mcquarrie keeps the pace swift with a blend of action and suspense, ensuring there's never a dull moment.

the introduction of an artificial intelligence villain is a bold move, tapping into the zeitgeist of ai in popular culture. however, the decision to reveal the antagonist early on doesn't quite pay off, missing an opportunity for a compelling narrative hook.

the globetrotting escapades, a trademark of mission: impossible, reach new heights, delivering breathtaking visuals and immersive locations. the returning cast seamlessly slips back into their roles, and newcomers like hayley atwell and pom klementieff inject fresh energy and unpredictability into the mix. the rogues' gallery feels reminiscent of john wick, adding a theatrical flair to the action set pieces.

while the stunts remain impressive, they didn't quite surpass my personal favorites from the franchise. nevertheless, tom cruise's commitment to practical stunts at his age is nothing short of awe-inspiring, infusing each moment with genuine tension.

dead reckoning part one introduces a more well-rounded approach, infusing humor into the high-stakes proceedings. as the first part of a two-part story, it strikes a balance between delivering a satisfying conclusion and setting up an enticing cliffhanger. while slightly less impactful as a standalone entry due to its cliffhanger nature, it leaves audiences eagerly anticipating the next thrilling installment.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning is the franchise's fourth genius-stroke in a row and my second favourite installment to date.

in many ways, it was always unfair to be the follow up to fallout, because it's the best - and at the same time so unlike the rest of the series. while motst of the m: i chapters are fun heist/caper actioners, fallout went all-in on an almost christopher nolan-esque "mythic homerian epic" approach that felt like a hyper self-serious departure from the franchise, an intimate character study. fallout might be the best espionage movie ever directed.

dead reckoning feels a little more in-line with what the rest of the series has felt like. dead reckoning brings back the awesome vibes of rogue nation, ghost protocol and brian depalma's original mission impossible. admittedly, though, after the sheer elegance and grace with which fallout flowed from scene to scene, dead reckoning does feel a little stilted by comparison. but that's it for as far my critic points go. were it not for fallout existing in the middle of this already masterful franchise, i think we'd all be saying dead reckoning is the best installment yet.

it's bigger than its predecessors in every way from the stunts to the scale to the stakes. tom cruise's commitment to his craft is unmatched and he absolutely delivers once again. likewise, christopher mcquarrie's direction is phenomenal and he deftly handles this absolutely massive blockbuster and delivers another feast for the eyes. hayley atwell is a fantastic new addition to the ensemble and she pairs so brilliantly with tom cruise. this film is an experience of pure cinematic genius made by people who know how to put the highest quality on canvas, thrilling and effortlessly entertaining. i mean, the way the fiat chase in rome and the train chase/crash in austria are directed is pure mastery of geography. the suspense, tonally-consistent comedy, setup/payoff, and constant surprise is remarkable.

it would have been easy for mcquarrie and cruise to follow up fallout with something that felt like more of the same but weaker, à la the dark knight rises. but dead reckoning instead feels like an entirely new creature all its own. i respect that choice deeply. yes dead reckoning part one is essentially only the first half of the story, and some table-setting work is done, but the movie still feels very contained by closing up the arc it started and it leaves you with a satisfying feeling, while wanting more. this is why i watched the movie two days in a row. simply perfect entertainment.

if m: i 8 manages to retain the same flavor while also adding new aspects, we're going to end up with a never before seen duology that stands apart from the rest of the series in both quality and voice.

the gold standard of hollywood, as tom cruise himself denoted his crew on the set of the film.

it is a shame that this masterful production-endeavour underperformed at the box office (thanks to bad release strategy by paramount and an earth-shattering run from barbenheimer). i can only hope that mission impossible 8 gets the time to thrive in theaters it deserves. i for myself cannot wait to experience what mr. cruise and mcquarrie have still in store for us.

let me preface myself by saying that this was my first mission impossible film i had seen. and i had originally seen it in theaters on july 23rd am posting my review from then.

since my knowledge was limited on the whole series as it was my first film, but this film has inaugurated me into the franchise for life. its everything an action should be. its fun, funny, serious, and knows when to laugh at itself.

despite the many flashbacks and throwbacks to previous film in the franchise, i think anyone could watch this film and be thoroughly entertained.

its a bit overtop at times, but fight scenes, chase scenes, and cinematography make the film just a spectacular film to watch especially in a theater. you win tom cruise. i'm hooked.

the film started off great with a polished submarine opening and ethan finding his way back to imf, but apart from a few other standout scenes this one feels emptier than the great films that came before it.

one of the biggest issues is that the latest mi felt like it was working to check off all the boxes on a running list of espionage/thriller tropes while also intentionally or unintentionally borrowing many iconic things from the james bond films. goldeneye, the world is not enough, for your eyes only, spectre, the spy who loved me, from russia with love, and quantum of solace were all very noticeable influences on much of the film, between gadgets, plot devices, yellow buggy getaway vehicles, and even classic bond film quotes. not sure what happened there since the previous mi films were all wonderfully unique in their own way and didn't borrow from anything but themselves.

another major issue was the script. the dialogue wasn't very genuine, especially between our favorite imf team members, and mainly every word spoken had something to do with "go! run! the key! where's the key? move! hurry!" that's fine for any run of the mill action flick, but fans have come to expect better from such an amazing franchise. the story is also messy and adds some new points that feel like last minute additions to a two part ending for tom cruise's ethan hunt.

looking past those issues, it really is a fun movie with some incredible moments. had the development team shaved off 45 minutes, added that unique spark like they had with prior films, and put together an edge of your seat story that had filmgoers off the charts excited for the finale, this could easily have been a 9.5/10. well deserving of an 8 however for being an ideal summer blockbuster film that doesn't strive to change the formula very much.

another excellent instalment of the mission impossible franchise.

i just about got this to an 8/10 and was just a tad off the level of fallout in my view, however with it being two parts we're only halfway through.

esai morales is a great addition to the franchise cast as gabriel and certainly fills the void left by solomon lane, who i thought made a great deranged villain across rogue nation and fallout. hayley atwell as grace i found a little nauseating in the early scenes constantly giving ethan the slip, but i acknowledge that's just me and my personal preference!

it's got the glamour and opulence from the global destinations on show, pulsating action scenes and the comic touches at inappropriate moments that we've come to expect from mission impossible, and i'll certainly be anticipating the second part hitting the big screen.

mission impossible - dead reckoning - part i is the seventh installment of one the most well-conceived, consistent and loved action franchises. the work done in the last years with "ghost protocol", "rogue nation" and "fallout" is remarkable, and "dead reckoning" fits perfectly in this virtuous path, giving the fans a spectacular and very entertaining movie.

the prologue sets up the story very well and presents ethan hunt's mission to recover two halves of a key capable, when together, to unlock unknown and world-changing powers for their owners. at the same time, although being a part i, the movie has a very good ending and is somehow complete even if the story continues in part ii. this is not obvious at all: we have many examples of annoying "to be completed" cuts placed somewhere without a meaningful closure of the movie (matrix reloaded is an example). dead reckoning does not do that mistake at all.

for the first time in the franchise, ethan and his team are confronted not only with a human villain (gabriel), but also with fully digital one. the basic concept of the digital forces / machines gaining self-consciousness and taking over the control has been vastly explored in literature as well as in cinematography. nevertheless, what is quite original and interesting here is that the movie explores the events possibly leading to that dystopian reality where machines are in control, and the fight to prevent that from happening, rather than to take down an already established technological power.

the plot is solid and well thought out. the story gets complicated in the understanding of the roles, double roles, changing sides, tricks, and objectives of the different characters rather than in the overall idea and logic, described above. it builds a solid framework for the action sequences, which all the mi fans are looking forward to. these are very exciting and brilliantly made, and tom cruise does exceptionally in these. there is no mission impossible without chases and the ones of dead reckoning part i through the tiny streets of rome really deliver! there is so much tension and fun, and the little moments of humor just make everything even better.

in different scenes, for example the venice and the train sequence, the movie makes you think of the first mission impossible, and there is nothing wrong with that. kettridge is also brought back from the first installment. compared to previous installments, though, i think that the action is lacking some of the sneakiness which is typical of the imf missions: penetrating some kind of impenetrable maximum security building or area without anybody to notice (at least until something goes haywire) is a typical example. too little of that happens in dead reckoning: too much of the action is loud and messy from the start, or from too soon.

being this movie a part i, it does a good job in setting up the story with moments of exposition. nevertheless, i do think there's a bit too many of these moments, so that too much is explained, sometimes in a kind of repetitive / business meeting way. some of these breaks from the action could have been used for a deeper exploration of the characters, for example. one of the themes of the movie, even if not really new in the mi legacy, is that this mission is going to involve and put in danger the people ethan cares the most about. "ethan, this mission is gonna cost you...dearly" (kettridge). spending a bit more time on the characters and on ethan's relationship with them would have made this theme more original and real: we could have seen how much ethan cares about his friends, instead of just knowing it, we could have connected a bit more on an emotional level with the things at stake.

one last note. i have watched this movie one week after having watched the fifth indiana jones (dial of destiny) and i was surprised by the amount of similarities: both plots revolve around finding two pieces of an object that must not fall in the wrong hands, since it gives access to unimaginable power. one of the fights, on top of a moving train, looks very very similar. both indy and ethan end up driving an italian vintage car, in italy...what happened there? is it just a coincidence or were the studios talking to each other? independently of the answer, i don't think there is one single thing that indy 5 does better than dead reckoning.
