tom cruise is a guy who for the last 40 years has surrounded himself with good writers and directors. robert towne, martin scorsese, steven spielberg, robert redford, neil jordan and many more.

in that time he has learned what it takes to deliver a good product. cruise is not here to pick up a big pay cheque. he is involved in all aspects of productions.

in a summer where action films have disappointed, you can sense that a lot of thought was behind each scene in dead reckoning part one.

jettisoning the different director approach. christopher mcquarrie returns for the third time. he even takes time out to mimic other franchises, the fiat car chase is very much james bond from: for your eyes only. then there are call backs to mission impossible's own 27 years movie history. the train sequence was a call back to brian de palma's original.

the mcguffin is a cruciform key which is in two parts. possession of both parts with give the nation owning it untold powers. however there is a rogue ai system called the entity.

it has brought in a man called gabriel (esai morales) to retrieve the cruciform key. gabriel is an old enemy of ethan hawke (tom cruise.)

using the bond formula of globetrotting around the world. big action sequences and breathtaking stunts. this is a solid exciting movie. partly overlong but cruise and mcquarrie show that you can mix familiar ingredients and still come up with something new.

this is the seventh in the mission: impossible series featuring the escapades of ethan hunt, played by tom, the leader of the imf force-impossible missions force-that tries to keep the world safe. in this installment, everyone is after two keys that when assembled together, can gain control of a powerful ai-artificial intelligence-that can be used to control all electronics in the world. hayley plays a thief that works with tom and his team to accomplish their mission. esai is the main bad guy that also has connections to tom's past and pom is esai's chief enforcer. everyone is after the keys and tom, so there are plenty of car chases and fight sequences and of course, fantastic stunts. the car chase in rome and the train scenes are some of the most thrilling to see and if you noticed in the title, this is part one with the second part coming next year-theoretically, if there are no delays.

it's rated pg-13 for violence, action and language and has a running time of 2 hours & 43 minutes.

i really enjoyed it and would buy it on blu_ray.

ethan(peak cruise) and his team have to stop a dangerous threat to the world.

this delivers most of what we want from a mission impossible movie. action and tension are built around stunts and showing how much of it is real, not handled largely by special effects that don't obey the laws of physics filmed in a way that obscures how little of it was done by the actors themselves. there's a great variety, with some real standout fights and chases. venice and the train will blow you away.

this definitely does do a lot of telling not showing though there is a reason for it. a major theme is whether or not hunt is able to protect the people he cares about, frustratingly this involves making certain female characters mostly serve as motivation for him, not allowed to be full people in their own right.

the movie follows ethan hunt (tom cruise) and his imf team as they race against time to track down a dangerous weapon before it falls into the wrong hands. the movie is packed with breathtaking action sequences, including a high-speed chase through the streets of paris and a thrilling fight scene atop a moving train.

the film's plot involves hunt and his team trying to stop a mysterious villain from starting a world war. the villain is played by henry cavill, and he is suitably menacing. the supporting cast is also excellent, with ving rhames, simon pegg, rebecca ferguson, and vanessa kirby all giving solid performances.

over the past 10-15 years, the "mission impossible" franchise has eclipsed james bond in popcorn movie-going fun. while "dead reckoning part 1" may not represent the tippy-top of recent m:i heights, it is certainly an entertaining, rip-roaring adventure best enjoyed from a theater seat!

for a very basic overview, "dead reckoning 1" sees ethan hunt (tom cruise) accepting another mission--this time to retrieve a key that unlocks a sentient ai which threatens the world's digital infrastructure. along the way, he meets up with old friends benji (simon pegg), luther (ving thames), & ilsa (rebecca ferguson) while making a new acquaintance in thief grace (hayley atwell). all the while, he is pursued by various factions--such as the mysterious gabriel (esai morales) & federal agent briggs (shea whigham)--who also want to get their hands on the key.

like i said, the m:i films are now the standard for action stunts and adventure filmmaking (perhaps even more so with harrison ford's indiana jones having recently rode into the sunset for the final time), and "dead reckoning 1" never fails to deliver on that front. cruise continues to dream up the wildest sequences possible and do them as practically (little cgi) as his body will allow, while director christopher mcquarrie cooks up a smorgasbord of adventure set pieces one practically right after another. if you don't see "dead reckoning 1" in imax, dolby atmos, or at very least a standard theater seat, you are doing yourself a great injustice and missing much of the film's pizzazz.

it helps that cruise hasn't lost an ounce of the humor and charm that has now christened him "hollywood savior". he runs and wisecracks his way through the whole movie, surrounded by the impressive cast this franchise has now cultivated. especially standing out is vanessa kirby's "white widow" character--the flick especially shines when she is heavily in the mix.

all that said, i think i enjoyed this movie's immediate predecessors--rogue nation & fallout--a tiche more than this one. why? two reasons: first, i'm not sure if the grace character was strong enough to banter about with hunt for almost the film's entirety. nothing against atwell's portrayal either--but this character can't hold a candle to the heroines of previous installments. secondly, the "sentient ai" plot line was a macguffin of the highest order (only serving to kick off the next action/adventure sequence). i know that all m:i films essentially function this way, but it felt a bit more forced here. perhaps this film's conclusion will better handle that central plot.

overall, though, i very much enjoyed "dead reckoning 1" for what it largely purports to be: the height of "popcorn entertainment" that draws people out of their homes and into the theater for the communal movie-watching experience.

tom cruise reprises his iconic role as the relentless spy, ethan hunt, in the latest instalment of the mission: impossible series. in this adrenaline-fueled adventure, hunt embarks on a high-stakes mission to retrieve the cruciform key.

this key is the only way of unlocking the source code of the rogue ai.

from the beginning, the film grabs viewers' attention and catapults them into a whirlwind of action and thrilling moments.

the fast-paced storyline leaves audiences on the edge of their seats as hunt confronts danger at every turn to save the world from the entity, an enigmatic artificial intelligence.

one of the standout moments in the film comes when cruise takes on one of his most daring stunts yet, riding a motorcycle off a cliff. it's a heart-pounding sequence that showcases cruise's dedication to delivering jaw-dropping action on screen. it's a true testament to the intensity and thrill that the mission: impossible franchise is known for.

beneath the exhilarating action sequences, the film also delves into the moral complexities of the technological age, raising thought-provoking questions about the potential risks and ethical dilemmas surrounding artificial intelligence. this exploration adds an additional layer of depth to the thrilling narrative, allowing audiences to reflect on the delicate balance between progress and the preservation of humanity.

cruise once again proves why he is the face of this successful franchise, effortlessly embodying the character of ethan hunt. his charismatic performance elevates the character to new heights, solidifying his status as one of the most iconic action heroes of our time.

the supporting cast, including hayley atwell as a new addition, delivers strong performances that complement cruise's dynamic portrayal. their chemistry and interactions inject further depth into the story, keeping viewers fully engaged and invested in the outcome.

overall, mission: impossible deftly blends heart-pounding action with captivating intrigue, making it a must-watch for fans of the series and lovers of adrenaline-fueled films. from the jaw-dropping stunts to the thought-provoking themes, this latest instalment proves once again why the franchise continues to be a staple in the action genre. buckle up, hold on tight, and prepare yourself for a thrilling ride filled with adventure, excitement, and non-stop action.

the mission: impossible films are blockbusters at their purest. they have groundbreaking action and witty humour, a phenomenal movie star performing the most insane stunts, some super badass women for him to court, they come out every six years and then we all completely forget about them. but with every new instalment, we're reminded of how much we should be loving them.

these days, they seem to treat films like products. sequels and reboots are dominating our screens, beloved spider-mans and star wars, banking on the brand rather than the art. but in this algorithmic industry, reckoning - part 1 reminds us that the art of film still exists, even in an overworked franchise. from the fantastic introduction of tom cruse's ethan hunt to the big finale on the orient express, there is story and production value on par with other cruse lead sequel, top gun: maverick (2022).

this film once again takes the stakes to new heights and not just with its brand new action set pieces. the franchise began as a 007-inspired spy thriller with mask-wearing agents. as they went on, they became more stunt oriented. while action has always been the highlight of the films, it's the political espionage sequences that are a big part of what spy thrillers are, going back to their roots.

the team of ethan, luther (ving rhames), benji (simon pegg) and ilsa (rebecca ferguson) are back and better than ever. hayley atwell (captain america) debts as a charming thief and pom klementieff (guardians of the galaxy) literally kills it as a silent but deadly assassin. henry czerny also makes his welcome return to the franchise since the first film.

reckoning - part 1 brings the political intrigue back to the forefront as the team use their sneaky spy tactics to bring down an all-knowing ai that has the power to seize control of all human knowledge. as over exaggerated as it is, it does makes sense that they would use something like a nihilistic computer for a macguffin. the film is called mission impossible after all. they manage to ground it quite well too. it adds to the unseen element the spy movies have, but in this case, the villain is literally faceless.

the film creates a sense of dread and mystery that makes spy films so engaging. a false sense of security, the feeling of something unknown scheming in the shadows waiting to strike. there's a reality to spy films that if they slip up just once, it will mean total disaster. they're basically horror films without the "horror". director christopher mcquarrie (jack reacher) uses these similarities well. the fact that they have masks so realistic, that someone you really love could be someone else entirely is chilling in itself. they acknowledge this with czerny and cary elwes (the princess bride) hilariously pulling and touching people's faces in public.

the series traditionally has the 61-year old cruse perform a signature stunt so outrageous, that it definitely earns the title impossible. this time, it's driving off an actual cliff on a motorcycle into a moving train. and that's only the beginning of the climax! characters are at their best when put into situations that no human would want to be put in and this is a movie about people whose job it is to do that. keeping with the thriller style, the scenes are all shot and acted in a way that invokes horror. the alley fight and the cliff jump are specifically stressful.

compared to most blockbuster franchises, this film is reliant on cgi effects while still going large scale. mcquarrie's direction insures cgi is used only if necessary and everything that can be done practically is done so. what you get is a tense, heart-stopping sequence stripped of all plot armour. there's no "nuking the fridge" here. despite their superhuman acts, they're still mortal, and their job comes with monumental risks. you can almost say that in a way, ethan hunt is the fictional personification of cruse himself.

finally, most "2-parter" movies just stop in the middle of the story with no real resolution. this film actually feels complete. it resolves the arcs it sets up while setting up the events of the next film making for a much more satisfying experience when the cliffhanger hits.

as a continuation of mission impossible: fallout (2018), reckoning: part 1 repeats the perfect combo that made it great. the film once again combines spy-film beats and the stunt-mastery of john wick: chapter 4 (2023), while remembering its beginnings as a cheesy super-spy show.

cruse and mcquarrie have truly spared no expense.

least some things don't change !!! for the last almost 30 years this particular franchise and tom cruise himself , continuously and without fail ,proceeded to awe and entertain us ! that is a very rare thing , in this days of falling filmmaking standards , which makes it . in my humble opinion , a very rare gem of a films. definitely , some of them are better than others , but none of them had fallen below certain high level of public expectations . always complicated but interesting story , good acting , crazily incredulous action and stunts ,all in all definitely one of the few modern films , which i will re watch !

i watched this film sooner that i ordinarily would have based on a clip i viewed of how the filmmakers and tom cruise prepared for that spectacular motorcycle jump ending with cruise crashing into the alpine train. that, and virtually every other stunt in the film required exquisite preparation and timing, so much so that the odds of anything like that happening for real would be less than getting struck by lightning twice in the same day. nevertheless, for die-hard action junkies and tom cruise fans, this is a must-see film in the franchise, as it never fails to deliver an adrenaline rush. somehow though, the plot of the story is left behind somewhat, as the opening sequence reveals a determined rogue ai destroying a stealth russian submarine, which will obviously figure in part two. oddly, i've only ever seen the original "mission impossible" with tom cruise and none of the sequels, before i ever started writing these reviews, so i'm tempted to go back and check them all out in due time. as for this story line, i'm still not convinced the cruciform key at the center of the story has been satisfactorily retrieved. with all the pick-pocketing and put-pocketing going on, i think there's probably room for the screenwriters to pull another fast one before we get to the stunning conclusion. with more death defying, impossible stunts for sure!

the mission: impossible franchise has been one of the most consistently entertaining and solid action franchises in cinema, and dead reckoning part 1 continues this trend with a very entertaining action packed instalment.

the story follows cruise's ethan hunt, as he races to stop control of a malicious ai falling into the wrong hands. this isn't exactly a reinvention of the wheel in terms of these kinds of stories, but the ai element feels very relevant and interesting and adds some very real stakes to the whole piece.

one of the reasons the story works so well is the brilliant collection of characters who you actually care about. all of the franchise favourites are here, with some meaty roles for ving rhames and simon pegg, and tom cruise is of course as charismatic as ever. but really it is the women who stand out in this film.

pom klementieff is a great addition, and rebecca ferguson and vanessa kirby shine. the highlight however is hayley atwell, who storms onto the scene with one of the best characters in the entire mission: impossible franchise. her performance is so magnetic and the character so fun and intriguing. she really is the star of this film.

mission impossible has always set the bar high for stunts, and dead reckoning delivers. it has exhilarating car chases, a very cleverly worked and inventive train sequence, and of course that famous motorcycle stunt, as well as many more. it certainly doesn't disappoint on this front.

if you love mission: impossible films, if you love action, if you love fast paced and energetic blockbusters that blend bombastic set pieces with developed characters and real stakes, then mission: impossible dead reckoning will give you everything you want and more.

the mission impossible movies since ghost protocol have slowly become some of the best modern-day action movies. tom cruise never fails to deliver on excellent action sequences with each movie trying to outdo the prior one. in addition, the plot and characters have been increasingly been getting better, with fallout being the best combination of tight plot, engaging characters and spectacular action. does this film live up to its predecessors? yes, almost.

dead reckoning part 1 contains all what one would expect with a mission impossible film. the greatest praise i can give this film is that once again, the action is fantastic. while nothing tops fallout's peak action sequences, the action in this film is leagues beyond any other modern action movies out there. tom cruise's commitment is non-stop and he knows what the audience wants. however, some moments in the action do feel too convenient and some moments seem almost nonsensical which was never a problem in its predecessors. it also feels like the film is saving its very best action for part 2 which leaves this film unable to truly stand out from its predecessors.

yet, what sets this film apart from its predecessors is the plot. the overarching antagonist of the film is unique and new for the series and it is appropriately built-up leaving the stakes the highest that they have ever been. if you pick apart the plot, there are holes and moments where characters simply appear which is somewhat disappointing since the previous films had tight plot, but this doesn't break the film.

the characters are fine with the standout being hayley atwell's grace who is an excellent new addition to the film who knows what she excels at yet is out of her depth in the world of spies and espionage but she is well-developed into well-rounded characters. the side characters are fine. there are one too many and some could've been cut to give time to series favourites like ilsa and benji. ethan is given good development and cruise continues to deliver with his performance. the main antagonist is interesting with a rough attempt at connecting him to ethan. i will reserve judgement on him since he will likely be more developed in part 2.

overall, dead reckoning part 1 is a great action movie that doesn't quite reach the heights of rogue nation or fallout. it still contains breath-taking action sequences and delivers on all the stuff fans love about mission impossible. i am hoping part 2 corrects the small shortcomings of part 1 but i still highly recommend this movie for any fan of action.

the film is one of the most expensive for what it delivers and the reason is because it was filmed during the covid times. that may had affected plot lines, scenes, quality of the acting or of the directing, removed budget from special effects and stunts, but it did not. so you get a three hour part one of something that is non stop action and stunt work and pretty decent acting. there are even some interesting emotional scenes where everybody delivered their best.

the problem is with the plot, the incredibly dumb mcguffin they are all chasing, the villain from ethan's past, the inconsistent logical holes, the camera magic with which each character appears in the scene at the exact moment needed, even if they had no way of getting there, each stage built upon a series of coincidences that are so far fetched that it becomes grating after a while.

and i don't really blame the writers, they had to top the last top, make everything bigger, louder, fancier. if the previous stories made little sense and were all like that, how could they possibly revert to some semblance of common sense? but it's the destiny of all american franchises that follow this pattern to reach a level beyond which nothing can be done. ethan in space? ethan time travelling? ethan fighting aliens? ethan becoming god? where can it possibly go?

bottom line is that every moment was good, tense, emotionally charged - i even had to pause the movie to vent some of the frustration, but the fact that most of the things don't make any sense almost cancelled the good work put in the film. a well done movie, but going nowhere.

over the last few years, the mission impossible films have been some of the best action films in cinema. now the 7th film in the franchise dead reckoning part one has been released and i watched it yesterday, here is my review for it. the premise of the film sees ethan hunt and his team have to track down a device that could cause world war 3.

main character tom cruise is back as ethan hunt and he continues his career renaissance with a fantastic performance here. even though the man is 60 years old, he is brilliant in all the action sequences and there is no inkling that he has any plans on slowing down. his character has also developed really well, you see how the previous films have affected him and it is cool seeing his view on being a member of imf.

supporting characters hayley atwell is new to the franchise and plays grace. she is an exciting supporting character and has a really good dynamic with cruise, it is a major part of the film and i liked how her character was used here as it really felt different to other female characters in this franchise.

ving rhames & simon pegg are back in their roles as luther and benji and they are both great. this has been a great team together over the last few films and they continue to be a fun duo in this film too. luther ends up having a larger role then i expected and that was a nice surprise for sure.

esai morales plays the villain gabriel and i really liked his portrayal. he is physically an equal to ethan hunt but he also plays the psychological game and it makes him stand out. his motivations are a little blurry but morales has the chemistry to make it work.

vanessa kirby & pom klementieff do really good jobs in their roles and i thought they were enjoyable to watch depsite not being an integral part of the plot.

the one character they do treat a bit poorly is ilsa faust played by rebecca ferguson. she was a major part of the previous 2 films but feels underutilised here, she is just a background character and unfortunately gets no development which is a bit of a let down.

story the story is alright. i liked how it showed how much technology has become a part of our everyday life and once it stops working or even works against us it can really affect people. also the story of ethan hunt as a character is pretty well written and actually shows some development. but it also feels very much like a part one, in terms that everything feels like build up for the next film, i mean its fun but definitely build up. also there are certain story elements that aren't really explored or explained and it makes things a bit uninspired and generic.

script the script is pretty well written. the film is pretty serious and that is conveyed well by the actors and the writers. there are dribbles of humour in there and when used appropriately they certainly gave a chuckle and i am glad it doesn't overuse this.

style the film looks fantastic and there are some awesome action sequences. the film travels all over the world and it is really cool seeing these different locations and these sequences used in these environments. knowing cruise does his own stunts makes it even more crazy considering some of the stuff that is done in this film. though i did feel like this film was a little long, it could have shaved 15 mins off and would have been a better film for sure.

overall overall, mission impossible - dead reckoning part one is a great film that continues the really good work that the franchise has been doing. it isn't perfect but certainly has me excited for the 2nd part of this film and see if it really hits the spot.

rating - 8/10.

this is the best mission impossible movie to date. the action is incredible and as always tom cruise goes above and beyond to entertain the audience. i also love how this movie shows how threatening and dangerous ai can be. and instead of making a huge evil robot it plays mind games with our heroes as a part of its algorithm. i thought that was genius. i was said to see ilsa die but i thought it served the story very well. the movie does a great job diving deeper into ethan's character and we get to see more of what drives him. the set design and costumes are excellent and the music is solid. all of the jokes they went for were actually really funny. overall this is an incredible action film. tom cruise and director christopher mcquarrie are keeping up the momentum after top gun maverick. (9/10)

the seventh entry in the venerable series currently in theaters. tom cruise is back as ethan hunt & this time he's after the proliferation of a potent ai entity who has a human protector, played by esai morales, out to procure a set of interlocking keys, one of which is being ferried by a career thief, played by agent carter's hayley atwell, who cruise intercepts at a busy airport. w/cruise's usual team (ving rhames, simon pegg & returning rebecca ferguson) on the ready, the race is on through various locales w/a stunning clincher on the orient express w/much of the action done for real (as per the mandate through most of the series) & the scenario/direction (oscar winner christopher mcquarrie returning for a third time, make that fourth since part 2 will be out next year) cracker jack smart makes this continuing series a good alternative to whenever the bond series finally rears its head. co-starring retiring mantis (maybe?) pom klementieff as morales' henchperson, shea whigham as an imf field operative out to nab cruise, cary elwes as a cia officer, vanessa kirby reprising her villainess role from the last adventure & returning to the franchise since 1996 henry czerny as cruise's boss.

tom cruise and mission impossible is back, this entry; dead reckoning - part 1.

i've been a fan of these films since i was a young lad, and i'm pleased to say this is a fantastic entry to the series.

car chases, hand to hand combat, gun battles, death defying stunts and small amounts of well timed humour, all surrounding a storyline which whilst doesn't take its self too seriously, still manages to maintain an incredibly amount of suspense.

tom cruise truly is the last big movie star, and by this point, knows exactly what we want from a hollywood blockbuster. the pacing in particular, was almost non stop suspense with drippings of character and plot building.

it's a near perfect movie - sure it's a little farfetched (but who watches these for the realism) and i did spot a few moments of bad cgi (the train scene particular) but this is the perfect saturday night movie. definitely worth seeing in the theatres, so what are you waiting for?!

tom cruise returns to the big screen with the 7th installment of mission impossible franchise with top-notch action and stunts. this movie is a treat for all the action-lovers out there. it's hard to believe that almost all the stunts are performed by the actors themselves and minimal cgi is used.

it manages to feel fresh and new considering the number of movies that have been made in the same genre. i am amazed by how the stakes keep getting higher and higher with each installment to the franchise. the only thing i didn't like about this movie is there were so many sub-plots going on that sometimes you are not able to catch up with some parts of the movie.

conclusion: go watch this movie on the biggest screen possible.

mission: impossible- dead reckoning part one

this might be the only mission impossible film to end with the audience still not knowing wether the mission was indeed possible or not 🤔

mission impossible dead reckoning part one is the seventh instalment in the tom cruise driven spy thriller franchise.

this film and john wick chapter 4 are from what i know of the two biggest action films to have come out this year and therefore it's hard for me not to compare them especially since it's difficult to dive too deep into the plot of this film without spoilers. that being said in typical mission impossible style the plot of this film revolves around ethan hunt and his team agreeing to a mission where by they must track down a key that in some way relates to a rogue ai called the entity which if someone could control would essentially lead to them having total world domination. ethan and his team are therefore sent to stop the key falling into the wrong hands or are they?

straight away the plot is more complex and feels more realistic than john wick 4 despite being seven films in compared to john wicks 4 the core plot of the mission impossible films are always grounded in reality. the idea that an ai rogue with the power to give someone or a group of people absolute power is frightening and at times a bit too real as it's something you could definitely imagine happening in real life.

as a result of this plot and also unlike john wick 4 the film keeps you guessing as to who's on which side which keeps you guessing as to how each brilliantly executed scene may play out.

that being said however i did find the action to not be as enjoyable as both john wick chapter 4 or a couple of the other mission impossible films for that matter. the film gradually gets more over the top but luckily ends just in the nick of time and stops itself going into the unbelievable.

i also felt the big bike/parachute stunt which has been hyped up in the marketing wasn't as interesting to watch in the film as it was to watch the bts of on youtube.

all this considered it's not my favourite mission impossible (probably 3rd/4th favourite) but it's still a lot of fun and definitely one to watch on the big screen.

just as warning in case you were planning to take your friend dracula, he won't enjoy this film.

the stakes are too high.

rating: 8/10 roll on part 2.

when fallout released i thought that this is the franchise's best and it would be difficult to match something like this, but with "dead reckoning" one could confidently say that there is always scope for improvement. keeping audience at the edge for almost 3 hours is no small feat, an art which i believed only the likes of james cameron or steven spielberg have mastered until now.

i watched this with usual expectation that we all expect from tom and christopher mcquarrie. it's a well balanced film that shows each characters in other dimensions. it's one of those films really hard to explain in words it must be watched in cinemas. what makes this stand out from other mi films is this one does not have a defined villain that ethan hunt is fighting. it's more of a back story to the final installment (perhaps). the best part of this mi7 is that - all the support character are big part of the film. meaning each characters are carrying the storyline in many ways. it's not a ethan film... everyone plays well defined rolls.. and for a mi film very funny indeed.

tom cruise is just super terrific at the job at his age and acting-wise he again brings his never-ending charisma to the screen and that's for viewers' utmost pleasure, though i really missed his awesome trademark smile, which was a huge miss in the movie.

second in acting that i loved and was quite surprised by was hayley atwell's whose beauty, lean sportive figure and onscreen charisma added a marvelous touch to the duo and tandem. kudos hayley, you're better, more beautiful and wiser than agent carter (2015) and that's an achievement by itself.

the movie a little fizzled out by the end, and especially on the train, though the motorcycle, jump and "entering" the train sequences were out of this world, superbly done though logically faulted. entering by the side windows while jumping toward the train and on its main course was quite a magic trick and after that both of them should have been stuck to the car (wagon)'s inner wall like an omelette! , but never mind, i will dearly and engagingly close my eyes on those.

as one or many users pointed out, a superb movie, and that's just part one of it. cannot wait for its refreshing and surly superb (as ever) part two in over a year.

my favorite mission: impossible movies are mission: impossible (1996), mission: impossible-ghost protocol (2011), mission: impossible-rogue nation (2015), and mission: impossible-fallout (2018); while mission: impossible 2 (2000) was not that good, and mission: impossible 3 (2006) was good enough. the new movie mission: impossible-dead reckoning part one (2023) was a great part one to the finale of the franchise that was very suspenseful with tom cruise once again being incredible.

tom cruise as ethan hunt along with ving rhames as luther, and simon pegg as benji who are all great together as a team; the return of rebecca ferguson as ilsa was also particularly good, but she needed to be in the movie more. newcomer hayley atwell as grace was fantastic joining ethan hunt on his mission, and she has a past involving being a thief of sorts, while knowing things on the main threat involving an intelligent ai. ethan hunt has a past with someone named gabriel that is part of the plot i will not spoil, but will say the actor who plays him, esai morales, did an excellent job as this character who felt mysterious in a way.

gabriel played by esai morales is really the main antagonist other than the evil ai in the movie; everyone is after two parts of a key that they do not know what it is for, but they know it can cause harm to the world. i liked pom klementieff's character named paris who was a cool assassin who did not speak most of the time, but when she does it is in a different language, and the return of kittridge played by henry czerny who was in the very first movie. this movie does have callbacks to the first mission: impossible movie directed by brian de palma with the cinematography having close ups on people, or a certain action sequence involving a train.

the action sequences are fantastic, that is what to be expected coming from a mission: impossible movie; they are nicely shot, fast paced, and suspenseful. tom cruise pulling these stunts brilliantly, along with the other actors being great in fight sequences or chase sequences in exciting entertaining ways. i liked the plot involving an intelligent ai that is called "the entity," and that people are looking for a key related to it, but they do not know what it unlocks or why it is so important.

mission: impossible-dead reckoning part one (2023) is a fantastic part one to the finale that leaves you with a satisfying cliffhanger and it will make you excited for part two. great acting, amazing stunts, some funny moments, fun action scenes involving fight scenes or chase scenes, and an interesting plot. after watching this, i wanted to watch it again, but also, i am now excited for part two.

dead reckoning is another milestone for action movies and for the mission impossible franchise but unlike fallout or rogue nation, there isn't the right blend of realism and fiction which makes it almost flawless but not perfect nonetheless.

the movie begins in a russian submarine and whatever happens inside it puts the map for the next two parts of the franchise. there are many tributes given to the first mission impossible movie but the mask trick seems to be over done here almost bordering to the point of convenience. unlike the other parts, most of the story happens in just 3 or 4 places in the entire movie. the action set pieces are without a doubt a phenomenal achievement and a landmark for action movies.

tom cruise without saying continues to prove why he is the last superstar to exist today and sets boundaries for action movies in the future which most probably won't be touched in our lifetimes. the best part of the mission impossible movies is that, the humour is genuine and doesn't relate on endless pop culture references and trends.

a major character dying in the 2nd act of the movie was rather a bold choice which most blockbuster franchises should be doing. coming to the soundtrack, lorne balfe's same score is used in pretty much all scenes, this is where ludwig goransson would have shined.

the movie ends of a mini cliffhanger and the 2nd part has a big responsibility to conclude the saga and produce the same standard of goosebumps inducing set pieces to keep the crowd elevated. i'm confident christopher macquarie and tom cruise won't miss.

the mi franchise has proven to be really entertaining and generally very well crafted. ghost protocol was like a fresh and great start of what has followed. i was really looking forward to this entry but came out divided. dr for me could not match the previous 3 entries. it simply missed heart and more but i am not completely sure what. the story with ai in its center did not really hit the mark for me but honestly a second viewing will most certainly give more and new insight. benji and luther felt more as extras instead of part of the team and honestly looked a little bored and tired. filming circumstances were of course difficult due to covid. the stunts and action were very good as one would expect but it felt like this was perhaps too much the focus. i did love the desert scene and several other scenes that were shot beautifully but i am afraid that most viewers would not see that as i do, but for me very enjoyable! don't get me wrong tom cruise deserves al lot of credit and so does cmq and the rest of the crew. compared to the fast & furious franchise (especially the last few) this is a masterpiece. hayley atwell is a great addition and blended in beautifully and is of course a classic beauty. she was really good and interacted beautifully with tom cruise. i have no doubt this will be very successful and let's be honest, it is a true summer blockbuster that all in all is very enjoyable and yes i am curious to see how all of this will end a beloved franchise that has given millions of people a lot of joy and excitement of several decades!

well worth a great compliment to tom cruise!

is this better than mi: fallout?

when the emergence of a rogue ai known as the entity upsets the balance of global power, ethan hunt (tom cruise) is assigned to locate a two part key that will allow whoever wields it to gain control of the entity. as hunt assembles his team of luther stickell (ving rhames), benji dunn (simon pegg), and ilsa faust (rebecca ferguson) to track down the key their paths cross with professional thief grace (hayley atwell) as the team works against gabriel (esai morales) a man from ethan's past who appears to be working for the entity.

mission: impossible-dead reckoning part 1 is the seventh installment in the mission: impossible franchise and was one of many productions that had to work around the covid-19 pandemic (hence it's $290 million production budget). as with other installments in the series since ghost protocol, the film garnered critical and audience acclaim but due to competition from summer releases such as "barbieheimer" the film saw its box office slightly diminished from fallout. while i don't think dead reckoning is as good as fallout, it still maintains the solid craft and writing the series has exhibited making it a worthy entry in the series.

in a rather timely fashion, the new antagonist the entity deals with the emerging concerns of a. i. and ties into feelings and fears of uncertain regarding the technology in an ear where digital outlets are becoming less trustworthy and we see the agencies in the film switch back to older technology as a workaround. the new antagonist leads to some really unnerving sequences especially a scene where benji is forced to give personal information to complete a puzzle box or when the entity mimics benji's voice. as per usual the action sequences are exhilarating with some breathtaking sequences and cruise and his ensemble have excellent chemistry with each other. the only downside is that esai morales isn't the greatest villain as he's essentially second banana to the entity so he's a slight step down from the likes of walker and solomon lane from fallout.

mission: impossible-dead reckoning part one continues the level of exceptional quality we've come to expect from this series and despite being the first half in a two part story it doesn't feel incomplete and still provides a solid experience that's reasonably self contained. whether it can continue on with the second installment remains to be seen but i'm optimistic.

it was worth waiting to catch this movie on streaming, because "mission: impossible: dead reckoning" part one lived up to its hype, to a good extent.

in a lot of ways, this particular m. i. movie contained intriguing parallels to the "james bond" franchise. i found some notable similarities (which was good), especially among the villains.

as for tom cruise playing ethan hunt, he was every bit as talented, riveting, ambitious, and powerful on screen. from performing his own stunts to making them look easy, cruise proved that he can do whatever he puts his mind to.

his minimally comedic bits were quite good too. on a darker note, the past was coming back to haunt ethan. these portions of the movie made it feel like something of a full-circle moment for this iconic character whom we've seen accumulate a fair bit of trauma over six movies.

three of the most unforgettable ladies in "dead reckoning" were hayley atwell (as grace), rebecca ferguson (as ilsa faust), and vanessa kirby (as alanna mitsopolis, aka the white widow). they each gave amazing performances.

like i said earlier, there was a distinct bond-style flourish to this movie. with grace, ilsa, and alanna, i saw something resembling bond-girl characterizations, which managed to fit the m. i. bill.

in this plotline, ethan was working on a new imf (impossible mission force) task to stop a deadly weapon - an active-learning defense system, nestled in a russian stealth submarine called sevastopol - from reaching certain corrupt parties who'd most definitely misuse it.

ethan's job was to find two halves of a stolen key that could control, perhaps even eliminate, the 'entity' (the doomsday weapon). as time went, ethan chose to do the right thing, even if it meant paying a lofty price and risking his life (and that of his friends) in the most perilous way.

the writers went full-on doomsday mode when they created this extinction-capable weapon. it was as captivating as it was chilling. the thing could take control of any digital framework and use it against us, for starters. the entity's main agenda was to control the narrative and, to achieve that end, it started targeting global intelligence networks.

as a distinctly sentient a. i., this weapon felt rooted in relevance like few others. given what a relatively simpler free-range artificial intelligence - like chatgpt, midjourney, and deepfakes (audio and video) - have achieved so far, the entity felt like a real-life foreshadowing of things to come.

i liked how the movie team maintained a slow-n-serious pace where needed before turning up the intensity. it benefited the story and made it feel convincing rather than purely commercial. with the stakes (in the plot) so high, this approach to visual storytelling set "mission: impossible: dead reckoning" apart from most of its previous instalments.

however, i wasn't particularly fond of the dumbed-down dialogues sprinkled throughout. i felt they sliced off some of the mystique and sophistication in this otherwise remarkably complex story.

all the friendship angles - featuring ving rhames (as luther stickell), simon pegg (as benji dunn), rebecca ferguson (as ilsa faust), and tom cruise of course (as ethan hunt) - were wonderfully balanced.

every single stunt choreography was on point. these were, as anticipated, the highlights of the movie. not a single frame was sub-par where stunts were concerned, especially the car chases and action involving other vehicles, like the orient express train (quite the detailed set there!).

all said and done, the team packed so much into part 1 that part of me is nervous what they have left to show in the sequel. but fans (like myself) of this franchise will believe there's hope for greatness as long as cruise is on board.

"mission: impossible: dead reckoning" part 1 was a shockingly simple story. they used all the familiar tropes and themes this franchise, and genre, is known for. the real entertainment was in learning exactly how ethan hunt (one of the most beloved fictional spy characters out there) got away and stayed alive. he quite literally saved the world (for a time anyway), and a good portion of the box office for that matter.

just like the two split halves of the cruciform key, it looks we have two parts to this movie. cruise is going to head back to where it all began, back to a certain submarine now under the sea.

let's hope they don't take long to release part 2. who knows which 'entity' out there is preparing to sow chaos in human society, more than it already has so far.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one (2023) is the seventh installment in the mission: impossible film franchise, and it stars tom cruise as ethan hunt. the film follows hunt as he tries to stop a mysterious new threat from starting a global war.

the film is directed by christopher mcquarrie, who also directed the previous two mission: impossible films. mcquarrie brings his signature style to the film, with plenty of exciting action sequences and jaw-dropping stunts. cruise is once again in top form, and he delivers a performance that is both physically and emotionally demanding.

the supporting cast is also excellent, with hayley atwell, pom klementieff, and vanessa kirby all giving standout performances. the film also features a number of cameos from previous mission: impossible films.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a must-see for fans of the franchise. the film is full of action, suspense, and humor. it is also a visually stunning film, with some of the best cinematography in the franchise.

there is a meta-narrative at work here that is being explicit and interestingly played upon. in fact, the entity should have been called "meta" it would have been closer to what device it serves in the film. of course the name was taken.

meta : "the entity - the artificial intelligence - operates as follows:

it can calculate all probabilities. in its calculations, it determines which character is most interesting for self-protection (who should steal the keys ?). therefore, it makes predictions by using the character motive (the thief comes in handy), the psychology of individuals and then subtly guides them in its plan without their knowledge.

there is a significant underlying subtext that could highly explain the second part of the movie (whether accepted or not). in addition to the narrative element of a "sentient" code to destroy the world, there is a perspective regarding this entity: the entity functions as the all-powerful screenwriter of the mission impossible film, it is the story.

the entity utilizes its computational power to manipulate human beings with fifty moves ahead. this is how the characters realize they are faced with inevitability, questioning which choice is the right one. it is like a screenwriter trying to make its way to the final chapter.

the entity uses one and then the other, but of course, it fears a character: ethan hunt (obviously). why? because he is the only one who is not interested in power and whose motivation is devoid of personal interest. he will do what is right, even if it puts him in danger, because "he will protect other's life more than his own" (it's the pinnacle of improbability: sacrificing oneself). essentially, he will use the keys to destroy the ai. therefore, there is concern from the ai that it must get rid of him.

there is a scene where the imf heroes try to predict the ai's calculations and make ethan hunt promise not to kill the villain because it is an acceptable scenario for the ai. it would win since no one would know how to use the keys. ethan hunt understands and swears not to kill him, he says it through dialogue - as for the audience but also because the ai obviously listens to conversations, perhaps through phones.

then comes the final duel, and what happens? ethan hunt decides at the last second that he will still kill the villain, even though it makes no sense from a narrative standpoint and everything will be lost, it blows up the plot. but ethan hunt is exactly what the ai cannot tolerate: unpredictability. he doesn't think within the context of normal probabilities. it is worth remembering that the first action sequence happens in an airport, where all the alleys and paths are numbered and arrows direct the characters.

another explicit scene occurs when something happens to pom klementieff that could make her turn against her crime boss and betray the villains (apologies for the terms). the ai realizes this although only the audience has seen her reaction in venice after the fight with ethan hunt, the ai calculates the probability and finds this: pom will betray the group, so it orders the villain to preemptively kill her, even though she herself didn't know she would go that far (she explicitly states after receiving the almost fatal blow that she is surprised that the villain's reason to kill her was because she would betray him, and that he was right - no one would have expected a furious character like paris to betray the bad guys as she seemed the most evil and crazy from the start, it was a complete shock but that is the point).

in fact, within the screenplay or the filmmaking itself, the ai acts as a screenwriter of a mission impossible film, calculating plot points. ethan hunt is the hero, he is the one who makes decisions that disrupt the causes and consequences until he breaks free from the plot and saves people.

furthermore, the opening credits consist of a trailer showcasing all the scenes we are about to see (as was done in a certain serial era). it might be worth investigating whether these quick excerpts confirm or contradict the unfolding of the story based on the characters' actions. it's possible that some of the previewed images never actually occured at all. it was like the ai's vision, its prediction. and also the trailer as a device.

it may not reach the level of a kubrick film where everything aligns perfectly, but it's present, it is explicit, and it's amusing to see further with this film, whether the movie can claim a potentially underestimated depth.

the ai is the script of the mission impossible charade, and ethan hunt is the one who must break free from the walls. and that works on all level of the narrative.

this movie, about ethan hunt and his imf team who must track down a dangerous weapon before it falls into the wrong hands, is a great seventh installment of the mission: impossible heptalogy (1996-2023)!

this is a solid seventh installment in the long-running franchise. it features stunning cinematography, intense action scenes, and a compelling antagonist. the plot is simple, but the movie does a great job of exploring the "psychology" of the entity, making it feel like a real threat. the movie's pacing is a bit uneven at times, and ilsa's death is handled somewhat disappointingly, but overall, this is a thrilling and entertaining action movie.

mission impossible is one of those franchises that started rough but got better as more entries were made. the previous entry, mission impossible fallout, might be one of the best action movies ever made. of course, i was massively hyped for the next entry but i had a slight worry when i heard it was going to split into parts. does the mission impossible franchise continue to cruise upwards or this time a mission failure?

let's start with the reason that many watch this franchise, the action and stunts. tom cruise continues to be one of the few proper action stars as he does dangerous stunts for our entertainment. this entry is no exception as he rides a motorbike off a cliff, speed gliding and does a fight sequence on a train reminiscent of the first film. tom doing it for real, makes the sequence feel more real and it certainly shows in the way these scenes are shot. in terms of action set pieces, the airport scene is incredibly tense with how many groups trying to mess or hunt the imf. the rome car chase is a thrilling 20 minutes of pure adrenaline and comedic joy. the 3rd act with the train is an awesome, stellar and gripping delight to watch. lorne balfe returns from mission impossible fallout to do the score for the film and he delivers yet again. his score makes every action scene more impactful and the emotional stuff hit harder.

all the returning actors continue to give great performances but the new character grace played by hayley atwell is a highlight. i appreciate that she isn't an agent like ilsa faust (rebecca ferguson). she is an amazing thief that adds a bit of chaos to everything while not being truly loyal to the hero or villain's cause. grace is not accustomed to the shenanigans of the imf so she adds an interesting pov to what is going on in the plot. there is also great chemistry between tom cruise and hayley atwell which makes their scenes together really enjoyable. henry czerny returns as kittridge from the first mission impossible and he is still great as he was 27 years ago. the weird rivalry and antagonism between his character and ethan are fun to watch. there is a big macguffin in the plot called "the entity" which is a. i. and this is so different for mission impossible which has it be a bomb or virus. the entity is quite scary because it is very fitting for the time we currently live in and feels quite possible in real life. the entity feels like the real villain.

the human villains, gabriel (esai morales) and paris (pom klementieff) are sadly quite disappointing. it was great to have villains that aren't agents going evil or arms dealers like in past films. gabriel even has a connection to ethan's past which makes him a more personal villain. unfortunately, they aren't explored much whatsoever and gabriel himself doesn't become truly involved until over halfway through the film. paris feels like a james bond henchman and gabriel ends up feeling like a person for ethan to punch rather than a compelling antagonist. the stunts and action are great but they are a little underwhelming when compared to how amazing the stunts were in mission impossible fallout. it seems fallout set the bar so high that it was too tough to top it.

the script is also a bit weak. there are so many times when the dialogue is just characters mentioning "the key" all the time. i wish they cut back on this repetition or rephrased some of the dialogue. i also think the intro scene is dumb for reasons i won't state but it really shouldn't have been in the movie. on that note, this being a part 1 does result in a non-complete story. the ending is not as painful as dune or spiderverse where it felt like it ended midway through a story. here, the end feels conclusive for the most part and leaves you at least partially satisfied. it is just clear that many lingering plot threads weren't settled. i am not a big fan of splitting movies into parts so i hope this is not a trend we bring back.

overall, it is genuinely crazy how the mission impossible franchise is still this great 7 movies in. compared to other long-running franchises, this one still managed to keep me excited for more. i am incredibly hyped for part 2 and can't wait to see tom cruise's iconic run again!

without a doubt, it's an excellent action film with some of the best stunts in the series, but as a mission: impossible film, it felt like a slight step backward for the series. in addition to growing ethan's friendship with ilsa, giving julia closure, showcasing the lengths he would go to protect those closest to him, and squaring off against an intimidating foe, fallout included mind-blowing action sequences and stunt work. to display action extravaganza after action spectacle while forgoing character development, dead reckoning: part one splits the movie into two parts. characters whom i have grown to love over a decade of movies feel wasted, neglected, or neglected. although hayley atwell's new character was wonderful and took up most of the screen time, i would have preferred to see more of the original cast. the new bad guy possessed an erratic ability that confused people more than terrified them. there were a few crucial emotional turning points that i simply didn't feel the weight of when i should have. unfortunately, i was left wanting more from this one. part two might wrap everything up and help me appreciate part one more in the future.

yet another mission, yet another exciting action thriller, yet another proof that the mission: impossible series is the most consistent action franchise of its generation.

what the biggest takeaway from dead reckoning is that it is structurally and visually similar to the first m:i film. christopher mcquarrie's direction is very often tilted; an obvious homage to de palma. some of the set pieces and the way the exposition scenes play, they are all set to please fans of this series.

dead reckoning is not necessarily as much a masterpiece as fallout, but that is an incredibly high bar. this movie stands on its own. it is breathtaking and riveting in its own ways. the mission: impossible movies follow a definitive formula. the formula will always work when the movies themselves is well made. the works of mcquarrie and tom cruise are excellent craftsmanship. they made a movie that upholds its practicality and entertainment value, while establishing a team of interesting characters that serve significant purpose to the plot.

this might be ethan hunt's most personal mission yet. the movie explores this fighting machine of a character, and why he does what he does. the thriller elements of the movie, which includes cleverly plotted dialogue exchanges, works surprisingly well amidst the relentless action sequences. this is a very engaging film to watch; dead reckoning is simply a good time at the movies.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one takes audiences on a heart-stopping ride filled with breathtaking stunts, intense espionage, and a riveting plot that sets the stage for an epic conclusion. directed by christopher mcquarrie, this latest installment in the mission: impossible franchise reaffirms its position as one of the most exhilarating action franchises of our time.

tom cruise returns as ethan hunt, the indomitable imf agent, and once again showcases his commitment to performing jaw-dropping stunts that push the boundaries of what is physically possible. from the vertigo-inducing skyscraper climbs to the adrenaline-pumping motorcycle chases, cruise's dedication to the role is awe-inspiring, and his charisma continues to make him the perfect leading man for this high-octane series.

the film's narrative follows hunt and his loyal team as they face their most formidable adversary yet, a shadowy organization known as "dead reckoning." with a plot that twists and turns, the film keeps audiences guessing and on the edge of their seats. mcquarrie masterfully weaves a web of intrigue, espionage, and double-crosses, ensuring that the stakes are always high and the tension never wavers.

one of the film's strongest elements is its ensemble cast. ving rhames returns as luther stickell, providing the much-needed wit and camaraderie within the team. rebecca ferguson reprises her role as the enigmatic ilsa faust, whose complex motivations add layers to the story. newcomers to the franchise, such as hayley atwell and shea whigham, deliver standout performances that enhance the film's dynamic and inject fresh energy into the series.

the action sequences in dead reckoning part one are nothing short of spectacular. from an elaborate heist in a high-security facility to a thrilling chase through narrow streets and crowded marketplaces, the film constantly raises the bar with its inventive set pieces. mcquarrie's meticulous direction ensures that each action sequence is meticulously choreographed, and the blend of practical effects and stunning cinematography create a visceral and immersive experience for the audience.

while the film is undeniably thrilling, it does suffer from a few pacing issues. the first act takes its time to set up the story, which may test the patience of some viewers. however, once the plot kicks into high gear, the relentless pace keeps the momentum going until the explosive cliffhanger ending, leaving audiences eagerly anticipating the second part of the story.

visually, mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a treat for the eyes. the cinematography captures the grandeur of the international locations, from the sleek modernity of dubai to the atmospheric streets of rome. the stylish production design and slick editing further enhance the film's sleek and polished aesthetic.

in conclusion, mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a thrilling spy adventure that successfully continues the legacy of the franchise. with its breathtaking stunts, intricate plot, and charismatic performances, the film sets the stage for an explosive finale that promises to deliver even greater excitement. fans of the series will find plenty to enjoy, while newcomers will be drawn into the world of ethan hunt and his impossible missions. strap in, hold on tight, and get ready for an adrenaline-fueled cinematic experience like no other.

well the summer finally hits the cinema after a string of bombs, and tom cruise saves the day once more, just like he did with tg: m last year.

and what a hoot the film is, from beginning to end. not in a long time has a film this ling feel like half of its running time.

but, just like dod a few weeks ago, you really have to take a huge pinch of salt regarding the maguffin in question for this first half of this story. it's very silly, and there are a few times when you really have to suspend disbelief, but it works, just about.

cruise as always is excellent as hunt, and he knows the character inside out, and this film shows his foibles, his weaknesses, and the rest of the team are as essential as always. the imf team is essential to the films foundation, and they seamlessly bounce off each other, just like previous instalments.

action, there is plenty of it, and there are a few standout set pieces, such as the prolonged care chase with the 'hilarious' fiat 500, and of course, what the trailer has partially spoiled, that stunt, and a wonderful final set piece , which reminded me of the first mi film, the lost world: jurassic park, and even dial of destiny to some extent.

balfe returns with an exceptional score, and the film as a whole, really doesn't give you much chance to catch your breath, as every minute is essential to the plot and the narrative.

say what you like about cruise, he has been the most consistent big name in the last 35 years, and his films are always an event.

so apart from the maguffin, and one scene where a character gets ridiculously, and i mean ridiculously clever, this series continues to deliver, and i hope it will for years to come.

the movie delivers on its promise of thrilling stunts, gorgeous locations in europe and abu dhabi, and high-octane chases, with cruise performing most of his own stunts. the supporting cast, including rebecca ferguson, simon pegg, and ving rhames, also add to the fun and excitement. the story has so many classic mission impossible moments and callbacks. it's good. however, the movie is not without its flaws. the story is a bit predictable with some plot holes and inconsistencies. the movie also suffers from being too long (10 minutes of a toing and froing dialogue with the antagonists) with some scenes dragging on unnecessarily. the movie could have benefited from tighter editing and a more focused script. overall, mission impossible: dead reckoning is a solid action movie that will please fans of the genre and the series, but it is not a masterpiece. i would give it 8/10 stars.

mission impossible - dead reckoning part 1" delivers an exhilarating experience that makes it well worth the trip to the cinema. the action, pacing, and beat of the film are what truly keep you hooked from start to finish.

while the plot dives into the ai zeitgeist, the tech play is a bit overplayed, but it's the relentless action sequences and perfectly timed pacing that stand out. tom cruise, as always, brings his unique brand of intensity to the role. despite my reservations about his off-screen persona, there's no denying his ability to anchor these films with compelling presence. though his character may seem a bit whiny at times, cruise manages to pull it off with a charisma that draws you in.

one of the standout aspects of this film is its sheer cinematic scale. with a top-notch home theater setup, it's easy to distinguish movies that truly deserve the big screen treatment, and "dead reckoning part 1" is undoubtedly one of them. the action sequences are bigger, bolder, and crafted to be seen on a vast canvas with booming sound.

the movie keeps you on the edge of your seat, delivering a series of heart-pounding moments and intricate stunts that are a hallmark of the franchise. the impressive visuals and pulse-pounding soundtrack enhance the overall experience, making it a thrilling ride from start to finish.

in summary, "mission impossible - dead reckoning part 1" is an impressive spectacle that lives up to its name. it's a film that demands to be seen in the cinema, offering an immersive experience that's hard to replicate at home. if you're a fan of the series or just in the mood for some high-octane action, this movie won't disappoint. enjoyed every moment!

"mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one", although not the best part of the series, has a lot to offer:

christopher mcquarrie returns with his great direction. his script (co-written by erik jendresen) is strong, although the story seemed a bit disjointed to me. the jokes, however, were good and well placed, as were the tense moments. fraser taggart's cinematography is incredible, so is eddie hamilton's editing, and the brilliant score by lorne balfe.

tom cruise's performance is strong, one of the strongest in the series. however, others like ving rhames, simon pegg, rebecca ferguson and vanessa kirby are also outstanding.

so overall, while i don't consider it the best of the series, it's a really good installment in the mission: impossible series.

i was surprised to see this playing at the cinema this weekend in poland, before its official release date. i decided to check it out since the early reviews have been so good and since i was in the mood for some fun action.

the m:i movies have really surpassed bond films in terms of action, ideas, and even fun. it's probably the best running franchise now. and ideas are where this movie really excels.

in the movie, an ai "virus" of sorts has slowly been overtaking the existing global tech infrastructure. it is becoming so powerful that it can control and alter outcomes, affect humanity in drastic ways, and even affect individual actions in a given moment. this is a cool idea and very relevant given the context of the world we live in today. this virus appears to have more sinister intentions for humanity. the imf team, us intelligence, defenders/enforcers of the virus, and other world powers are all interested in a key that "opens something" and with which the virus can supposedly be controlled. and so you have the basic storyline as all of these sides will battle each other to get to that key first, which alanna mitsopolis, a black arms dealer, is looking to sell.

the way that this is set up is great, as there is a feeling throughout the movie that the stakes are very high. at different moments, the movie seems to have this eerie, almost surreal, matrix-like feel to it, that is created by the complex reality of the story and the tone of the film. the standout stars in the movie are cruise and hayley atwell, who plays grace, a thief that at one point gets her hands on the key and gets pulled into the action. they are great as a duo throughout much of the film. the banter and comedy is also quite good as i had a couple of actual laugh out loud moments. there was a little more "lightness" in this mi entry in general.

esai morales as gabriel, the main defender of the virus and also one of the pursuers of the key, was also quite good. throughout the movie he acts as if he is a medium for the virus or in some way controlled by it as his actions essentially channel what the virus wants. i was a little confused by his character or how such a character would even come to be, but some of the logic can definitely be checked at the door. essentially, he, as well as the other dueling sides, has interest in the power of the virus. i also really enjoyed henry czerny back as kittridge and shea whigham as jasper, who spends most of the movie trying to chase down ethan and his team.

the other stars in the film are the ideas and executions in the action and set pieces. there is a marvelous battle in nighttime venice. a surprisingly entertaining and funny car chase sequence where ethan and grace try to get away in a janky little fiat. and an absolutely ridiculous final train stunt sequence. its one of those that make me go "oh come on!" in disbelief while simultaneously not being able to look away due to the amazing and captivating execution.

overall this one is action-packed, with great ideas and execution, and is a lot of fun. it feels a bit more "classic" in tone with a lot of the themes and plot developments resembling the first m:i movie. i really enjoyed that. there is more intrigue and mystery than outright action. as i said, there are a lot of funny, more lighthearted moments as well and cruise is the one delivering a lot of them. i guess it's a bit disheartening that with all that said, i still felt bored at moments during the movie. perhaps this was just the state of mind i was in. perhaps it is a statement of how high the bar has already been set by all the m:i movies and ideas in the past. and perhaps it is also a result of being a bit jaded by all of the action and cgi films of the past decade, which have left me with a feeling of riding one roller-coaster after another, with each one trying to outdo the previous one. it didn't blow me away and take me by surprise as much as top gun maverick did, for example.

with that said, there are plenty of clever ideas here, inventive action, and funny and lighthearted moments, along with an overall more classic espionage movie tone. it's good and people will not be disappointed, even if it is a part 1 of 2. it leaves you with a feeling of closure as far as the events that transpired, but also with a knowledge that more will come and that it could be quite spectacular. it's value might also grow on a repeated viewing and once the second part completes the story.

viewers seek out mi films for two reasons: the crazy stunts, and a "won't strain your brain" popcorn movie. this movie checks both of those boxes.

cruise does fewer dramatic roles in favor of splashier action flicks of late. and not surprisingly, they're pretty darn good. but not always perfect.

when you go to a mission movie (much like bond or bourne) you're watching for the thrill ride and excellent supporting cast and twisty story. all are present in this film, but it's missing one thing that would make it a nine or a ten: a strong villain played by a capable actor. the "big bad" is a rogue ai program called the entity, so no on-screen villain in that regard. the entity's human chess piece-avatar is played by esai morales (replacing nicolas hoult), a very middle grade actor who is unable to inspire any true tension or fear. by comparison henry cavill as fallout's chess piece bad guy was phenomenal.

the other new performers: pom klementieff, hayley atwell and henry czerny all acquit themselves well. fringe returnees vanessa kirby and rebecca ferguson (who i guess isn't really' fringe') are also terrific.

cruise, the ultimate performer delivers numerous edge-of-your-seat stunts that are amazing. his jaw flexing, minimal dialogue ethan hunt still carries the emotional weight we need to see from the lead actor in an action series.

but, that villain, or villains, as the case may be, and the demise of one of our favorite players, for me, left the ending feeling hollow and flat. so to was the silly scene with morales staring at the sky screaming "hunt!!!" a la captain james t kirk bellowing out the iconic similar scream: "khan!!!" i'll see the next one for sure. just hoping for a rousing wrap up since cruise has said this will be his last mission film.

although the story seems a little lackluster and is filled with typical action movie clichés, they feel completely in place in what is the best mission impossible film to date.

tom cruise delivers once again with some white knuckle set pieces and stunts that keep you on the edge of your seat. and the great thing is that they don't stop coming throughout the films almost 3 hour run time.

pair this with the comedic quips, an amazing car chase sequence as well as a decent serving of hand to hand combat and christopher mcquarrie has directed exactly what the dictionary definition of a popcorn action movie should be.

overall a great movie that looks amazing on the big screen with its stunning set pieces and locale choices that has some weaker story elements and is very predictable yet the non stop thrilling action will have you overlooking it's shortcomings.

no other franchise does action and espionage like mission impossible does. seven movies in and these movies continue to surprise. this series is the best at using action sequences to build the characters, show their relationships and motivations. the airport sequence, the car chase in rome and the train sequence are all built on the choices the characters make in them and kept the audience on edge of their seat throughout. tom cruise commits to the stunts as always and it's glorious to behold. hayley atwell really surprised me as a thief who gets caught up in the adventure. she was a true wild card here. having an a. i. be the villain is both a unique and current day choice. it's a terrifying force and its presence is felt throughout, leading to one of my favorite moments in the film. the 3rd act on the train is really special, operating on multiple levels of deception, betrayals, hand to hand fights, culminating in a spectacular crash. i had a blast with this film. even as a "part one", it felt like a whole movie. i love this series and the filmmaker's commitment to practical stunts and their ability to keep the audience guessing. this is what espionage movies should strive to be. i had a great time at the theater. 8/10.
