title: "dead reckoning: a riveting addition to the mission impossible franchise"

review: i recently had the opportunity to watch "mission impossible: dead reckoning," and i must say it lived up to the high expectations set by its predecessors. this action-packed thriller takes the audience on a wild ride filled with heart-stopping moments, clever twists, and intense espionage.

one of the film's strongest points is its incredible cast, led by the ever-impressive tom cruise as ethan hunt. cruise once again showcases his dedication to the role, delivering an outstanding performance that keeps viewers on the edge of their seats. the chemistry between the cast members is palpable, adding depth and authenticity to their characters' interactions.

the plot of "dead reckoning" is intricately woven, with multiple layers of suspense and intrigue. it intelligently combines elements of international espionage, high-stakes heists, and jaw-dropping action sequences. each scene is meticulously crafted, offering a perfect balance of heart-pounding intensity and well-timed comedic moments.

the film's visual effects are nothing short of spectacular. from breathtaking chase scenes to elaborate set pieces, the attention to detail is impressive. the use of practical stunts and minimal reliance on cgi adds a genuine and immersive quality to the action sequences, making them all the more thrilling to watch.

additionally, the film's soundtrack heightens the tension and enhances the overall experience. the score perfectly complements the on-screen action, elevating the emotions and immersing the audience in the adrenaline-fueled world of the mission impossible franchise.

while "dead reckoning" maintains the essence of the series, it also manages to introduce fresh elements and unexpected plot twists, keeping even the most dedicated fans guessing. the writing is sharp, filled with clever dialogue and engaging character dynamics.

overall, "mission impossible: dead reckoning" is a thrilling addition to the franchise that is sure to please fans and captivate newcomers alike. it boasts a talented cast, a gripping storyline, impressive visuals, and a pulse-pounding score. if you're a fan of action-packed espionage thrillers, this film is an absolute must-see.

rating: 10/10.

"mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one" is an action-packed blockbuster that delivers on all fronts. with heart-stopping stunts, a compelling story, and a talented ensemble cast, this latest instalment in the long-running franchise is a testament to the enduring quality and excitement that the series consistently offers.

the story centres around our beloved superspy ethan hunt (tom cruise) and his team as they are tasked with retrieving a powerful key that holds control over an all-encompassing artificial intelligence (ai). as the mission unfolds, ethan and his team find themselves entangled in a web of danger and deception. they encounter formidable adversaries who are determined to possess the key and utilize its immense power for their own sinister purposes. the key becomes the ultimate prize in a high-stakes game, where the fate of not only the intelligence community but also the world hangs in the balance. what sets "dead reckoning part one" apart is its exploration of ethan hunt's character and the personal stakes involved in the mission. as the story unfolds, we delve deeper into ethan's past and witness the emotional toll that his life as a spy has taken on him. the movie delves into the sacrifices he has made and the price he continues to pay for his dedication to his team and the greater good. throughout the film, ethan hunt grapples with complex moral dilemmas, testing his loyalty, resolve, and the limits of his endurance. the narrative presents him with challenges that go beyond physical prowess, forcing him to confront his own vulnerabilities and question his place in the world of espionage. with twists and turns at every corner, "dead reckoning part one" keeps audiences guessing as loyalties are tested and alliances are shattered. the relentless pursuit of the key fuels the tension and propels the story forward, building towards a climactic finale that leaves audiences eagerly anticipating the next instalment.

tom cruise once again proves why he is the perfect choice for the role of ethan hunt. his dedication to performing his own stunts is awe-inspiring and brings an unparalleled level of authenticity to the action sequences. the supporting cast, including ving rhames, simon pegg, rebecca ferguson, and the new addition of hayley atwell, delivers stellar performances that enhance the film's dynamic and chemistry.

it isn't easy to create a franchise with consistently good movies (almost consistently, since mission: impossible 2 was garbage, but we've seen much worse), and it is even harder to make it better and better with each instalment. with the mission: impossible series turning 23, it has come a very long way from the campy action flick mission: impossible, to the dark, perfectly narrated mission: impossible - dead reckoning, the seventh film in the series.

m:i 7 has all the trademarks of a mission: impossible film - dangerous missions, intrepid characters, groundbreaking daredevil stunts (most of which are performed by tom cruise himself), and some humor sprinkled in the mix. but it brings even more to the table than the previous movies with the most dangerous villain in the series to date, explorations of friendship, allegiance and morality, and a very serious ethical question which may define our reality in the years to come.

and do they level up the stunts! the climactic action sequence on board the orient express makes dangling from the burj khalifa look like child's play (it is not). however, the stunts serve a much greater purpose than showing off the budget; they become the very vehicles that carry the story forward, without making it seem like cash flick. the story is, as mentioned before, expertly narrated, reminding one of a robert ludlum novel, and still being better than the bourne movies. the characters go through excellent development - the brother-sister relationship of ilsa and ethan, to the friendship between luther and benji, to the smooth arc of the franchise's newest female lead - hayley atwell's grace.

it is fascinating, even magical, how tom cruise's films keeps bringing us back to the theatres. in an era when ott platforms reign supreme and movie pundits herald the end of the big-budget flick, top gun - maverick had movie buffs scrambling for tickets, and m:i 7 is all poised to reignite the audience's faith in the action movie. so, i tip my hat to you, mr cruise, for your exceptional work in almost every genre, and the magnetic power you wield over every film freak on planet earth.

in turns nail-biting, introspective, heartwarming, heartbreaking, comic and diabolical, m:i 7 has everything you'd ask for in an action film, and so much more, but even then one feels disappointed that it has to end.

as good as the previous installments have been, this one manages to beat them all: more action, more stunts, more stars, and ethan hunt still the hero you can count on when it all seems so impossible. this one chooses a very prescient theme, the dangers of ai. it also has the most emotional impact of any of the other movies. and it isn't another superhero movie. it's a movie about real (if somewhat implausible) heroes.

preparing just before christmas 2022 to see at the vue imax in the manchester printworks (the second biggest screen in europe) the return of big jim with avatar: the way of water,i was surprised to find at the screening, a specially made for imax preview of the next mission impossible. counting down the weeks to release after this preview,i got set to go back to the imax, in order to uncover the mission.

view on the film:

designing the chic appearance of the character herself, and revealing in an interview that "i thought that it was also night time, (when part of the film takes place) so i thought it would be nice to bring some light to the face, and to have something that would be like war paint." pom klementieff gives a blazing performance as paris, a battle angel who klementieff has takes everyone down with a brutal force, and drives in at full speed to wipe out hunt and his fellow spies, with a cold eyes killer gaze.

pocketing the attention of everyone, hayley atwell gives a sparkling performance as grace, who atwell laces with a caper charm, as grace flirts with distractions, whilst slyly committing another successful steal.

entering the danger zone, the cruise missile hits the target with a winning style, with cruise's passion and dedication to the series being visible in the complex, fully loaded stunts he performs, the miles of running he does across the screen, and also expressing hunt's attempt to remain cool undercover, whilst encircled by those desperate to unmask him.

reuniting with the imf, co-writer (with erik jendresen ) / director christopher mcquarrie & cinematographer fraser taggart (who was the second unit director of the new zealand sequence in mission impossible: fallout) ignite a smoking hot atmosphere of jagged dutch angles, push-ins and glossy whip-pans, reflecting the tightrope that the imf are walking on for the mission.

driving down the streets of italy for the mission, mcquarrie and taggart unleash spectacular action set-pieces, which fire crisp wide-shots that cleaning display the full scale of the sequences, with rough and tumble close-ups pinned on an urgency twisted open by every killer move by hunt.

going right back to the first film in the franchise, the screenplay by mcquarrie and band of brothers creator erik jendresen brings out a superb euro spy - style hard edge, via a tightly coiled focus on hunt and his fellow imf agents espionage activities, which the writers brilliantly criss-cross with a globe-trotting, to catch a thief mcguffin tale, as shadows from hunt's past emerge on an impossible mission.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a 2023 american spy action film directed by christopher mcquarrie from a screenplay he co-wrote with erik jendresen. it is the sequel to mission: impossible - fallout (2018) and the seventh installment in the mission: impossible film series. dead reckoning part one sees tom cruise returns as ethan hunt, whose imf team are confronted by a mysterious, all-powerful foe known as "the entity". the ensemble cast also features hayley atwell, ving rhames, simon pegg, rebecca ferguson, vanessa kirby, esai morales, pom klementieff, mariela garriga and henry czerny.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is not just another entry in the iconic franchise; it is a cinematic experience that elevates the art of action filmmaking to dazzling heights. this film is an audacious tapestry of heart-stopping stunts, intricate plots, and emotional resonance that captures the essence of what makes the series a beloved staple in modern cinema.

tom cruise, once again embodying the unparalleled ethan hunt, plunges into a world rife with danger and deception. his commitment to authenticity is palpable; each death-defying stunt becomes a testament to his dedication to cinematic excellence. the breathtaking sequences-from high-octane chases to nail-biting hand-to-hand combat-catapult viewers into a whirlwind of adrenaline, pulling them deeply into the narrative's stakes.

however, it's not merely the spectacular visuals that set dead reckoning apart; it's the masterful storytelling woven throughout. co-writers christopher mcquarrie and a talented ensemble create a rich tapestry of characters who each bring their own motivations and moral complexities to the fray. the layers of intrigue are reminiscent of classic spy narratives, yet they pulse with a modern urgency that keeps audiences guessing.

what truly distinguishes this installment is its emotional core. as ethan grapples with loyalty, sacrifice, and the weight of his past choices, viewers are offered a rare glimpse into the heart of an iconic hero. this deeper exploration humanizes the high-stakes espionage game, making every twist and turn resonate with profound significance.

the film is a stunning marvel, blending practical effects with flawless cinematography to immerse audiences in its globe-trotting adventure. each location feels alive, enhanced by a gripping score that heightens the tension and emotion of every frame.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is not just a film; it's an experience that challenges the boundaries of what action cinema can achieve. it leaves audiences breathless and yearning for more, proving that the thrill of the chase is only the beginning of this extraordinary journey. as the credits roll, one truth remains clear: ethan hunt is not just on a mission; he's become a legend-and we're all fortunate to witness it.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a thrilling and spectacular spy action film that delivers on its promise of high-octane entertainment. the film follows ethan hunt (tom cruise) and his imf team as they race against time to stop a deadly weapon from falling into the wrong hands. the film is directed by christopher mcquarrie, who returns for his third consecutive mission: impossible film, and co-writes the script with erik jendresen. the film showcases mcquarrie's mastery of crafting complex and engaging plots, memorable characters, witty dialogue, and stunning visuals. the film also features some of the most impressive and daring stunts ever seen on screen, performed by cruise himself, who proves once again that he is the ultimate action star. the film boasts a stellar cast, including hayley atwell, ving rhames, simon pegg, rebecca ferguson, vanessa kirby, esai morales, and henry czerny. the film is a thrilling and satisfying first part of a two-part finale that sets up new challenges and surprises for ethan hunt and his team.

"mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one" is a celebration of physicality and the art of action sequences, standing out with spectacular chase scenes in rome and venice that will leave viewers on the edge of their seats.

at its core, the film is a showcase of tom cruise's tireless dedication to providing an authentic and breathtaking experience for the audience. the famous scene in which cruise rides a motorcycle off a cliff is not just a marketing gimmick; it's an impressive display of courage and commitment to genuine action. cruise, who has become the embodiment of ethan hunt, takes on daring stunts that would make most actors hesitate.

furthermore, the chase scenes in rome and venice elevate the film to a higher level. the high-octane chase through the streets of rome is masterfully choreographed, featuring fast cars and gravity-defying motorcycle spins. it's a deadly dance of metal and speed that keeps the audience glued to the screen.

the action doesn't wane when the plot shifts to venice. the film presents a spectacular chase through the alleyways of venice, with ethan hunt and his team facing numerous obstacles as they strive to complete their mission. this sequence is a directorial marvel, combining impressive set pieces with thrilling stunts.

finally, the train scene at the film's conclusion, while following the typical checklist of ethan hunt's feats, stands out as a defining moment that illustrates the franchise's ability to exceed expectations with each new installment. cruise once again throws himself wholeheartedly into a breathtaking sequence, and the tension is palpable as the action unfolds.

director christopher mcquarrie, who has been at the helm of the series since "mission: impossible - rogue nation," continues to demonstrate his skill in creating unforgettable action sequences. the blend of cgi with practical effects results in visually stunning and emotionally engaging scenes. however, the screenplay introduces many implausibilities, a common flaw in these "mission: impossible" films, especially the use of masks by characters to impersonate others. if the script eliminated this, it would be challenging to develop the plot as we see it, both in this film and the previous six.

"mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one" is a testament to the power of authentic action in cinema and a tribute to tom cruise's fearless dedication to this vision. it's worth noting that cruise has already reached the age of 61, and while he once stated that this film and its sequel would be the last for the character ethan hunt, in july 2023, cruise expressed interest in continuing to make more films in the series as hunt. here's to a long and vibrant future for tom cruise and ethan hunt.

back in its heyday, hollywood would deliver a summer blockbuster that would have the effect of making your socks fly off, land across the other side of your room, your mum would tell you off, yet you wouldn't care because the following day you would be in school raving about it with your friends making those who missed it jealous.

those days are long gone. hollywood saw fit to focus more on targets, social justice and deconstruct or subvert your expectations, of the lore, the characters, in a backdrop of reduced demand due to covid. why go to the cinema any more?

mcq, tom cruise and their partnership, that's why.

in this latest iteration of a well trodden path, one that exudes 'family' without actually saying it, tom delivers again.

yeah yeah, we've seen the bike off a cliff, something about ai (bet there's plenty more of that on the way) and some hot chicks.... that's not why i say 10/10.

i say 10/10, because the women are bad ass strong, feminine, independent, don't revolve their world around mr hunt, in fact, 1 turns up to help, 1 is trying to get away, 1 is trying to kill and the other is trying to just get rich and powerfull and the imf are in the way. no male character is undermined devalued or deconstructed or subverted in the making of this film. mr hunt is mr hunt, although we do learn a little more about his background and why he cares about his team so much. i say 10/10 because, this is a rollercoaster, that takes 2:45 and feels like 90.

i say 10/10 because the story makes sense, the object one has to aquire to go from a to b isn't replaced by a task to do c and then d, with an object e. there's an evil villain yet, but there's a weakness and it's upto the imf to aquire this, beset by fraud, theft, sleight of hand, violence, trickery.

i say 10/10, because when spielberg said to tom cruise, that he saved hollywood, he was right. word of mouth on this film is going to give it legs, it's taken more in 1 weekend than other 'blockbusters' did in 10. i am going back to see it tomorrow. i will buy it on streaming. i will re watch all the other mi films, and may even go a third time. i was going to do this with star wars 7 thru 9.... then i saw them.... i will do this with mi:7

i say 10/10.

i will never forget the first time i saw mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one. not only is the movie absolutely spectacular, but i got to watch it in one of the most famous movie palaces on the planet; the tcl chinese theatre imax in hollywood! let me tell you if you ever get the chance to see a movie there... do it! i got lucky enough to see a fantastic movie on that historic screen, but even if it wasn't, the experience alone would've been amazing. plus the audience there was so into the movie, cheering and clapping numerous times throughout the runtime and i had so much fun with that!

mission: impossible - dead reckoning is a movie that demands to be seen on the biggest screen possible! it's an unforgettable cinematic experience - one of the greatest action movies of all time, setting the gold standard for spy films and delivering an exhilarating experience that commands your attention from start to finish! i was in complete and utter awe. writer/director christopher mcquarrie and star tom cruise prove no one is doing it quite like them, crafting one of the most thrilling action flicks since 2018's mission: impossible - fallout - one of my personal favourite films of all time. so it is no surprise that i have nothing but praise for this new entry: dead reckoning part one. frankly, it's an incredible film that will have your jaw on the floor. not only are the iconic stunts absolutely breathtaking to witness, but the story is very cleverly written, the performances are brilliant and mcquarrie's direction has so many hitchcockian sensibilities to it while also feeling very michael mann or even nolan-esque. it's a brilliant film that i can't seem to find any faults with, adding to the lineup of mission: impossible films that consistently deliver some of the best experiences cinema can offer. this is why we go to the movies!

what i really love about this franchise is how it is continuously changing; it never stagnates and always evolves into something new. each entry feels very different from the last, while also offering exactly what you've come to expect from these films. until mcquarrie came on as director in 2015's rogue nation, the directors would swap out after each movie, allowing for the style and feel of the films to change with each new entry. but man am i even glad mcquarrie has stayed on board. he is such a talented writer and filmmaker that he has been able to completely change everything about his approach to filmmaking for each of his mission: impossible films. with the visual style, approach to blocking, lighting, camera angles, cutting patterns, and music, mcquarrie seems to reinvent himself with each new movie. i love the look of the film, with lots of colourful lighting cues and gorgeously composed shots. plus all the dutch angles were very welcome! i'm normally a sucker for movies shot on film, but i thought the switch to digital photography for this film made for quite the poignant shift and it aligned with the subject matter quite well - as well as giving this film a distinct look over the others.

mcquarrie conducts a symphony of action and heart-pounding thrills you need to see to believe! in a series that has topped itself with each new installment, they have done it again! the action is perfect, the world-ending stakes never more real than now and tom cruise remains unstoppable. what a movie. it's also the mission: impossible with the most going on thematically since the first. dead reckoning is easily the most story-theme-plot driven mission: impossible since de palma's, with a pivot towards the existential. some of the heady discussions, veiled as exposition, slow the movie down, but they're some of my favourite bits--and clearly where mcquarrie's heart is at. the film feels like the complete opposite of fallout, and that genuinely worked for me. instead of using a plot structure built around the major set pieces like in fallout, this film is a much more emotional, dramatic, and intellectual buildup to the explosive 3rd act. i found it so clever how mcquarrie structured the film, from what he let the audience know before the characters, to how he so cleverly made use of the villain in the film. there was lots to unpack here, and the writing made the action throughout so much more satisfying! like, we've all seen the stunt for this film as they've centered the marketing around it and even released behind-the-scenes videos of how they did it... but that until you see what the stunt is for in the movie you won't ever fully appreciate it. my god was my jaw ever on the floor! yet again, the production value is through the roof with some of the most well-defined and exhilarating set pieces photographed in ways that truly make you feel like you're in the middle of the action. the emphasis on capturing things in camera makes a huge difference, and you can feel it. again, no one is doing it quite like mcq and cruise! there's so much to love!

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is definitely the movie of the year, with impeccable action scenes that border on perfection, it's a franchise in an infinite crescent where each movie that passes gets better. dead reckoning part one is an exhilarating spectacle filled with breathtaking stunts, cunning intrigue, compelling stakes & a breakneck drive that leaves your jaw on the floor. i never once felt its 2hr 41min runtime, in fact, when it ended i was in shock to see we had been there for 2.5 hours as the movie flew by! it's exceedingly well-paced and well-written. the movie is a delirious blast - it's a zany, almost dream-like tech-paranoia thriller infused with hitchcockian intensity! each action sequence is long, crazy, and intense. the story is big and sprawling, but i like how it both felt complete and left you dying for what comes next in part two! i also really dug the mission this time around and how the technology they're after factors into the characters' individual arcs. this macguffin has a haunting relevance to now which only made the movie feel darker, and this is already the darkest and most emotional of the m:i films. mcquarrie tells a very complex story with lots of moving pieces and characters, yet does a perfect job of guiding the audience along! it's also quite the thematically intelligent script and has a lot for the audience to engage with besides the action!

there's just so much to love in this film - and i haven't even mentioned the cast! no one is doing it better than tom cruise of course - he defies all limits and is effortlessly cool, truly becoming a swiss army knife of an actor as he handles all of the action, drama, comedy, and emotion masterfully. he's exceptional! but the rest of the cast was exquisite too! hayley atwell stole the show in all of her scenes and made for a great match for cruise's character! the returning cast members simon pegg and ving rhames are always mvps, i just wish rebecca ferguson had a little more to do here. vanessa kirby and esai morales were both excellent inclusions to this film, the former having an even more interesting role here than in the previous film. but i really have to mention how incredible pom klementieff is here. she sculpts an entire character almost entirely through forceful body language, musical-like movement, and facial expression. it's almost a silent movie performance. she's truly remarkable here; even better than in the guardians of the galaxy movies!

i cannot stop thinking about the brilliance of dead reckoning part one. much like with the other mcquarrie mission films, it is the perfect fusion of action, comedy, spectacle, and edge-of-your-seat set pieces. the level of craftsmanship here is truly insane. that last 3rd act sequence with the orient express is honestly one of the most brilliantly conceived breathless 10 minutes i've ever seen on film - it is easily the best train sequence i've ever seen! the entire film is a perfectly portioned meal of a movie, it's one hell of a roller coaster ride that manages to avoid the typical "part one" issues! tom cruise and christopher mcquarrie have saved the movies.... yet again! dead reckoning part one is an impeccably made action film that does not stop entertaining, it's a tense film full of emotions that is easily one of the best in the franchise!

bring on part two!

another exhilarating addition to the mission impossible franchise! despite the odds, tom cruise once again delivers a stellar performance, showcasing his unwavering dedication to his craft. while the original film remains my personal favorite, this latest installment certainly contends for one of the series' best. the opening sequence captivates with its masterful storytelling and provides valuable context, while the train scene stands as an awe-inspiring testament to the art of action filmmaking, boasting one of the most prolonged sequences in cinema history that held me spellbound. perhaps, trimming the runtime to a concise two hours would have elevated this film to an all-time classic. the car chase, though impressive, overstays its welcome, and there are instances where verbose and overly explanatory dialogues hinder the movie's pace unnecessarily, catering to even the slowest of viewers. furthermore, it seems cruise's linguistic prowess has become a staple in his films, but perhaps a break from this recurring theme would be refreshing. moreover, the inclusion of more brian de palma-esque "slow-motion scenes featuring dying characters" feels excessive, and the superfluous desert scene, akin to the one in john wick 4, adds little value. additionally, certain character decisions and actions become increasingly perplexing and illogical. however, let's remember that we don't seek perfection in the storyline; our primary objective is to be enthralled by the action, and in this regard, mission impossible 7 truly excels, leaving the latest john wick installment in its dust. kudos to cruise and the entire team; in my opinion, this film is well worth a trip to the theater.

undoubtedly, this franchise continues to amaze, with each new entry surpassing its predecessors remarkably. following the astounding fallout, expectations were naturally sky-high for dead reckoning, and true to form, tom cruise astounds once again. he is an exceptional talent, unmatched in his commitment to the art of cinema-a rarity that only reveals itself sparingly. rest assured, i won't divulge any spoilers, as this film deserves to be experienced on the grand canvas of the silver screen. prepare to be utterly mesmerized upon witnessing cruise's unwavering passion and dedication! i had the privilege of watching this masterpiece yesterday, and even now, i find myself awestruck by the sheer ambition with which cruise sets out to entertain us. this is the epitome of true cinema, an experience that fulfills the deepest desires of every moviegoer. remember, it all boils down to a simple rule: when you give your all, success will inevitably follow. at 61 years young, cruise's boundless enthusiasm remains unparalleled-a sight seldom seen. allow yourself to be swept away; venture forth to the theater, and prepare to have your senses blown away. this is an opportunity you cannot afford to miss!

the latest entry in the mission: impossible franchise, aptly titled dead reckoning captures the magic of cinema and condenses it in a near-three hour celebration of story, spectacle and emotion. if there is one reason to go to the movies, then this is it.

in a 1969 episode of the mission: impossible tv series entitled "submarine", a former ss officer is in custody of the imf team and made to believe he is on a submarine under attack as they get him to reveal the bank account and location of stolen nazi funds. whereas that highly-regarded episode focused on a series of numbers being the end goal, this one begins with an artifical intelligence that has learnt so much about mankind through the data it has collected that it takes on a sentient nature, holding the upper hand over the millions who have willingly given their lives to a digital world. mission: impossible dead reckoning begins with a submarine believed to be targeted by an invisible enemy setting in motion the events which reveal the macguffin, a halesque sinister force and a world facing not only the external threat of its own data-collecting systems but an internal one spurred by the temptation of man in his desire for power and control.

what follows is a mission: impossible film in every sense which is replete with high stakes, car chases, beautifully choreographed fight scenes and locations that take on a life of their own reflecting the imf team's emotional journey and the pacing of the film at every corner.

the deserted runes of rub al khali in abu dhabi are perfect for two isolated agents, ilsa (rebecca ferguson) and ethan to find one another, just as the densely-populated abu dhabi airport offers an espionage meet-cute in a crowd of strangers amid a crisis of bogdanovich proportions as benji (simon pegg) faces his fears while trying to track a suspicious package that reveals more about himself than he bargained for. in a nod to "what's up doc?" with undertones of "the thomas crown affair", tom cruise's ethan meets his match in grace, played to perfection by hayley atwell as the apparent petty thief who has more identities than an imf agent and even more sass to spare. the streets of rome provide a picturesque backdrop to pick up the pace as grace and ethan find themselves struggling in a hilarious and nail-biting chase scene involving a small yellow fiat providing the perfect set-up for close encounters of the screwball situational kind in one of the film's many humorous highlights. venice is the heart and core of the movie, providing a tapestry of haunting emotional scenes that push ethan to the point of no return as he faces his greatest fears and the loss of those he considers kindred ghosts, floating in and out of the world around them ensuring order remains in place. norway juxtaposes the concrete man-made bridge with the natural mountainous terrain of helsetkopen during a ticking time bomb segment where the physical stakes match the personal.

what follows lays out a spectacular set-piece that harks back to frankenheimer's the train before the third act takes events to a level straight out of the second uncharted video game in true mcquarrie fashion. the much-hyped bike parachute jump does not disappoint and if you miss it on an imax screen within the first few days of release then be sure to experience the film in 4dx for an immersive exciting experience expertly woven together by editor eddie hamilton and composer lorne balfe's subtle score which elevates the emotion and tension while soothing during the more personal moments.

the labyrinths of each location, be it night-lit streets and small alleys, river mazes or the majestic grandeur of the doge's palace bathed in artificial dancing light while simultaneously shrouded in an unsettling shadow of a malevolent force's gaze, all heighten the tension and emotion. what is equally impressive is the number of characters and how each is given their due. aside from the obvious choice of ethan and his nemesis gabriel, grace, benji, luther, paris, kitteridge, ilsa, alanna and even agents degas and briggs all have their own journeys and are transformed by the end of the film. it's a wonder to watch as these characters exhibit layers that unravel, highlighting who they truly are and showcasing how they, like the imf agents, all make their own choices with regards to their fate and who they align themselves with. background information on each one is feathered throughout which leads to the actions they take with appropriate consequences.

the visual feast on screen is only matched by an array of stellar performances, layered with comedy, emotion and a delectable desire for each character to connect to one another, to the audience and to their true selves. cruise excels in bringing ethan's journey to a simmering crescendo that questions who he is, who made him and what matters the most. rebecca ferguson's presence delivers the emotional punch of the film and she gets one of its best fight scenes against a stunning backdrop. pom klementieff delivers a wickedly insatiable performance as paris, who, like a firecracker in every frame, sizzles with unhinged potential and never fails to dominate her every scene. esai morales' gabriel straddles both morality and humanity, connecting ethan's past and future with a maniacal and devoid-of-humanity turn that would put solomon lane to shame. regulars simon pegg and ving rhames get an emotional gloss that allows them to punch above their usual range, inviting the audience to lean in and discover what makes them so indispensable to ethan's every escapade. hayley atwell is a revelation. she shines in every scene and her eyes look at the world she's been thrust into with bewilderment, fear, confidence and longing bringing an addition to the mission films that is both welcome and refreshing. she matches cruise's charisma and the on-screen chemistry between the thief of artefacts and the retriever is a cat-and-mouse chase you never tire of watching.

with themes reflecting isolation, trust, security, family, artificial intelligence and a world that's rapidly evolving in governance, perceived morality and balance of power, mission: impossible dead reckoning is in itself a huge setup for its impending sequel that cannot arrive soon enough. mcquarrie delivers in every department be it narrative, action, emotional resonance or visual storytelling, gifting the audience everything it would expect from a summer blockbuster that deserves repeat viewings in as large groups as possible.

how chris mcquarrie, tom cruise and his team will outdo this instalment is beyond me but with action, thrills, and character-defining moments that leap off the screen and embed them into the audience's hearts alongside setpieces that merge the humorous and high-tension, dead reckoning part one is a dead cert for an entertaining reminder of how movies used to be made before the era of cgi-overload. with the soulless replication of human emotion through digital means dominating releases in recent years, mission returns to reiterate that there's no substitute for strong characters, an emotional timebomb and locations that take you on a journey with each scene, and is a welcome hark back to the golden age of entertainment.

in 1996, with brian depalma's mission: impossible the fuse was lit but it's in 2023 and chris mcquarrie's dead reckoning part one that it truly finds its bang, celebrating the best of the franchise and of cinema in a must-see movie made for the big screen.

well, it's finally here. the one film that might instantly demote "indiana jones & the dial of destiny" to second place. and it lives up to the advance hype!

the prologue is like a cross between "war games" and "hunt for red october." as there's a russian federation sub, in the bering strait, testing a new navigational system controlled by an experimental artificial intelligence. but, the ai evidently goes rogue when it causes one of the war game scenarios to back-fire on the captain and crew. more importantly, however, is the mysterious disappearance of the fail-safe deactivation key from the captain's personal effects when the bodies are ultimately recovered!

this key becomes the mcguffin (a term first invented by alfred hitchcock for a vital plot gimmick) for "dead reckoning part one." fueling half the action sequences. the other half is fueled by the sexual tension between ethan, ilsa, and half-innocent bystander grace. plus the psychological tension between ethan and gabriel!

grace and gabriel are the relatively new faces to this film franchise. the former is played by hayley atwell, who's probably better remembered as captain america's wwii girlfriend and british master spy, sergeant peggy carter. although, with much-longer hair, in this role, she initially looks more like michelle monaghan as julia (ethan's ex-wife-turned-medical missionary).

gabriel, on the other hand, is played by esai morales. most of his fans will always remember him best as the older brother of ritchie valens in "la bamba." but, in this film, he channels some of that same cold-bloodedness he demonstrated playing robert davi's enforcer in the 007 film "license to kill." adding just a touch of new age nihilism into the bargain.

equally unrecognizable, as a marvel films alumnus, is pom klementieff as paris. without her mantis garb and make-up, she looks and acts more like devon aoki's ninja character from the "sin city" films! and gary elwes radically departs from his comedic good guy roles by playing a double-dealing washington, dc, bureaucrat.

the returning cast members look and act just as you think they will. only more so, given the stakes in this first installment! so, for those of you who haven't seen it, yet? expect a virtual roller coaster of a movie. for those, like me, who plan to see it a second time? you won't regret it.

the fact is human kind needs a boogyman to release their anxiety on. if that boogeymen doesn't exist usually people have a tendency to despise the other, of a different skin color, different religion or different nationality. however there is a new "boogyman", which of recent times receives more and more publicity and that is collective fear of ai (artificial intelligence).

suddenly the anxiety can be directed to non human entity, which is not sentient in its origin at least not in the organic-classical sense.

this concept in film isn't anything new considering films like 'termination' has been offering its own interpretation, however of late this subject has been very popular topic, as in our modern times ai has been subject which is more and more debated.

often hollywood blockbusters are being used as a indoctrination tools, to program the collective subconscious of viewing public, as it is with excellent'mission impossible 7' otherwise know as 'dead reckoning'.

no matter how unpopulartom cruise is being painted by mainstream press, he is still one of a very few true movie stars of the old generation.

for gods sake dude is 60 years old, looks 40, still does his own stunts and constantly delivers very high value entertainment, from top gun sequel to now arguably the best action film of the year.

this installment of mi7 is everything we love about this franchise. as stylistically director and producers seemed to get back to the style of the first brian de palma 'mission impossible' (plenty of dutch angles is being used) this new installment has breath taking action set pieces, which are realistically shot, without reliance on cgi.

the performances are very good as most actors in every scene want to build the intensity by delivering their lines in that deep voice that triggers the subconscious mind of the viewer, being hypnotized by actors delivery. the score perfectly builds the tension with editing and directions creates perfect tempo for each scene, so the audience feel entertained at all times.

acting wise the stand out is a hayley atwell, which becomes the center character, which the story is build around. she also becomes a female character, which becomes in some way romantic interest of tom cruises character, although as with most tom's movies this aspect is underplayed.

esai morales becomes formidable charismatic human antagonist, which is in servitude to the ai, otherwise known as 'entity' giving its almost demonic characteristic, as our heroes try to stop the inevitable using a key shaped like a catholic cross. (pretty straightforward symbology here ;))

bottom line it's always hopeful as it is with mi7 to know that this is part 1, so at least you know that at the end of this film you will not get the full conclusion to the story. i for one am very looking forward to part 2 and judging by breath taking action scenes with fantastic stunts, acting and immersive sound design, this franchise is defiantly in safe hands as tom cruise haven't lost his star power.

highly recommend!👍

if there's one word to encapsulate the newest addition to the mission impossible franchise, it would be 'astonishing'. "mission impossible: dead reckoning" is an absolute tour-de-force in the action genre, a breathtaking thrill ride that never lets up. in the ever-evolving world of high-octane blockbuster cinema, this film achieves the improbable by constantly raising the bar on itself.

the film maintains a blazing pace, rocketing through its generous runtime of over two hours that passes in a whirlwind of exhilarating action, never once lagging or losing momentum. tom cruise, as ever, commits to his role with an unparalleled ferocity, throwing himself into outrageous stunts that will have you catching your breath in amazement.

the film's cinematography is stunningly crafted, transforming the insanity of the over-the-top action into a beautifully realistic spectacle. the visual style is such that the film's extreme nature feels not only plausible but entirely believable.

"dead reckoning" is not just about adrenaline-pumping sequences; it's also a finely balanced narrative, drenched in character development. each character, regardless of the breathtaking action unfolding, gets their deserved time in the spotlight. this movie keeps you riveted to the edge of your seat, not just with tense action but also through its enthralling storytelling.

the film's standout scene - a prolonged, intensely choreographed set-piece aboard a train - is an instant classic. this high-stakes sequence, full of inventive danger and remarkable stuntwork, is one of the most memorable action scenes in recent memory.

unlike many action franchises, "dead reckoning" ensures that its spectacular exploits have weight and consequences, adding to the audience's investment in the proceedings. this film doesn't just explode; it resonates.

another impressive aspect of the film is its clever callbacks to previous entries in the series, weaving a rich tapestry that rewards long-term fans and underscores the coherence of the franchise.

while the "john wick" series deserves its plaudits for remarkable stunt work, "mission impossible" edges ahead by balancing breathtaking action with a strong narrative, character depth, and a certain mystical aura that enhances its appeal.

in anticipation of "dead reckoning part two," we must appreciate the cinematic achievement that is "mission impossible: dead reckoning". it's an invaluable lesson to other action franchises (the "fast and the furious", take note) on how to create an action movie that thrills, engages, and resonates.

finally, a standing ovation to tom cruise for once again delivering what is undoubtedly the best action film of the year. the relentless dedication he brings to these movies is a testament to his commitment to entertain, and entertain he does, in spectacular fashion. "mission impossible: dead reckoning" is a testament to how far the action genre can be pushed when made with passion, creativity, and a touch of madness. it's not just a movie; it's an experience. and it's one not to be missed.

tom cruise has accepted the mission of saving hollywood's summer as he did last summer with the classic action film top gun: maverick. i'm here to tell you that mission impossible: dead reckoning part one, notwithstanding strikes, has completed that mission as one of the best action movies ever, arguably even better than maverick.

although too many action set pieces litter the movie's landscape, each one is a work of art that tops similar ones even from the mi canon. if cruise's ethan hunt has ridden a motorcycle before, he has outdone himself here as he catapults over a brick wall like steve mcqueen from the great escape or drives over a cliff in norway saving himself like no one else.

if you think you've seen the best fight scenes inside and above a train, change your mind when ethan hunt tries to save a runaway train while he fights off the bad guys--an homage to hitchcock's north by northwest and the myriad other train fights in action pics.

as everyone wants to get two pieces of a key to the power of an ai that promises to destroy the world, a hitch macguffin if there ever was one, hunt has time enough for not one but two and maybe three attractive women who are just as tough as he.

softening the hard exterior of his hero, director christopher mcquarrie, has given cruise a chance to exercise those acting chops separate from most of the stunts he does himself (he must be self-insured!). the women mainly played by hayley atwell (she joins imf) and rebecca ferguson are attractive and strong, and he is strong and vulnerable, traits that help make this one of cinema's outstanding thrillers.

if you get a chance to see commentary on his motorcycle jump, you'll appreciate how the film preserves the old hands-on tradition with little apparent cgi. how cruise and mcquarrie will top themselves in part two is anyone's delicious guess.

like cruise himself, ethan hunt is aging and perhaps ready to give the mantle to someone like atwell. but then again, tell that to 80-year-old harrison ford.

the latest mission: impossible film is an almost three-hour long, adrenaline-fueled spectacle where tom cruise risks his life for the sake of our entertainment. it is intense, gripping, hilarious, engaging, and entails mind-blowing action sequences. christopher mcquarrie and tom cruise manage to outdo themselves yet again and deliver the best film of the franchise. the action is off the charts, and the stunt work is impressive. not even a. i. can stop ethan hunt/tom cruise from endangering his life. this entire movie is nerve-racking and had me on the edge of my seat from start to finish. the car chase sequence in rome left me in awe. ethan and grace riding around in a small yellow fiat is one of the numerous highlights of the movie. hayley atwell fit right in and gave a stellar performance. her charisma, zeal, and energy that she brings to the screen is so infectious and immediately brought a smile to my face. it's always a tremendous joy to see her on screen. i'll probably be replaying the train sequence on a loop till the second part comes out next year. how on earth are they going to top themselves after this incredible feat of the long running franchise?

final verdict: 10/10.

an ai gone rogue threatens to disrupt the world as we know it, and its key is a hotly sought commodity that ethan hunt and the imf must find. this key is the mcguffin for a prescient plot, but audiences aren't watching 'mission impossible' films for their riveting stories. since 'ghost protocol' (2011), tom cruise has been on his own mission as an actor and entertainer - to outdo himself with audacious stunts in each entry. 'dead reckoning part one' is no different, where cruise rides a bike off a cliff, as heavily promoted in the trailers. naturally, this may appear to be the film's centrepiece, and while it looks jaw-dropping on a big screen, the action has much more in store across its close to 3-hour run-time. the screenplay's pacing takes a little beating, but the film is thrilling, especially in its climax.

once again, tom cruise and christopher mcquarrie's constant need to challenge their respective boundaries result in some increasingly tense set pieces. paired with the franchise's iconic theme, they succeed in pushing you to the edge of your seat. additionally, the plot raises the stakes for ethan and his team, including benji (simon pegg), luther (ving rhames) and ilsa (rebecca ferguson). hayley atwell shines as grace and is a charming addition who pairs off brilliantly with cruise's ethan, both dramatically and comedically. in fact, this may be the funniest mi film in the franchise so far.

of course, the star of the show is tom cruise, whose running antics are awe-inspiring despite his increasing age. his commitment to doing most of his stunts allows the fight choreography to breathe, and the film is so much better for it. in this year of adrenaline-driven action films, it has become increasingly hard to distinguish one from the other, but cruise ensures he stands out from the rest. the fact that this franchise still has enough life left in it after seven films without feeling too exhaustive says a great deal about cruise and mcquarrie's passionate dedication to action-based blockbusters.

i'll admit that some of the mission: impossible movies blur together (though i like them all, to varying degrees), so i have to cautiously say that dead reckoning part one might be the best so far. i've only seen the others once each, and didn't rewatch any in preparation for this one, but i don't remember any of the others being quite this entertaining or amazingly well-paced.

after the slog that was indiana jones and the dial of destiny, dead reckoning was a huge relief - a big-budget sequel in a long-running series that actually lived up to the anticipation. this film has an amazing final act- the whole last hour is just perfect, as far as action movies go, being similarly thrilling to the go-for-broke final act in the most recent john wick.

tom cruise is great in the action scenes of course, but he's also doing great work here in dramatic and comedic capacities, too. the rest of the cast are also all really good, and even if the most exciting part of the movie is the whole extended final sequence, the action before then is still fantastic (and includes one of the best car chases of the past few years, too).

it's over-the-top action that also feels believable and authentic, and i think they just got the balance perfectly right here between hilariously ridiculous and genuinely intense/suspenseful. there's a lot of set-up near the start that felt a bit wordy - lots of silly technical jargon - but i guess they had to establish a central conflict to play out over two movies, so the extended opening was probably needed. but once it really gets going, dead reckoning part one delivers some of the best blockbuster action since max max: fury road (yeah, it's almost that good).

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is the seventh installment in the long-running spy action franchise, and the first part of a two-film finale that promises to wrap up the saga of ethan hunt (tom cruise) and his imf team. directed by christopher mcquarrie, who also helmed the previous two entries, the film pits hunt against a rogue artificial intelligence called the entity, which threatens to unleash global chaos unless hunt can stop it with the help of a mysterious key.

the film delivers on its promise of spectacular action sequences, stunning locations, and death-defying stunts, all performed by cruise himself with his trademark intensity and charisma. some of the memorable and breathtaking scenes in the movie are the abu dhabi airport sequence, the car chase in rome, the train fight on the orient express, and the climactic bridge explosion. they are all highlights that showcase mcquarrie's skillful direction and cruise's fearless commitment. the film also benefits from a strong supporting cast, especially hayley atwell as grace, a skilled thief who becomes hunt's reluctant ally; vanessa kirby as white widow, a black-market arms dealer and broker who has a history with hunt; and the rest of the cast, including rebecca ferguson as ilsa faust, simon pegg as benji dunn, and ving rhames as luther stickell, who deliver excellent performances.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a thrilling and satisfying spy action film that delivers on its promises. it is one of the best films in the franchise and one of the best films of 2023. fans of cruise and the series will love it, as well as action lovers in general. the film is also a great introduction to the final installment, which is expected to be even more epic and explosive.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one continues with the adventures of ethan hunt(tom cruise) & the rest of the imf team, after the events of mission: impossible - fallout(2018). ethan hunt & the rest of his allies at imf, must find a deadly weapon, before it's taken by people with a nefarious agenda.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a mind-blowing film. director christopher mcquarrie has given us a movie that has maintained the high bar set by a movie in the mission: impossible franchise. although, mission: impossible - fallout(2018) is the best film in the franchise, this one is a close second. the action set pieces are jaw-dropping. the fact that tom cruise performs all his own stunts is mind-blowing! the visual effects are phenomenal. all the gorgeous locales worldwide, have been captured beautifully by cinematographer fraser taggart. tom cruise is outstanding as ethan hunt. hayley atwell is spectacular as grace. ving rhames is awesome as luther stickell. simon pegg is fantastic as benji dunn. rebecca ferguson is amazing as ilsa faust. vanessa kirby is brilliant as the white widow. esai morales is effective as gabriel. pom klementieff is unforgettable as paris. the supporting cast is excellent. mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a must watch for action movie buffs, fans of the mission: impossible franchise, tom cruise fans & pretty much everyone else. go & watch it on the biggest screen possible(preferably imax) & have an absolute blast! can't wait for mission: impossible - dead reckoning part two(2024).

the real mission impossible behind the scenes was creating an action/mystery spy caper during the coronavirus' global outbreak. i theorise its impact caused the static physicality of the exposition scenes juxtaposed with the conversly b*lls-to-the-wall action set-pieces. ideally one has both the story & the dynamics unfolding simultaneously. perhaps managing large sets adorned with extras, stuntfolk, crew, & onlookers for hours on end was too burdensome under social distancing & vaccination rules.

nevertheless, the narrative thrust was intriguing & touched on ethereal concepts on a few occasions - no small feat for an actioner.

i wondered if the airport sequence was filmed pre-pandemic because it appeared to be such a lively, crowded set.

tom is ageing gracefully (... not!) but is always cognisant of ethan's risks & limitations. that is what delivers the payoff to these jawdropping feats.

looking forward to dead reckoning part 2. we'll learn more about ethan's past, surely, when that hits the screens in 2024/5.

as always, the cast & crew delivered under what were trying conditions. everyone looked handsome & delivered with aplomb.

it won't be regarded as the best mi in this series but it's definitely "out there" which makes it, to me, one of the memorable ones.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is the first part of a chess game. we have assembled all the pieces. some pawns have been removed from the board and the rest of the pieces are in position for part two. the m:i series started off as a spy thriller, then action film, then grounded the stylish filmmaking in favor of more gripping writing that still helmed great action. with dead reckoning part one we marry the spy thriller of the first and the stupendous action of the others into one of the best of the series.

the m:i series seems to work best when it focuses on the agents of imf rather than their characters' personal lives. focusing on the action works, so the action must be great. we get the expected amazing action scenes sure, we get a tad bit of backstory for ethan which sets up reasons for many things that drive the plot as well as how someone gets recruited, which is the focus of one of the main characters. we understand that these are people whose duties are to want to do the impossible. it's their choice, coerced against death or imprisonment. this gives the film permission to film the dialogue and plot driven scenes like action scenes. characters ping-ponging large paragraphs of exposition works to move things forward in a way that the action doesn't interfere. and the action works, not because it's just awe-inspiring or filmed well, it all feels real. we know that not every single action shot is completely real, but the suspense in every scene is real because the film wasn't an entirely-shot green screen lifeless idea of what action should be. m:i is original and pays homage to action movies of the past in a delightful way e.g. tomorrow never dies or the italian job, or even the first m:i.

a 10/10 film to me means that i was fully satisfied. nothing jumped out as something that i would change or try to make better. in short, it delivered everything that it wanted and needed to. it's the type of film that only happens a few times a year. it shows other films how it's done. it also wears it's part one subtitle on it's open sleeve and the last few minutes plays it perfectly in setting up the next film. a. i. has become more ever present in 2023 than ever before and you'll be engaged with the way the film handles the idea of not just our rogue agents, but the rogue adversary that seems more real than sci-fi. not every film needs to do this, but in a complex web of characters and their motivations, feeling a sense of connection is the true accomplishment of dead reckoning. tom cruise and his mad action made by top hollywood talent is the icing on the cake of this masterpiece.

difficult to fault this, in the action film genre. cruise just puts absolutely everything into these films, a franchise 7 films in that just gets better and better, incredible for a long running series. it helps that you have likeable and capable actors playing likeable and capable characters. what carries is though is obviously the spectacular action, and (sorry james) nobody does it better. incredible sequences and entirely or almost entirely proper stunts, not cgi. enhanced, like bond, by superb locations that just take the breath away. a long film and you never notice, because it moves at relentless speed. and while cruise is the star and the glue holding it all together, the others are more than just support, and what other film has 4 strong and capable female characters in leading parts? certainly not just decoration like the early part of the bond franchise, with some notable exceptions. bring on part 2.

first up, it's a part one, but don't worry you won't feel short-changed or teased (unlike another lengthy summer blockbuster this year, the animated one, which seemed to stop mid sentence).

some of the weaker mission impossible movies have felt fast foody and i don't really remember what happened by the end. this one, yes, a part one, is the longest of the movies yet at 163 minutes, and what that gives it time to do is develop multiple characters and allows for very long, complicated and breathless action sequences.

there is a flamboyant and noteworthy cast of women. i really thought when the casting team landed rebecca ferguson for rogue nation that they just got lucky, then they landed vanessa kirby for fallout. in this movie we get both of them (playing ilsa faust and the white widow), and two franchise newcomers of the same calibre. just think about that, there are four incredible women with incredible roles in this movie, and it doesn't feel forced or inauthentic. vanessa kirby's welcome return proves a great decision as she is even better this time, and her white widow has some real character development, then they've cast hayley atwell as grace, another incredible decision, she is a revelation, sassy and kick-assy. henchwoman "paris" (pom klementieff - great name by the way) doesn't get as much development as the others, but has great style and gets more time towards the end.

over to the villains: there's continuity and ingenuity when an old friend returns from the first movie and then esai morales completes a wildly perfect casting process, as the sensual and contained gabriel (great name by the way, evoking the archangel, and playing on his allure and deadly sweetness). the non-human character in the movie is also pretty great without giving anything away.

perfect villain casting was one of the strong points of the bond franchise of old (a royalty of european arthouse actors including max von sydow, klaus maria brandauer, michel lonsdale, robert shaw etc), and that's not the only thing the mission: impossible crew have learned from nor the only action movies they've been watching. the "empty quarter" sequence for one seems very much out of the nolan playbook (the villain offering a dilemma too), whilst the "james bond isn't able to protect his women" motif is applied well to ethan here.

i feel like they got everything right with this movie. some of the dialogue and filming of dialogue is sensational, and it feels like it's an emotionally mature film too. ethan emotes, and there's just little things, like the way ilsa hugs him that have a great emotional intensity to them. the core team are showing their age for sure, but they've harnessed that, luther (rhames) is at his best and most soulful here. there is no reason for action movies to be immature and mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is proof of that.

ethan hunt is back, defying gravity and logic in "mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one," a film that delivers pulse-pounding action, a captivating mystery, and tom cruise's signature charm in spades. this seventh installment in the franchise proves that even after 26 years, the "mission: impossible" formula remains exhilaratingly potent.

a shadowy past casts a dangerous present: the film throws us headfirst into a labyrinthine plot, where hunt grapples with the ghosts of his past while facing a threat with global consequences. details remain shrouded in intrigue, but glimpses of a powerful artifact and a shadowy new adversary hint at a complex web of deception and high stakes.

cruise shines, stunts sizzle: the action sequences are breathtaking, pushing the boundaries of what seems possible. cruise, as always, throws himself into every stunt with reckless abandon, scaling skyscrapers, hurtling through the air, and defying death with a grin. the film's centerpiece, a visually stunning escape from a crumbling berlin train station, is a masterclass in suspense and execution.

beyond the explosions: while the action is undoubtedly a highlight, "dead reckoning" is more than just an adrenaline rush. the film is surprisingly character-driven, delving deeper into the emotional core of ethan hunt and his team. the camaraderie and loyalty within the imf are palpable, adding a layer of human connection to the high-octane adventure.

a masterful blend: director christopher mcquarrie, who also co-wrote the script, ensures a seamless balance between action, intrigue, and emotional depth. the pacing is impeccable, keeping the audience on the edge of their seats without overwhelming them. the score is electrifying, perfectly complementing the on-screen action and amplifying the tension.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one" is a triumph for the franchise. it's a thrilling ride that leaves you breathless, but also thoughtfully engaged. cruise's charismatic performance and the expertly crafted story make this film a must-see for action fans and cinephiles alike. prepare to be captivated, surprised, and thoroughly entertained.

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one (2023) delivers exactly what you expect from a mission: impossible film - thrilling action sequences, intricate plotting, and tom cruise defying death at every turn. this installment, the first half of a two-part story, raises the stakes even higher for ethan hunt and his imf team as they face a new and terrifying threat: a rogue ai known as "the entity." christopher mcquarrie returns to direct and co-write, bringing his signature blend of meticulous planning and breathtaking spectacle. the action sequences are truly phenomenal, showcasing cruise's dedication to practical stunts and pushing the boundaries of what's possible on screen. from a pulse-pounding car chase through rome to a dizzying train sequence, each set piece is masterfully crafted and leaves you on the edge of your seat. the much-talked-about motorcycle jump off a cliff is as impressive as you've heard.

beyond the action, dead reckoning part one also delves into the complex ethical questions surrounding artificial intelligence. the entity is not just a computer program; it's a rapidly evolving intelligence that poses an existential threat to the world. the film explores the dangers of unchecked technological advancement and the potential consequences of relying too heavily on ai.

mission impossible is one of those rare franchises that has been getting better and better with each installment. until now.

the plot can be summed up in a few words -- ethan hunt must find a special key to save humanity from an ai entity -- and yet the writers make matters so unnecessarily convoluted that the film winds up at an incredible 2 hours and 43 minutes long, a large percentage of which is far from white-knuckle action. this leads to some serious pacing issues.

one of the film's key set-pieces -- a car chase in which ethan and the newest imf member grace (hayley atwell) careen about in a yellow fiat 500 -- is played for laughs, which is at odds with the general tone of the franchise. roger moore was just about able to make this kind of nonsense work in for your eyes only (his silly yellow car being a 2cv), but in dead reckoning, it's just embarrassing.

the deactivation of a bomb by benji (simon pegg) is a pointless piece of padding: he must solve several well-known riddles in order to do so, with seconds to spare at the end. the final piece of the puzzle could easily be solved by simply rotating the last dial through all the remaining options, but that doesn't occur to brainiac benji. this entire scene could have been cut from the film without detriment.

cruise's much-touted motorcycle jump off a cliff sees ethan riding his bike at high speed over rough, rocky terrain towards the precipice. i'm no expert, but wouldn't hitting extremely uneven ground at that speed cause him to crash? (in reality, cruise pelted along a specially constructed, very smooth ramp, the rocky ground added digitally in post).

in one of the most ridiculous scenes, hunt rescues grace by parachuting through the side of a moving train (this carriage built from balsa wood?), right into a gun toting henchman -- what are the chances?. equally unlikely is how bad guy gabriel (esai morales) departs from the speeding locomotive: by falling backwards off the train onto a crash mat in a waiting truck, a feat that, realistically, would have less chance of success than me asking hayley atwell for a date.

and as a graphic designer, i hated the fact that when grace's various crimes flash up on a laptop screen, each misdemeanour is in a different font and point size. why would that be a thing? a bored programmer with an interest in typography?

preventing the film from being a total disaster are a great turn by pom klementieff as blonde henchwoman paris, the actress stealing every scene she is in despite having next to no dialogue, and an incredible finale in which ethan and grace must race through several of the train's carriages that are dangling over the edge of a bridge, director christopher mcquarrie reminding us a little too late that he can put together an effective action scene.

"dead reckoning" (part one) has the same old mi formula: the apparently difficult and intricate mission, the funny and witty dialogues with benji and luther and, of course, the hot resourceful (and traitorous) girl (plus, the sexual innuendos). but it feels like the same old script with nothing more to give.

there's too much plot armor for an action movie. you know, the convenience of poor aiming from the bad guys, the easy get out spots in situations that doesn't seem like it (or, in other words, predictable coincidences), superpowered protagonists (or enemies if it fits the same plot armor), bad guys who doesn't intervine in fightings waiting for the protagonist to get his way, people in the surroundings that doesn't seem to care what's happening, predictable "unsung" heroes or, in general, deus ex machinas everywhere.

we know it's called mission impossible, but on the majority of the earlier movies, there was a plausible impossibility, with attention to detail and buildup. in this one it's just mediocre.

it gets a little bit better after the 70 minutes mark with the reappearance of ilsa faust (rebecca ferguson); although, she as a love interest seems off. however, the plot armor is still very much there; even with ironically an overpowered villain with a pocket knife to justify a pivotal moment for ethan hunt (if you've already see the movie, you know what freaking scene i'm talking about).

besides, there's constantly bad acting (it seems like a parody of action cliches) and bad casting for the main villain.

and the cgi is not that good everytime. there are several scenes where is too evident that is computer generated, and not in a good way; like the car chases (where there are several continuity errors) and, also, in the last survival mayhem, which is pretty cool, but the cgi is so evident that it throws you off about the credibility of all that is happening.

so, in the end, with this mission impossible, you get the same formula, but nothing more. and, for that, is better to waste your time in rewatching the good classical ones.
