it's a bloated version of what the franchise has managed to do in the past with a tight run time, simple story concepts and characters that stand out, but then get out of the way for cruise and the action. i can't imagine anyone watching this and being left on the edge of their seat, unable to wait for the sequel.

this falls completely flat and while they allowed themselves more runtime, they don't take advantage of it. maybe the weakest in the series that i've seen.

mission impossible dead reckoning is a very different movie than the past 4 entires. for one, it doesn't have a well defined awesome villain. 2- the film leans hard into dutch angles and closeups of actors. there's hardly moments where you can take in the scenery or get yourself used to the geography of the locations. this was never the case in previous entries. 3- what are the motivations of the characters to do the dangerous things they are getting themselves into? it's on thin ice motivations-wise. 4- there's a lot of tell, not a lot of show going on. things are being described to us as opposed to being shown in a clever way. 5- other than the climactic train stunts, there are no memorable action sequences as compared to previous entries. 6. the film is too long. the content in this movie could have been 2 hrs. it is a really bloated movie. 7. the hand to hand combat is not that great in the film when compared to other great action scenes that have n presented in other films this year.

the good stuff: 1. ethan hunt character is great overall.

2. some of the effects work is really great.

cut the movie down to 2 hours and i would think it's a 6 or 7.

simply put this was a massive let down and step back from the highs achieved in fallout in many regards.

the action sequences where far less creative than seen previously seen, with only the car chase in rome and final train crash standing out.

the main nemesis being a unoriginal ai system and a lackluster man with little compelling motive hold nothing to the fantastic solomon lane in fallout (who you can actually sympathise with)

and finally the worst offence was the outrageous downgrade from ilsa (a fan favourite with depth, connection to ethan/the audience and actually use to the mission) to grace, one of the most useless, annoying side acts who runs away 3 times before finally understand the depth of the situation (leading to ilsa's death!) and is then instantly forgiven and basically handed a spot on the team in place of ilsa.

we are then expecting to go on and just accept that grace has somehow earned the audiences respect despite being given every reason to hate her.

overall very disappointing but it was always going to be hard to live up the the peak of it's predecessors.

rather than "dead reckoning" this entry in the franchise should be called "by the numbers"

the scenery and locations they've chosen for cruise to sprint through are stunning, but that's all that really happens and there's nothing to differentiate the film from any of those that have gone before.

glamorous villains, expensive clothes, balletic unrealistic fight scenes, rubber masks, bomb threats, panicking comedy sidekicks, double crossing government officials, pickpocketing, outlandish and impossible stunts and lots of cliched dialogue while ominous music plays - we've seen it all before. it's not terrible, it's just been done lots of times before and the plot events are more sign posted than a theme park.

what plot there is, is riddled with holes which are ignored at the expense of trying to build tension - yet at no point did i have any concern that cruise's character would not prevail, much less die. the same could be said of his sidekicks - apart from the one who is replaced - an event which can be seen coming from further away than christmas.

the scenery is beautiful and the action well shot, yet the central premise is cruise sprinting between fist fights, long monologues, tricking people interspaced with overly long foot/car chases.

the fight scenes are too choreographed and look completely unnatural. most would not look out of place on a dance floor. for supposedly "elite" operatives, none seem to grasp the premise that guns are the best way to kill someone quickly, instead resorting to knives for some reason.

the story ends pretty much where it started and it left me wondering what the point of the film was - aside from making the studio a large amount of money.

mission: impossible - fallout is one of my favorite movies of all time. i will never forget watching it in theaters for the first time. i love all the movies and the overarching storyline.

but with dead reckoning part 1, i'm just confused now. why are these next two movies being made? it doesn't have anything to do with the previous films, so it feels like everything we previously saw means nothing. sure, they mention a few names from last time, but the 4th movie directly affected the events in 5, and capturing solomon lane directly affected the events in 6. but here, there's basically nothing except for the white widow returning. this feels more like a glorified spin-off with ethan hunt than a full sequel.

i am fully aware this is the first half. i love me a good cliff hanger. as long as it's done correctly... but this isn't. the movie literally just stops abruptly and thinks that having a monologue with music is a good outro. it's not. there's no big reveal at the end to make you excited for what comes next. no surprises, no characters returning out of the blue, nothing. when dead man's chest ended, barbossa coming back from the dead was extremely cool. and it was built up from the beginning. but here, the movie just stops. not cool.

but what about the action scenes? they unfortunately leave a lot to be desired. they hyped up that motorcycle jump to absolute death... and in the movie we get to see it for a whopping four seconds. four!!!!!!! i don't care if he did the jump himself. it doesn't feel like it when you cut it so hard and only show me a small part of it! the halo jump in fallout was so great because it was all one cut. that showed that they really did risk life and limb for this stuff. same with tom on the outside of the plane in rogue nation. we got to see that happen in real time for at least 10-20 seconds. but they just gloss over this so hard in dead reckoning... why?????

the pacing is absolutely atrocious. the reason why fallout and rogue nation were amazing is because they trimmed the fat and cut to the chase... literally! those movies had a lot going on, but they got straight to the point. in this movie? there isn't a lot going on, but it's the longest of the movies so far. so we have overly long sections of people talking about nothing and extended scenes of people staring or spouting what's going to happen before it happens. it's lame. the dialogue in fallout beats the dialogue in this 500 times over.

we have literally no idea who gabriel is. the actor who plays him isn't menacing or stoic at all. and the movie chooses not to tell us anything about him outside from the fact that he killed a girl when ethan was younger. how does that make him more evil than solomon lane???? solomon lane was going to detonate 2 nukes in the middle of kashmir in the name of creating world peace, and you expect us to believe this motiveless brick of a person named gabriel to be even more evil? without giving us any reason to do so????

don't get me wrong, the movie isn't entirely bad. but much like the dark knight rises, it's hard to appreciate it when there's so much wrong with the movie. i haven't even gotten into grace joining the imf, kitridge returning, ilsa dying in the most emotionless way possible, it goes on.

i'm not mad (well, maybe a little). i'm just confused. after the masterpieces that were rogue nation and fallout, we were all hoping that christopher mcquarrie and tom cruise would just knock it out of the park. but that hasn't happened yet. we'll find out next year if they did or not. that's what frustrates me the most.

a lot of us have pretty much grown up while loving this franchisee - one installment at a time. and it has been wonderful to see the franchisee evolve (specially last two movies) with changing times and taste of audience. but latest 'dead reckoning part 1' turned out to be very disappointing due general lack of depth in plot, characters and dialogues.

'sense of urgency' has been one of pillars of mi but throughout this movie, none was felt. everyone was just going about sitting and talking in long scenes revealing little and repeating the same points. after initial 30 minutes, i thought may be movie will pick up pace but there was absolutely no build up or edge of the seat scenes. multiple times, i found myself waiting for scenes to get over during later part of the film.

villian was kinda inconsistent and non-threatening and come onnnnn ----> 'he loses the key to ethan and he just shouts his name in frustration like this was a scene in home-aloneee' !!

tom's character seemed sympathetic or caring towards new female lead but they never showed any reason why he should be!!! in the climax, tom spent way too much time on bike while alot of action happened in the train.. eventually he jumps but then again climbs on top of train and villian actually ran towards him to fight!! seriously ....????!!

action and stunts are top notch with healthy dosage of trademark humour but overall too thin on plot line, characters or relationships!!

and i dont know when i will get over the scene where female lead is worried if he will leave her alone on the train and he says "i will be there!!!!!!???!?!?!"

alas.... so much wasted potential and money!!!

my wife is a big tom cruise fan, so we went to see this movie as part of her birthday celebration. i don't get the hype. the plot felt very forced to me with contrivances and bizarre explanations for things rather than true exposition and plot development just to be able to get to an action sequence. the action sequences also felt very stale as we have seen people running on trains and car chases through european streets many times in the past. the storyline was also very convoluted. overall, i did not find this one very interesting. while my wife is looking forward to the second part, i will go just to support her but i'm really not that interested in what happens next.

over all it was entertaining but the writing was very cheesy. at one point there were 8 people in a room and each person spoke one line and then another person finished that sentence and it went on like that for 5 minutes. what really did it was when the main "bad guy" was fooled by ethan and in anger he yells out "eeeeeettttthhhhhaaaannnnnn" to the air as the camera pans away. it was a good action movie and there were some redeeming qualities like simon pegg and haley atwell and tom running a lot but i could have watched the movie on silent and still got as much out of it. entertaining but really cheesy.

not enough simon peg, and not enough of the team solving problems.

the fun in these movies is from the characters different strengths and them playing off of each other. and that was missing here.

it starts off pretty good, i was thinking "yeah! a good action movie" and then it ended up feeling quite long.

while at times pom was quite good, at other times she felt like a 90's bond villain; which was just out of place in this movie.

ilsa wasn't bad but i didn't see any real chemistry between her and ethan and the way she died seemed silly and forced for the story line. with a fairly long sword she lost to a guy with a short knife.

gabriel seemed like he was computer generated rather than just bossed around by a computer.

briggs, while good, sounded silly complaining how ethan always goes rogue, because he seemed to forget that he always gets the mission done that way.

and don't even get me started on why ethan told kittridge up front that he was going rogue, he could have pretended like he was going to get the key and return it to him for awhile.

while impressive, the real motorcycle/parachute jump was made odd by ethan whining about it. his entire career has been stunts like that and he never whined about them before.

the tiny car chase was funny, but it felt like the movie switched to inspector gadget for awhile. it just didn't fit.

also, a signal being analog doesn't mean a computer can't interpret it and even alter it. it would just switch it to digital then back to analog. fun fact: when a 'digital' signal is transmitted over wires like network cable it is actually an analog sinewave where up is on and down is off.

and finally, if i had to hear them say "the entity" one more time!!!! at some point they would just say "it".

weak villain they should have showed why the villain guy is listening to the entity or why he hates hunt so much.

the entity isn't organic, but at least it's unique it's like it was forced into the plot this is because everything just suddenly happend, the movie could have been about a stopping the bad guy creating the entity and failing (but that is already done)

the stakes are weak they should have showed what the entity will do after destroying the key, fake atomic bomb is not enough. (in the movie they just told it by saying it hacked into important places)

they should have showed the bombs in the bridge earlier in act 3 so that the stakes are a little higher.

too lucky i know they need luck in order to beat the entity, atleast make it so that hunt didn't look confused after crushing into the train and make him react to the enemy, make it that he opened the parashout on purpose to tackle the enemy, make it more him rather than luck.

ps, i honestly wanna rate 1 star because i saw a review with 10/10 saying it it was soo good he could cry.

a 2 hour and 45 minute film about a key and people talking about said key !

have i got the key ? do you have the key ? who has the key? does anyone have the key ? i actually don't care anymore and would like whoever has the key to use it as a weapon and put me out of my misery !

aside from that the action scenes are great fun, tom cruise does lots of running and plays russian roulette with his life.....although i'm pretty sure he's made a deal with devil and is immortal. he's certainly aging slower than most 61 year olds ! 5/10

also side note: why do these reviews require 600 or more characters ? so annoying.

this was the first movie of the entire m:i universe that i couldn't finish. i tried, but after 2 hours of watching it, i just couldn't stop thinking about what went wrong with one of my favorite - if not the favorite - movie franchises.

the action is still good, tom cruise is still a flawless ethan hunt, and well... there's more cgi in this one to my uneasiness, it had everything to deliver, and yet, after the first 90 minutes i saw the same old traps that movies are falling curse to: bigger, harder, stronger, faster, but no better.

the premise of exploring ethan's past is interesting, but the main villain is cartoonesque, smug, with questionable fashion taste, being an incredible hand-to-hand fighter while looking in his 60s (yes, i know the actor and tom cruise are of the same age, but i guess tom has much more money to spend on cosmetic procedures) and this unstoppable force to match ethan's skills, but wait... didn't we have that portrayed majestically by sean harris? the anti-ethan plot thing?

i get it, movies need that momentum, but i couldn't bear with this plot. portraying an ai as an "entity" is a bit bland, but it fits the current world, having henchmen be its voice was generic and that may be the word to describe the feeling i had while watching it: generic.

it's a very well-executed action movie, but there's no heart in it. they had to dumb down the characters in order to create a climax, the ethan from the previous movies, the one thrown in impossible choices, and still thinking outside the box was just a plaything in this movie. oh, right, they also had to introduce a new annoying-as-hell femme fatale in the most uncreative james bond fashion that simply fails to see who is really trying to help her as she always backs off to save her skin, creates more trouble, is saved by ethan, rinse and repeat while killing a character who had a thousand times more connection with ethan.

i swear, the dumbness level of screen and character writing was above the charts with this one. you have a bmf agent with a sword versus an old dude with a knife, and she simply lets go of the reach advantage to engage in physical combat that gets her killed. great writing, seen that a million times. in fact, you could say that to the entire second half of the movie, that's why i didn't bother myself with watching all of it, i was truly done after 2 hours and 5 minutes.

fallout was the perfect setup for a much better movie. you had a team, you had an ethan finding a bit of peace... and they ruined it. i honestly regret watching this.

you'll have to really blindly love tom to get around the sketchy and predictable dialog in this repetitive thriller.

planning for the mission doesn't make sense.

vingh gives the predictive line and simon plays his typical beta roll.

but, you get to see ton in multiple running scenes, obviously his favorite. especially in venice where he runs and runs. venice isn't that big for all that running.

rebecca's character winds up without purpose. who choreographed that bridge scene?

the train scene is absolutely adolescent car after bleeping car.

overall, one of the worst movies tom has been a part of....right there with cocktail.

this could have been 60 minutes and then i would have felt less pain.

i don't even care about part 2.

i wish ai wild have written the dialog.

let the submarine collect barnacles.

i don't get it! even after being stabbed for twenty minutes, she reached the falling wagon (so no one would notice) and lifted the weight of two people? that's how? like in marvel movies, why didn't you give him wings and unlimited power?!

with parachutes, how did he get on a train at that speed? then he just hit that guy with a gun! each wagon fell one minute at a time, then the last wagon was suspended for five minutes! was the resistance of the connections stronger or what? it is not a locomotive that pours coal into the train, but the speed of the train did not slow down a bit! and another bug, how did it come to your mind?

it was really hard for me to like this movie. i used to justify the miracles of mission impossible series to myself, but this one was not logical at all. there's probably something wrong with the direction that caused mission impossible to lose its line of thought. there is no doubt that tom cruise's acting and stunts made for an enjoyable viewing experience. let's hope the second part is better.

there is so much for me to say and yet nothing at the same time. as an avid m:i fan, i experienced many sleepless nights waiting for the 8th when i got to watch this movie in cinemas. after seeing countless trailers and shorts of the stunt, i had a great feeling about this. but after walking out of the cinema, i ultimately feel robbed and empty.

firstly, this movie puts the m:i franchise to shame. although many will review this movie with high ratings, i feel that if you have watched the rest of the franchise, you would begin to understand where i am coming from. every mission impossible is about doing the impossible; missions that are far too dangerous, and stunts that would kill your average person. however, this is exactly why m:i is so so good. it gives you a rush of feeling and hooks you in for every second of the movie. this movie, although still great with beautiful scenery and a decent and relevant plot, does not convey that.

the movie felt incredibly forced and unnatural. the scenes were extremely jolty, and the smoothness viewers had experienced in all the other movies was not met. there was way too much storytelling in this movie, almost making sure that you could understand every little moment. however, the fun of this franchise is being shocked within a second and having to piece together what you just witnessed. the comicality in the movie became increasingly frustrating and annoying, and ethan hunt was simply trying too hard to be funny (again, not at all like his character in the other 6 movies). in all the other m:i movies, ethan does not think and make a comical comment about the dangerous situation presented to him, he just does the thing. in this movie, i think i developed a slight hate from this new personality that had overcome him for the entirety of this film.

the stunt that would change cinematic history was in fact shocking and extremely impressive (including the fact that cruise did 6 takes too get it perfect), but only lasted a short time before he genuinely teleported into the window of the train. how he got there? i am really not sure. this was the only major stunt performed during the whole film, and is simply not great enough or long enough to make the whole film great.

from unnecessary storytelling to a forced comical dialogue to 'lighten the mood', this movie honestly looks embarrassing compared to the rest of the m:i franchise. extremely disappointed with this movie, especially since it was built up so much in advertising.

i'm sure as people read this, they'll heavily disagree. haters will say this is a gross exaggeration of a review, but real fans will know this is exactly how it was.

this is a poor addition to the library of mi movies. cruise is played for laughs, with slapstick stunts that aren't funny and all of his edge is removed as he is constantly one-upped by the new additions, who themselves have precious little charisma. tinseltown tom also looks jowly and botoxed and seems to have been slightly manipulated at points by cgi or ai or de-aging-god only knows. the action scenes are eternally long but don't ratchet up the tension. it felt in some ways like a swan song for hapless ethan hunt and a franchise looking to extend itself with new young lackluster characters.

why is this film 2.5 hours long and it's only half a story?!

why does tom cruise's face look like it's ai? (not a pun or spoiler) his features are melting into his waxy face.

so much exposition and not enough time to appreciate the beautiful locations or build enough meaning into the relationships.

far too much talking and not enough left for the audience to work out.

fab set action pieces, especially the yellow car and the chase in venice and lets face it (pun intended) , this is why most people choose to watch any movie with ethan hunt as the main character.

whizz, bang, exposition, exposition, and one hollywood action star with a strange, smooth, barely moving face and a long wait for the exposition to pay off in the next film.

felt like watching one of the taken or john wick sequels instead of a mission impossible...... tom cruise did put up pretty good action scenes, but unfortunately they did not give me the thrill of classic "mission impossible twists". some action scenes are meaninglessly over-extended, which actually made me feel exhausted instead of attracted. in a word, the amount of content is just not enough to fill 150 minutes. besides, i have always expected mi series to be somewhere between jason bourne and 007, meaning the plots have at least some sense of reality for me to empathise, but unfortunately again, this one failed my expectation. the new and old characters are not well portrayed at all: the death of an important character did not make me feel anything much; and the ai supervillain setting brings out too much unreasonable plot(just for the most basic part i mean why the ai wants to acquire that key rather than destroying it since it is the only thing that can threaten the programme). to conclude, i just feel ethan hunt and his team deserve a much better ending movie than this. hopefully part two can be better, after all mi is the only blockbuster serie that still interests me.

i watched with focus for about 40 minutes. i didn't think i understood the mission. venice was shot beautifully. then i found myself wondering about tom cruise's skincare. has feminism got us to where the women in the film all get attacked and beat up. the women don't wear fun clothes. could hayley wear black knit top and pants like tom, instead of a vest? how did they conveniently find a coal-fired train for the long action sequence? i sat through whole thing, but too expensive for me. i am going to start watching the old mi tv show. i liked how they chose a team at the beginning based on what skills were needed and it was a caper.

felt like this was written for a 6th grader. so many obvious explanations about the plot that weren't needed. so many out of character goofy moments for ethan hunt, whose usually always even keeled. so many moments where physics didn't matter and shock value was prioritized. so many cheesy one liners where the shot lingers on the character, making it even cheesier. i never comment on any movie and try to embrace them for what they are, but i am baffled at how the same team that gave us incredible films ended up with such a shallow movie. attempts to make the viewer care about the characters or be intimidated by the villain just didn't land. i guess no one is perfect, and the team missed the shot on this one. hoping part 2 is a bounce back game for tom cruise and the gang!

i was so excited to watch mi7 and i had very high expectations. especially after tg maverick which is one of my all-time favourite films by tom cruise.

the best mission impossible for me is mi4 ghost protocol. each mi movie after that had to exceed what i felt with mi4. the overall cinematic experience- suspense, action, story, dialogue, character development and just the thrill of it all - was top notch. in fact, i had watched mi4 numerous times!

the following movies mi5 and mi6 were great. but sad to say, mi7 was a huge let down. although kudos to tom cruise and the rest of the cast and crew - one can truly tell how much heart and soul were put into making this film. however, in terms of how it connected to me as an audience, it just fell flat. and it was too long... stretched by dialogues that felt repetitive. i slept through those parts. especially as they kept on talking about "the key". my goodness gracious - it became a bit annoying.

even the stunts - i've seen them many times before like in fast and furious movies. the motor bike scene jumping off the mountain, that was pretty cool, but when ethan lands, it felt a bit abrupt. it should have been more exciting if we saw him trying to land on the train from the top view. i'm not a film maker, but i'm looking for breathtaking, edge of your seat moments that we have yet to see. i think that's what made mi4 so special, when ethan was on top of the tallest building in dubai. no one has ever done that.

mi7 felt like a james bond movie, but the american version. would i watch mi7 part 1 again? maybe a year or two later. i have to forget how it made me feel sleepy and bored. well, i hope dead reckoning part 2 is waaaaay better. crossing my fingers.

i get that it was shot during covid. it had lots of money and lots of hard work that went into making it. i've worked years in film production and i know exactly what that is about.

but the story is just plain awful and, to me, the most glaring are all of the female characters. all that work with ilsa, wasted. hayley atwell's paper thin introduction-then replacement for ilsa. vanessa kirby's presence was ill conceived and pointless. pom klementieff part was very thin. pom's fight scenes were pretty cool though. her character was just thin. very few lines and one of the most under developed antagonists in the movie. i haven't got a problem with any of these actresses. they are incredibly beautiful, charming and gifted actors. but the writing is super bad. there is also the imbalance of so many love interests, as well as the imbalance of too many antagonists and this is just the first half of the 2 part story to play off convincingly to cruise. again, good actors, crap writing. i would also add that the fight choreography with esai morales is "off". i'm not sure if they were struggling to make him look good and he wasn't up to it, the editing, the choreography or the shot design but it just doesn't hit the right beats and suspension of disbelief suffers. the chase scene with the mini cooper is overworked and lame. the lead up to and the "big"(?) marquee stunt of cruise riding over the cliff is overwrought as well. i did like the shot of him crashing into the train in a timely fashion but it's nothing that would save the movie for me.

i used to hate the overly stylized im 2 with the preposterous end fighting scene where the motorcycles kept changing, the tires kept changing, physics kept changing, etc.,... (nothing to do with the actual movie really but i heard that dougray scott lost the part of wolverine because of him being in this movie and cruise's inflexibility. the same inflexibility that lead to strife with reshoots with henry cavill on one of the superman movies. all over his mustache.) for an "action movie" it barely has a pulse, imo.

i really wanted to like this movie; i've been a fan of the franchise for years, and the last two offerings were quite entertaining. but this one fell flat for me. the character development was lacking... the deaths were ridiculous at times; it felt more like a comic book movie. don't get me wrong, this was tom cruise, doing everything we have come to love about tom cruise... but i really wish they would've spent more time and money on script development, rather than on the stunts. having said that, it was entertaining... and re-introducing old characters and integrating old timelines certainly helps prop up this teetering work; but even with all of that, i'm not sure i'll tune in for part two.

the action scenes and locations are amazing. the actors all did a good job. the movie should have been amazingly entertaining. the story and plot ruined it. contrived. confusing. mind numbing.

i think this is supposed to to be a twist on lord of the rings, but it just doesn't work. there is this one key to command and control everything in the world, it holds all the power. everyone wants it. rather then wield it, ethan hunt and his gang are going to go on a journey to a harsh environment (deep under the sea) to destroy it.

how this doubled up looking house key is so powerful is that it can control or destroy a rouge ai called "the entity". the "source code" of the entity is stored on a sunken sub. this ai though has permeated into systems outside of the sub and has appointed a devout psycho to carry out its wishes to stop ethan hunt and his friends. of course not just stop, but mentally screw and toy around with in the process. even though the entity exists outside the sub, somehow destroying the source code on the stored drive in the sunken sub will kill it off for good.

i wish they didn't have this ai bad guy. it obviously was very hard to cnopd.

i love tom, especially after top gun 2, however this movie was just meh. formulaic plot, one item of interest changing hands.

irritating close up shots of face, subpar dialogues, predictable plot armours. notch down in the level of stunts, moreover the showstopper stunt had already been put on yt, killed the whole experience of tom jumping off the cliff. female characters were all over the place and why was pom's character there even, the faces she was making during the car chase were cringe.

i loved ilsa as she had more depth. could have killed off benji or luther as the writers are anyway not giving them much to do apart from being present in the movie.

was expecting more.

good plot. started out with great execution but ended up following the john wick model of endless idiotic chases, fight scenes, car scenes, implausibility and 2.5 hours of what could have and should have been a 90 minute movie.

ethan hunt vacillates between between a super genius spy, assassin super hero and a complete bumbling goober idiot head over and over and over again.

and now we get to wait a year to see the second half of the movie that shouldn't have even been it's own separate movie.

but, i'm pretty sure tom cruise wants nothing more to be able to look in the mirror and see his dashing image in the makeup room as they produce another way too damn long movie.

i honestly don't know if i'll have the energy or desire to sit through another 2.5 freaking hours.

i definitely won't pay to watch it.

i can honestly say that i was very disappointed with the new addition. waited so long for this. it was very eyecatching and the stunts were great. but it seriously lacked in storyline and some of the stunts seemed unnecessary and drawn out. i'm hopeful that the second part will have more substance to it. it's great for a visual experience but fell really short of substance when it came to a story and cinematic experience.

i am hoping that the franchise will step up their game and have a proper script and not just use it as a shock factor of stunts.

tom cruise is a brilliant actor and i felt this cheapened his ability.

where do i even start? one of this year's biggest blockbusters, and certainly one of the most anticipated films of the year. overshadowed by it's close release to oppenheimer and barbie, most people expected huge drop in box office sales. nonetheless, i still went to watch this movie with an open mind and a considerable excitement. after all, the latest installment in the series before this movie, fallout, was arguably a fan-favorite. little did i know that i was in for a less-than-pleasant experience. i thought i had to start by talking about the plot and the casting. it is exactly what you think it is if you've read the short summary on imdb. a goose chase for a dangerous weapon that everybody wants to control. as well as the risk being obviously the fate of the world which hangs in the balance. a recycled and overused premise that we've seen a million times before. the whole sequence through the streets of venice felt pretty familiar for some reason. i soon found out, and i kid you not, that this car chase was set in exactly the same place as fast and furious x. and i'm not just talking about both of them being set in venice, both car chases in both movies actually end up in the same place where the cars had to go down the flights of stairs. you've got to be at a new level of desperate if you need to rip an entire scene from the fast and furious series. funnily enough, that doesn't even come close to how bad the casting was. grace's actor, hayley atwell, is without a doubt the most unlikeable character to ever come out of the series. backstabbing ethan all movie only for him to completely forgive her every time with zero repercussions. she is literally the reason ilsa faust died, but on the very next scene, luther plays it off by taking all the blame from grace and comforting her by saying that "ilsa died so she could save you". like, am i missing something here? another honorable mention is vanessa kirby's character, alana, who honestly felt like it could have been played by any unknown actor and it would still have the same effect. paris's character should have taken her place but even she had her flaws. we understand too late in the movie that she is working with gabriel, simply because it genuinely seems like she's just a mercenary throughout most of the film. the only thing that saved her character for me was the fact that we find out that she isn't dead at the end of the movie, so who knows how that turns out. and finally, esai morales's character, gabriel. now, i'm not trying to blame that performance solely on esai, but what in god's name was that? talk about a villain falling short. the way the writers created him may have set him up for failure. but that still gives no excuses for how esai missed the mark completely. even dante in fast and furious x felt like an actual, fully fledged villain. and that's saying something. horrible cast, horrible plot, and sub-par performances all around to say the least. i was eagerly waiting for the ending, not just because i wanted the movie to end as soon as possible, but also because it was the movie's last chance at redemption. one redeeming scene at the end could've saved it for me. but alas, this is the way the movie industry works now. as expected, the ending left me feeling like i had just wasted almost 3 hours of my life watching an unfinished mess. marvel was the first to do it with avengers: infinity war and avengers: endgame. but at least marvel's writers did it the right way. infinity war felt like a fully fledged and coherent movie on it's own. it captured your interest and immediately hooked you as well as leaving you begging to know what happens next. then came spider-man: across the spider-verse which couldn't quite accomplish the same feat. and now with this movie which also failed to do a two-part movie the right way. moral of the story is, if you're going to split your movie into two separate movies, you should at least put some effort into making that first part seem like an actual completed movie. and not just what seemed like an unfinished project.

with all that being said, i can still confidently say that the cinematography and tom cruise with the help of his team are the only things that make this movie worth watching. the action scenes, however lacking in effect, are pretty enjoyable and should be enough reason for you to check out the movie for yourself. only for tom cruise though.

i don't quite understand the ratings, but this movie suffers from poor direction. the loud sound and fast pace keep it going, but most scenes lack emotional connection with the characters. the performances by simon pegg and esai morales (gabriel), the new antagonist, are somewhat commendable. however, tom cruise and the female cast members fail to leave a significant impact. take, for example, guardians of the galaxy, where the female characters possess strong personalities and deliver compelling performances.

the main issue lies in the mediocre action sequences. a good action sequence should strike a balance between realism and impossibility, something the previous mission: impossible films accomplished. unfortunately, this installment falls short. the action scenes lack danger and appear fake and nonsensical. the train scene, in particular, suffers from jarring jump cuts. it's disappointing to see the characters engage in impossible feats but not witness the creative ways they save themselves.

furthermore, the overall plot and dialogues are confusing. while i appreciate complex movies, this one leaves me perplexed. the writers take too many liberties with who is chasing whom and which side characters are on. the threat of ai as a dramatic element no longer captivates; it's just a code running on electricity. the concept of outsmarting ai and doing the unexpected feels tedious.

in summary, i can give it a maximum rating of 6, but it deserves a 5 due to the weak direction. even if everything were executed flawlessly, the movie would still fall short of being mind-blowing, perhaps reaching an 8.5 at best.

don't know why but the mission was too easy in the movie. the ai entity is so intelligent to control the whole cyberspace, calculate all possibilities but couldn't figure out that killing ethan might be the easiest solution instead of doing time pass with other ladies. also they just conveniently gave location to their next meeting to everyone as if it's public info. it just seemed very linear and dragged a little.

my biggest issue is the lack of chemistry between characters and just genuine conversations between them. the background score was constantly playing irrespective of what is the situation. felt like tom was in some trance and was just there to do action scenes. in the whole movie i didn't see a single good emotional scene from him. if he wants to do just stunts then he might as well start a youtube channel. the stunts although good were maybe unnecessary. they could have got an easier way get ethan on train for example then to jump from a cliff.

hopefully in next movie they do concentrate on the story and plot line and not just action scenes. this might be the worst mi in the series.

i am deeply disappointed with the excessively long wait for the seventh installment of the mission impossible franchise. the initial allure that emerged from the breathtaking first trailer has completely faded after watching this film. unfortunately, all that remains is a profound and bitter sense of disappointment. the convoluted dialogues veiled in violence, coupled with action scenes overly focused on visual spectacle, fail to deliver the desired impact.

benji and luther indeed push their boundaries this time, while the hastily developed relationship between grace and ethan, considering their backgrounds as cunning thieves, is implausible. it is regrettable to see the minimal meaningful dialogues given to pom klementieff's character, paris, despite her agile performance. she appears silent and tragic. as for esai morales, let's not forget, he merely replicates the antagonistic character from previous films. his acting is remarkably poor, and he fails to grasp the meaning of the lines he delivers. even in fight scenes, it is evident how awkwardly he struggles. how can ilsa meet such an absurd fate? just moments before, she nearly took the life of the formidable salomon lane in previous films, yet now she falls at the hands of someone far more feeble. and how can this team display such high spirits after ilsa's departure? it all feels like watching a comedy disguised as mission impossible-an entry filled with recklessness, devoid of existential concerns, lacking meaningful conflicts or substance, with only tom cruise's aging and forced daring actions.

nevertheless, i appreciate the chemistry that develops among the cast members, their genuine camaraderie. however, i am perplexed by the sudden emergence of consciousness in the ai. as witnessed, the film's genre abruptly shifts into science fiction, while the nonsensical use of halloween masks only adds to the confusion. honestly, i hold greater regard for the prosthetic makeup used in the fourth film. yet, as the film progresses, the insanity and implausibility become increasingly apparent. i am certain that in the eighth film, they will repeat the same mistakes, perhaps even leaping from helicopters in the arctic.

of course, i understand that crafting a complex story is no easy task, but the narrative in this film feels severely unbalanced and weak, like a monkey losing its way in its stride. it is difficult to comprehend how eugene kittridge could become the cia director after previously serving as the head of imf in the previous films. and the scene with the exploding submarine is entirely nonsensical. how could their bodies remain intact after being exposed to a nuclear blast? this is an incredulity that is hard to believe.

the film attempts to defy progress by employing halloween masks, but in my opinion, it is nothing more than a foolish and forced science fiction fantasy. although i acknowledge that the film tries to connect with the present era, the excessive delivery in blaming technology as the ruler of humanity is nothing but an irrational science fiction delusion.

mission impossible 5 was seriously the best in the recent one following it,there was so much plot twists, mystery and nobody knew who had what.

the ai plot was weak,the scenes where he just walks on and conducts a deal with the woman having the key was unrealistic,the car being hit by the train was expected,i don't know why he had to run on the roof,we get it man,you want everyone to know she doesn't limit you,cruise but this is a movie.

some parts of the movie,it got from pathan like the helicopter scene.

this one just fell flat,there wasn't good action, good story telling,just a bunch of adults running after some keys.

i missed the old ones,they hit different.

had a bit of a hard time with this one. on the one hand some action scenes were really good, the desert scene in the beginning and the never ending train scene in the end were engaging. but as a whole this installment felt like a step backwards from the previous ones. weaker in some way.

we get to witness that tom cruise at 60 still can run and do impressive stunts. but at the hefty runtime this movie has you would expect more from the story. the idea of an ai adversary is intriguing, but it became a hollow bad guy. despite the movies length it somehow still felt rushed. like that they tried to do too much and too little at the same time.

the choreography in the venice fight scene felt really off, didn't look good at all.

hayley atwell was kind of a miss for me, didn't really fit in and her chemistry with cruise wasn't there. feels like they forced her in so they could take someone else out.

good to see henry czerny back as kittridge, he's a solid actor although he didn't get too much screen time here.

remains to be seen how they tie this thing together in the second part, but it feels like they could have been content with this if the pattern is the same.

first off i have to say that i love tom cruise and his films. i've defended the guy even when it wasn't fashionable and the last samurai is in my top 3 favourite films. maverick was epic and i respect his commitment to his craft but having seen mi: dead reckoning i do have to say that it was just okay.

i totally appreciate that the film wasn't woke and there wasn't any messaging being thrust down our throat though maybe pom fighting evenly with tom is a bit of a stretch. and so for that reason i do understand that it is important that the film does well at the box office to show hollywood the way forward.

but with that in mind, let's not get too carried away because it still suffers from some real problems. the sense of peril for any of the characters has all but vanished because we've seen what the characters are capable of and we remember the other films.

i mean did the bomb in the airport really have any tension behind it at all? we know the franchise. we know they won't detonate a bomb in an airport in the first act. so it seems false and treating the audience as if they have never seen an mi film before.

and having an audience that knows the characters leads to other problems. having seen tom and ilsa kick the literal crap out of room loads of guys before, having her run away when presented with the unnecessarily dramatic scene in venice seems really forced.

let's be honest, no one really presents a credible physical threat to those two (because of what they've shown us in the other films) and hence to have them split up and run away just feels really pointless or rather clearly foreshadowing a lazily constructed and unsurprising moment of apparent drama. why would you do that? why would ethan shout run when they could fight their way out of the situation with ease?

and likewise the makers really do need to pay attention to the marketing that they do for these films. when they splash memorable images of tom and hayley in the train everywhere pre launch, it kills any tension in the second act of who might die. it's patently obvious who will die because you've previously shown me who is on the train at the end.

similar to this is the never ending fixation with the need for amazing stunts. the bike jump is impressive but is it really that more impressive than the bond ski jump at the beginning of tswlm which was nearly 50 years ago? and in turn it can't just have been me that felt like they thought of the stunt first and then crammed in a kinda pointless scene to facilitate it? an obvious stunt for stunt's sake is not conducive to building tension. i might as well watch the x games for that.

yes the film was fun but like john wick, when there is too much action and the main character has despatched bad guys with ease for the last 90 minutes, seeing them do it for another 30 minutes is just wallpaper.

while the film was okay, the acting was good, the music was great and some of the action was kinda cool, it did feel generic, a little lazy and a little 'going through the motions'.

what i really fear, and i saw this with the glowing praise of wick 4 and extraction 2, is that we become like the left and just because a film is 'on our side' (i.e. isn't woke) that we give it a free pass when it is, well a little bit boring.

ps can we also acknowledge with sadness that the thing that made hayley atwell so hot (you all know what it is) has been lost with the push/pressure to make her lose weight.

eric's grade: c 'dead reckoning' is the seventh installment in the tom cruise led 'mission: impossible' franchise. once again this sees cruise teaming with director and co-writer chistopher mcquarrie who has been solely in the tom cruise business since 2014. since 2012 nine of the twelve movies mcquarrie has worked on have been tom cruise films, and mcquarrie has really found a career defining niche with the most recent set of 'mission: impossible' films directing 'rogue nation', 'fallout' and now both installments of 'dead reckoning'. in addition to cruise this latest entry features many returning actors from the franchise including ving rhames, rebecca ferguson, vanessa kirby and simon pegg with new additions such as esai morales, pom klementieff and hayley atwell. while 'dead reckoning' has cleared over $500 million at the box office that figure becomes a tad less impressive when compared to its $291 million dollar budget which ranks it as one of the most expensive films ever made.

the plot here is chaotic and features a new high tech terrorist that ethan hunt, played by cruise, and his imf team must hunt. this new supervillain is none other than a computer program. nearing the realm of science fiction and comic book plot lines an advanced war program on a russian submarine gains sentience. now it threatens the safety of the entire planet as it can control anything digital, and its predictive modeling makes it a doomsday prophet for a new age. this prophet comes complete with human disciples in the form of morales' gabriel and klementieff's paris among others as apparently it still helps to have some humans to usher in skynet and judgement day. once again ethan and friends must go "rogue", which they even sort of wink at in this film as it does happen in pretty much every 'mission: impossible' film, in order to put an end to this next generation enemy as it becomes apparent that all the governments of the world want to possess the entity to control and use it whereas ethan's small force determines it should be destroyed and are striving to that end. to start the adventure they must hunt down a key split into two parts. off to the arabian desert they go to track down key half one which is inexplicably being held by ilsa faust who is now the primary love interest of hunt as well as a disgraced former british spy played by rebecca ferguson. they track the other half to abu dhabi and then rome where somehow a thief played by hayley atwell enters the mix as she gets the key loses the key gets it again.... it's easy to lose track. she spends a great deal of time running away from ethan hunt before, predictably joining up with his cause. they figure out the entity, as this sentient ai is called, can pretty much do anything, see anything, manipulate anything connected to computers or satellites or the internet so they have to go old school analog to get the drop on this thing. the whole thing culminates in big action set pieces, a runaway train, questionable allegiances with revelations about the location and nature of the entity as the heroes square off against the villains for all the marbles.

so i have greatly enjoyed the 'mission: impossible franchise'. this includes the first three films which, for the most part, aren't as well regarded, but the franchise leveled everything up starting with 'ghost protocol'. since then every installment has tried to feel bigger with more audacious action and higher stakes. while this installment has a lot of tension, and the stakes are higher than ever, i don't feel like the action here is anything better than we have seen before. the burj khalifa sequences in 'ghost protocol' are eye popping. the helicopter chase from 'fallout' is dazzling spectacle. i feel like they are almost at their creative limit with attempting to come up with action to astound and amaze the audience. the action here is still enjoyable, however, and not the downfall of this film. the writing to me is very all over the place. i am thoroughly confused regarding who wants what with this entity as well as what the entity can and cannot do. we have no data on how it recruited humans to do its dirty work or even what its intentions are. there are many problems when it comes to trying to dissect the enemy and all of the moving pieces surrounding it not to mention its limitations if it, in fact, has any. as presented it is ostensibly an omnipotent presence that can manipulate the present and foretell the future? the entire inclusion of the hayley atwell's thief character is nonsensical. it is like the film makers wanted some new blood and they found a way to shoehorn someone into the story logic be damned. not only does her whole presence not work for me, but once she is in play almost every action she takes makes no sense. she consistently attempts to run away from ethan falling into malevolent hands each and every time she attempts to flee. rebecca ferguson is finally freed up to be a more a part of the story after the events of previous films, instead they just sideline her, and seemingly replace her with atwell? i greatly enjoy the action 'dead reckoning' offers even if it is not breaking new ground, but this is the most convoluted plot and confusing character development that the series has ever had, and we haven't even brushed on the fact that the bad guy the entity has at its beck and call is a nefarious figure from hunt's past. of course he is, and on and on it goes. turn off your brain and enjoy some action as tom cruise runs and runs searching for the latest widget to save the world, but engage your brain at your own risk as 'dead reckoning part one' is a fun, but problematic hot mess.

i wanted to like this movie but unusually as i love mi movies i lost interest. the role of grace (hayley atwell) i found annoying and her acting was bad. i didn't understand why the tom cruise character keep saving her. the start of the movie was excellent, then along came grace. the character development was weak and the only parts i really enjoyed were the interactions with the old team, these were excellent funny, exciting, clever. the two excellent actors rebecca fergusson and vanessa kirby were under utilised and tokenistic such a waste of talent compared to the hayley atwell role, that got screen time but did little to impress. i'm hoping her role won't continue in next movie but if it does i'll wait to view when free to air.

it was going strong, but sooner or later you run out of story. this has all of the most boring, been done a thousand times scenes that now cost double the money. getting rid of ferguson and going with the new thief, not my cup of tea or something that should be in m:i. they've clearly exhausted their ideas. this is like fast and furious. super boring now because it's just rinse and repeat. if they don't get back to what works, i think this will die out like fast and furious. hopefully, it will recover. there is part 2. but let's get some team action back in there. get some cohesive stuff going on. bring back the impossible mission. raise the bar and steaks. tom don't show your awesome stunts a thousand times before the movie. i'll watch the next one. but let's hope for something better. still a huge cruise fan.

i loved top gun maverick. i loved born on the 4th of july. i love minority report. there are some parts of color of money that are brilliant. this new mi installment was a disappointment. it was as if they were making a mockumentary. i thought they wpuld break character and outtake the whole movie. tom cruise's lines are delivered with an overly dramatic, nasally, inhale. the setups are procedural at best. the lumbering scenes with disappointing comedic beats fails at every level. i yawned at least seven times throughout the film. i want to come back to the theaters and see big movies on the big screen. this was barely a reason to leave the home. let's do better next time.

my movie-going rating is always determined by the number of times i look at my watch and i did that repeatedly throughout this. i will concede that some of the action stunts were great but when they weren't happening the movie plodded.

i realize that logic needs to be suspended during action films. but really----cruise rides his motorcycle off a cliff, parachutes down right through the exact spot on the train when one of his femmes fatales is just about to be shot??? and didn't i just see indiana jone have a car chase though the cobblestones streets in europe. do keep in mind when you are in a foreign country, it's always very easy to find the car you are chasing.

finally both henry czerny and ving rhames need to lighten up.

mi: 1, mi: 4, mi: 3, mi: 5, mi: 6, mi: 7, mi: 2

in that order. seriously had high expectations for this film, but i was uncertain of the direction of this series since the 5th movie. when it was announced that mi:7 was a part one. i rolled my eyes, it should of been left as mi:7 and then just continue on to mi:8, that's was pointless and it almost separates the film from the rest of the series; which is weird considering you can usher a whole new cast and still not have to call it a two-part.

since a kid i loved this series watching the first mission impossible and buying it on vhs, even the n64 video game. yes that old. what i love and miss from mi:1 was that serious spy thriller. very little laughter, if any out of hunt. the suspense and dialogue in mi:1 is so good you have to rewatch it several times to understand what the motives were for several characters. and there's a reason the director is a legend it shows in mi:1. and i believe mi:4 is the perfect version; if you were to go the action adventure route. mi:4 i can truly appreciate the flow and adventure of that film. brad bird did a fantastic job. everything about the fourth movie is great, you can feel the suspense till the last second. and the hanging out the tower scene still raises my anxiety. they should have kept that medium for the franchise. i can literally continue this review all about mi:4 because i can see the attempted balance of that style to what christopher mcquarrie was trying to do with his dark knight nolan style of view since mi:5. which i didn't like because it was a copied style, pasted to this franchise. like many other franchises. and it was working for mi:5 & mi:6, but for this film it seemed forced, not enough salt or sugar in the recipe. mi:7 feels watered-down.

let's begin...so much appreciation for the other films now that i've seen mission impossible: dead reckoning. lots i didn't like about the film and things i did. i'm not a big fan of christopher mcquarrie's version of mission impossible but i still favor mi:5 & mi:6 over mi:7 by several stars. sorry chris. this movie like others said feels flat or empty. the beginning was kind of slow and not as clever compared to all the other mi intros. the villain is so terrible, really so another repetitive character-arc plot. he's basically john cena in fast and furious 9, long lost associate of hunt who caused everything to happen. who we've never heard about in first six films. not featured or mentioned in any of the previous films; and he knows ethan's every move. didnt we get something like that with solomon lane. barf. why was the woman in the white face in the movie? ohh...i forgot we need a female antagonist because i have to be a mindless noob and follow trends that others follow without thought. her character seemed so pointless.

things i liked: grace was a fresh-hot face to the series, the music was really good; better than some of the previous. *watching this in imax was cool, soundfx were great. mostly everything i didn't critique i enjoyed*

so are all directors and writers sitting together and saying to each other create the same films. because the plot to this is weak and redundant. really an artificial intelligence machine capable of controlling everything and potentially destroying the world or controlling the world: eagle-eye, fast and furious: 6, a. i., ready player one, free guy, matrix. and the countless a. i. based movies. this made the movie drop several stars itself. the real mi:7 was part of a british intelligence branch that dealt with misinformation in media and sabotage. there alone is good source material. seeing it thru ai is boring and is just a repetitive plot. in mi:4 the kremlin was exploding in the first half of the movie. mi:2 the intro, mi:5 airplane takeoff intro.

the only reason i ranked mi:7 above mi:2 is solely due to that fact that they created a love story sequel, right after the fact they created a blockbuster spy action thriller that catapulted the whole series. did not make sense to create that version of mi:2 at that time. no one wanted to see a love story right after the amazing movie that was mission impossible.

hope mi:8 brings it back! or bring back brian de palma(at 82) or brad bird!

it's not a bad movie, but it's kind of a let down. perhaps the worse m. i. film since m. i. 2.

the dutch camera angles give it a cheap feeling.

the exposition dialogues are long, tedious and boring: submarine exposition, then office exposition with people laying back on their chairs and no tension, then exposition by ethan's briefcase (followed by the most overwhelming message distraction)

in many scenes (in both exposition and action) the camera changes sides and it's hard to follow who is looking where.

the car chase is treated as a joke for far too long, which diminish the seriousness.

the a. i. story (although interesting) doesn't do anything groundbreaking.

ethan is wanted by everyone and walks around without a mask on? come on!

girl and supervillain fight alone and ethan runs to save her, but he is far away. guess who loses.

and the 2 big stunts of the movie (bike and train) are spoiled by the trailer.

also, we spend 2,5h chasing a mcguffin, which is boring.

we don't even know what the villain wants or what happened in the past between him and ethan.

this movie has many flaws. boring, predictable, and the pacing was off. especially at the start, before the airport scene.

what i liked?

some of italy's scenes, because i've been there and i recognized the landmarks.

and most of the final scene with the train. even though the villain shouldn't have survived that fall, due to velocity.

a movie of this length demands a good, cohesive plot, strong characters, good dialogue. well there was none of that here. after a poor opening sequence, of a submarine being blown up (a russian submarine, manned by a crew speaking english with funny accents) the rest of the film did not improve much.

in a movie of this type - escapist fun - i like to see at least one beautiful sophisticated woman in lovely clothes. there were four females playing strong women (all the subordinate roles were taken by men) and each was boring and badly dressed. i'm female and if i want boring and badly dressed i can look in a mirror. is it so wrong to expect a little glamour when i go to the movies? rebecca ferguson can look gorgeous, and she's a good actress but she was seriously wasted in this film. she sort of hung around looking depressed before getting killed. and why on earth hayley atwell was cast is a mystery - at least to me. she has zero star quality, and there was no charisma between her and tom. but the worst casting was vanessa kirby as the white widow; there is simply no way this person was believable as a mob boss.

you also need a good villain and that was missing too. the guy playing gabriel just wasn't striking enough.

good action sequences, although nothing that hasn't been done many times before, and the car chase could have been shortened considerably without any loss to the plot.

tom continues to amaze. he's 61 and yet could pass for late forties, even in close up.

in summary, pretty entertaining, but far too long. my vote is five - but those five stars are all for tom.

hey guys, for me it seems like i've seen a whole different movie than you, obviously, m:i dead reckoning part 1 is rated highly. and while i understand that as a standalone action movie it is very well executed and solid, it is imho very disappoint as a part of the mission: impossible franchise. i just want to share my 2 cents on it.

for me, it was a 5/10 at most. and i live and breathe the m:i franchise over everything else, like star wars, lotr, potter, whatever. i also love and admire tom cruise for his incredible work. i am a male in my thirties and have seen every m:i movie on the big screen as it came out, except for the first one in the nineties.

but for me, this new installment in the franchise just falls flat. let me explain why.

first off, it is far too comical. there were always small jokes or light moments during the franchise, but the whole beginning part of this movie felt more like a marvel love and thunder dumbness. the car chasing scene in the first half was incredibly hard to watch, complete opposite from the one in fallout in paris for example. how many times will you recycle the "woman can't drive" joke. the movie theater laughing for 10 minutes straight is not what i expect when going to a mi-film, at all. this already has wrecked me completely to the point i almost started crying to what they had done to this part of my favorite franchise.

not "dark" enough, goes along with my first point. there is no feel of real danger or menace, like in m:i 3 or fallout for example. ethan was always ahead of the situation or everything turned out great after every scene. the scene from fallout with the heist on solomon lane's truck, to catch him right in front of the police eyes? planned and done perfectly.

the only "dark" moment was when gabriel kills ilsa, but again, that happened just for the plots sake, to tear off some emotion from the audience. of course it was ilsa to die, we wouldn't care at all if it would have been grace instead.

this theme gets even worse with the main villain. gabriel was a wet towel, compared to owen davian or solomon lane. esai morales played well, don't get me wrong, just the character itself was very shallow. those guys were a real threat for ethan and the imf as a whole. in contrast to that, ethan plays with gabriel the whole movie and defeats him twice in part 1 already, one by having the opportunity to kill him easily if not for gabriel's plot armor, the other by stealing the key in the end. where is the tension going into part 2 if the main villain is no threat and just a joke to be played with?

the whole ai thing is also very hard to grasp. i get it why they've chosen it, to give the story a 70s vibe with the analog technique to be used, as a nod to the original m:i series. but ai going rogue and people trying to abuse it for power feels so sucked dry and seen millions of times already.

there is no real mission: impossible moment. that one is the biggest one for me i suppose. like no moment in the movie lets you sit on the edge of your seat watching ethan do a crazy stunt or activity for minutes. no tension. every movie had that kind of moment:m:i server room scenemi:2 entry into biocyte tower, exchange of chimera and bellerophonmi:3 ethan interrogation with davian and death after electrocution, resurrectionmi:4 burj kalifa climbmi:5 underwater server roommi:6 halo jump, solomon rescuemi:7 tried this with the bike jump, but it was already dead on arrival, seen it so often on instagram, trailer, general movie pr. also, it was over like in seconds and while i can imagine how hard this stunt was to pull of, just watching it felt "meh, whatever."

you didn't even see him flying towards the train and aiming at it, that would have provided some tension at least. also, the cgi of the rocks, which meant to hide the ramp was done incredibly poorly.

also, the opening of the movie with the submarine stuff felt more like a james bond, instead of m:i. in every film of the franchise the opening would include ethan and his team doing things to kick off the plot. the screen time of luther and benji felt too short, i especially love luther's character.

easter eggs or recalls, plot repeats:

mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a disappointing addition to the iconic franchise, delivering a lackluster experience that can be succinctly described as both boring and a rehash of the same old stuff we've seen countless times before.

from the opening scenes to the final credits, the film fails to inject any fresh energy into the mission: impossible universe. instead, it relies heavily on tired tropes and predictable plot devices that have become all too familiar in the series. it's as if the filmmakers took a checklist of successful elements from the previous movies and mechanically reproduced them without any attempt at innovation or creativity.

the narrative, which should be the driving force of any action-packed spy thriller, is painfully unoriginal. the plot unfolds in a predictable manner, with clichéd twists and turns that do little to engage or surprise the audience. the attempt to build suspense falls flat, as the storyline lacks depth and fails to provide any meaningful stakes for the characters.

despite a star-studded cast led by tom cruise, the performances feel uninspired, as if the actors themselves are aware they're going through the motions of a tired script. even cruise's charismatic presence can't salvage the film from its own mediocrity. the chemistry between the characters, a crucial aspect of the franchise, feels forced and lacks the genuine camaraderie that made earlier installments enjoyable.

the action sequences, once the hallmark of mission: impossible, are surprisingly decent. while there are moments of intensity, they are overshadowed by the sense of déjà vu that permeates every frame. it's evident that the filmmakers relied on the formula that worked in the past, neglecting the opportunity to push the boundaries and offer audiences something new and exhilarating.

in summing up, mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is a prime example of a franchise resting on its laurels. it fails to deliver the excitement and innovation that fans expect, offering instead a tedious and formulaic experience. if you're seeking a thrilling and fresh take on the mission: impossible series, look elsewhere, because this installment is just the same old stuff.

the film boasted its fair share of action sequences, alongside numerous storylines and characters that remained largely unexplained. furthermore, to my surprise, there was even a classic love triangle thrown into the mix. in theory, these elements should have combined to create an engaging experience, but unfortunately, they fell short of expectations.

in terms of action, the movie delivered its trademark thrilling sequences that have become synonymous with the franchise. tom cruise's dedication to performing his own stunts added an extra layer of authenticity and excitement. however, the plotlines felt disjointed and lacked cohesion, leaving several loose ends and unexplored avenues. the character development also suffered as a result, leaving some individuals feeling underdeveloped and lacking depth.

moreover, the introduction of a love triangle felt forced and out of place, diverting attention away from the core storyline. while such romantic entanglements can add complexity to a narrative, in this case, it seemed unnecessary and detracted from the overall experience.

despite these shortcomings, mission impossible still possesses its trademark charm and the potential to entertain. the film may find a more suitable home when enjoyed through a streaming service, where one can appreciate the action sequences without feeling let down by the plot's shortcomings. with any luck, the next installment in the franchise will learn from these missteps and deliver a more cohesive and captivating adventure.

mission impossible: dead reckoning" finds itself in that well-trodden territory of action flicks that dazzle more with explosive set pieces than with a compelling plot. the film labours under the weight of dialogue that is as wooden as a boardroom table, with scenes that overstay their welcome, akin to a never-ending maths class on what should be a lazy sunday. the storyline is straightforward to the point of suspicion, possibly the brainchild of artificial intelligence, stuffed with enough absurdity and plotholes to pad out its runtime.

yet, tom cruise remains the spark that keeps the film watchable if barely, his synergy with simon pegg and ving rhames injecting some much-needed vigour. however, hayley atwell's character tests one's patience; her repetitive betrayals wear thin, her eventual predictable turnaround as surprising as a rain forecast in london.

in a twist of irony, the most authentic thrill comes from a motorcycle stunt - a jaw-dropping moment of madness that cruise, ever the showman, performs himself. it's this dedication to the craft that pulls the film back from the brink of being a total write-off, reminding us of the unique magic that only cinema can conjure.

the movie is the seventh installment in the mission: impossible franchise and the first of a two-part finale. it features tom cruise as ethan hunt, who is tasked with retrieving an all-powerful, artificially intelligent algorithm dubbed "the entity" before it falls into the wrong hands. the movie is both a timely rumination on the dangers of ai as well as a banger of an action sequel that never slows down

the film is directed by christopher mcquarrie, who crafts a winding head trip that houses some of the most precise, rhythmically assembled, and tension-filled sequences in the series' history. the action sequences are thrilling and intense, and cruise's performance is outstanding

the movie also features the return of the first movie's morally dubious intelligence head, eugene kittridge (henry czerny), which serves less as a wistful cameo and more as a throwback to the series' neo-noir roots - a welcome antidote to a summer overrun with empty nostalgia. the plot is well-crafted and keeps you on the edge of your seat throughout

overall, mission: impossible - dead reckoning part one is an entertaining and enjoyable return for the mission impossible crew. it's a blast that highlights the dangerous world ethan hunt operates in. i would highly recommend it to anyone who loves action movies.

"mission impossible - dead reckoning part one" fails to live up to its high-octane lineage, not just stalling, but derailing entirely. tom cruise reprises his role as ethan hunt, but from his very first scene, it's evident that the indomitable spirit of the agent we once knew is significantly dulled. not only does cruise look visibly aged and wearied, but the conviction in his performance is also notably absent.

spoiler alert -one of the major plot holes is when hunt is mysteriously in moscow without any prior indication or reasonable explanation. it's as though scenes were cut without any thought to continuity. another glaring oversight? the antagonist's motive seems to change three times throughout the film, leaving audiences scratching their heads in bewilderment.

the product placements are so overt, they're almost laughable. there's a chase sequence where hunt, instead of focusing on his pursuer, conspicuously sips a branded coffee before dashing off. and, let's not forget the cringe-inducing moment when a high-stakes confrontation is interrupted by a character's ringtone - a jingle for a popular soft drink.

to add to the debacle, the supporting cast's performances are shockingly subpar. key dialogue scenes felt like rehearsals, with lines delivered so flatly that they robbed the movie of any semblance of tension. the chemistry, or rather the lack of it, between the team was palpable, making their camaraderie feel forced and unnatural.

in conclusion, "dead reckoning part one" is a muddled mess, riddled with plot holes, and overshadowed by its transparent attempts to cash in on product placements. the "mission impossible" franchise has seen highs, but this installment is undoubtedly a profound low. if there's any mission to accept here, it's hoping for a redemptive 'part two'.

while tom cruise is important to this film, the stunts are the real star. the production values and the increasingly outrageous stunts are about as good as can be. the plot is preposterous and unwieldy, but not as dumb as a fast and furious film. for such a thin plot, the film's length seems unnecessary. the main villain is a malevolent computer, which could be an ominous threat, but it also deprives the film of a larger-than-life human adversary for cruise's larger-than-life ethan hunt.

ethan hunt and the imf team must track down a terrifying new weapon that threatens all of humanity if it falls into the wrong hands. with control of the future and the fate of the world at stake, a deadly race around the globe begins. confronted by a mysterious, all-powerful enemy, ethan is forced to consider that nothing can matter more than the mission -- not even the lives of those he cares about most.

mission impossible dead reckoning part 1 continues the tried and tested formula of the franchise, presenting an edgy tech plot falling into the wrong hands, and tom cruise's iconic character attempting to save the day. while the movie delivers some thrilling action sequences, including a commendable jump from a cliff by tom cruise, it doesn't bring much new to the table.

the film follows the well-established mission impossible formula, with car chases, daring stunts, and high-octane action driving the narrative. while these elements remain entertaining, they don't offer any fresh perspective to the story, resulting in a sense of déjà vu for viewers familiar with the series.

tom cruise's dedication to performing his own stunts, particularly the cliff jump, deserves applause and adds an authentic touch to the movie. however, beyond these moments, mission impossible dead reckoning part 1 feels like old wine in a new bottle, with a story that echoes previous installments in the franchise.

while the movie may not bring anything new to the series, it still manages to provide a satisfying and time-passing cinematic experience. fans of the mission impossible franchise will likely enjoy the familiar action-packed adventure, even if it lacks innovation in its storyline, for others it will just be an average watch.
